body:
## Summary

Under frame weighting, sequences with few annotated frames (e.g. EgoPoints sequences with 2–12 evaluated frames) contribute almost nothing to the overall metric, while long sequences dominate. Per-sequence weighting gives each sequence equal influence regardless of annotation density.

## Effect on scores (AllTracker baseline, 50 sequences)

| Tracker | Frame-weighted | Per-sequence |
|---|---|---|
| AllTracker @ 1024px | 66.6% | 65.5% |
| AllTracker @ 768px | 64.0% | 63.8% |
| AllTracker @ 512px | 58.6% | 58.1% |
| AllTracker @ 384px | 54.2% | 54.2% |
| CoTracker3 | 55.8% | 55.2% |
| CoTracker2 | 56.7% | 54.4% |

Ordering is preserved. Changes are small (~0–2pp).

## Change

Two lines in `AveragePointAccuracy.aggregate()`.

body:
Sub-issue #263. Covers everything up through **Cluster 1** of the test plan. **Cluster 2 (render basics) will follow in a separate PR.**

## Summary

- **RTL / jsdom test harness in place.** Added `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/user-event`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, and `jest-environment-jsdom` (pinned to `^29.7.0` to match Jest 29). Jest is now configured with `testEnvironment: 'jsdom'`, `testMatch` extended to `*.test.tsx`, and `setupFilesAfterEnv` wires `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers globally. `pack-output/` added to `modulePathIgnorePatterns` and to the eslint ignore list.
- **Cluster 1 helper tests landed.** New unit tests for `matchNode`, `matchNodeKey`, `isCollection`, `toPathString`, `pathsEqual`, `isDescendantOf`, `splitPropertyString`, `editingStatesEqual`, and `getNextOrPrevious`. The `toPathString` suite locks in the new `/` + `encodeURIComponent` encoding from §2, including the `\0` sentinel for the single-empty-key edge case and the substring-lookalike cases that motivated the §2 rewrite.
- **Refactored `src/helpers.ts` into well-organised `src/utils/` submodules** while reorganising tests — drove out of needing somewhere coherent to land the new tests. Existing `src/utils/helpers.ts` (single-function file) and the trivial `src/utils/index.ts` barrel are gone. Public API names re-exported from [src/index.ts](src/index.ts) are unchanged.

## Structure changes

`src/helpers.ts` → split into:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [src/utils/pathTools.ts](src/utils/pathTools.ts) | `splitPropertyString`, `toPathString`, `pathsEqual`, `isDescendantOf`, `editingStatesEqual`, `Path` |
| [src/utils/filter.ts](src/utils/filter.ts) | `filterNode`, `matchNode`, `matchNodeKey` (+ internal `filterCollection`) |

[test/](test/) now strictly mirrors [src/utils/](src/utils/) — one test file per source file.

11 internal `src/` files updated to import from the new submodules. No name-stable public API changed.

## Out of scope (next PR)

Cluster 2 — render basics: mounting `JsonEditor` / `JsonViewer` against varied data shapes, asserting visible output, `rootName` and collapsed-state props. That work needs the new RTL harness landed first, hence the split.

body:
## Summary

PR #4545 added the Escape focus-restore fix (#4539) to the shared `InfoDisclosure` component inside `SidebarTokenView`, but the regression tests only exercised the **cost-info** trigger. Both the cost-info and TUI-untracked popovers go through the same `InfoDisclosure`, so the fix already benefits both — but a future refactor that splits `InfoDisclosure` into per-trigger components (or introduces a per-trigger override) could silently drop focus-restoration coverage for the TUI-untracked path.

This PR adds a third regression test that exercises the TUI-untracked trigger specifically.

## Changes

- `packages/dashboard/src/components/SidebarTokenView.test.tsx` — new test `restores focus to the TUI-untracked disclosure on Escape (#4539)` placed next to the existing TUI-untracked render test, mirroring the cost-info Escape-restore test pattern.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd packages/dashboard && npx vitest run src/components/SidebarTokenView` — 34 passed (was 33)
- [x] `cd packages/dashboard && npx vitest run` — 2255 passed across 124 files (no regressions)
- [x] Verified the new test fails when the `triggerRef.current?.focus()` line is temporarily removed from the Escape branch of `InfoDisclosure` — both the existing cost-info test and the new TUI-untracked test fail, confirming the new test correctly locks the shared-component wiring in place. Source reverted before commit.

Closes #4546

author: gangster
body:
Follow-up to #89. The mutate policies broke on the **Deployment autogen path** (the tests only exercised bare Pods):

- `mutate-workload-labels` derived `app.kubernetes.io/name` from `request.object.metadata.name`, which Kyverno autogen rewrites to the (nonexistent) pod-template name → substitution error. Dropped it; `app.kubernetes.io/name` is no longer required (`require-workload-labels` requires only `team`, which is auto-injected from the namespace).
- The standalone `automount` scalar patch produced a malformed autogen patch (`Object 'Kind' is missing`). Folded automount into the securityContext patch (`mutate-pod-defaults`) so strategic-merge resolves the type under autogen.

**Verified live on preprod** (bare Deployment, server dry-run): `automountServiceAccountToken: false` + hardened `securityContext` + `team` label all injected via autogen, **zero warnings**. Smoke-check now runs against a Deployment. app-alpha stays Synced (no thrash).

author: fashraf94
body:
Read-only discovery confirming/refuting the execution-model assumptions the Forge Enforcement Keystone Spec (V1) rests on. Every answer is backed by a pasted file:line snippet.

Headline findings that affect the lock:
- Q2: max swaps/tick is NOT 1 (N risk rotations + 1 Haiku swap, no cap); trades[] is written per-swap inside each txn + re-read after each risk swap, so a trades[]-derived breaker can bind within a tick if placed in the execution loop.
- Q5: V1.2 ("Swap Evaluation Pipeline Refresh") is NOT merged; margin is inline (agentTriggerGate.js:104, hardcoded 0.5 :106), no shared helper exists -> Scenario C.
- Q3: archetype identity lives at battle.agentContext.archetype, NOT battle.archetype as the spec's 4.1 hook assumes; strategyPreset is user-mutable post-creation.
- Q4: day_trader/Hermes are not agent archetypes; degen is the HFT exemplar; riskOverrides + defaultPreset are dead fields.
- Q6: validateTradeDecision gates Haiku swaps; risk-manager forced swaps bypass it structurally (guardrail overrides do not).

No production code modified; only this findings file is added.

body:
PR #142 switched ``_get_saved_features_dir()`` to return a ``str`` (via
``feature_store_dir`` → ``os.path.join``), but ``get_partition_dir`` operates
on Path semantics (``.parent / f\"{.name}_p{K}of{N}\"``). A partitioned run
(``--partition K N``) now bombs with:

```
File ".../notebooks/features/calculate_features.py", line 84, in get_partition_dir
    return main_feature_dir.parent / f"{main_feature_dir.name}_p{k}of{n}"
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'parent'
```

Wrap the ``str`` with ``Path()`` at the single call site (line 187) so the
partition-dir derivation works again. One-line change. Verified locally
(parse OK) and on the cluster (the v4 preflight after this patch progressed
past the failure point).

author: xpoes123
body:
## What

Two requests:
1. **`/stock graph`** — a matplotlib equity curve of portfolio value over time (needs persisted data → new `portfolio_snapshots` table).
2. **Granular profile + buttons** — `/stock profile` now has **Overview / Today / Graph** buttons. *Today* shows each stock's move today (biggest movers first), with day P/L and top gainer/loser.

## How

- **`portfolio_snapshots`** table (account/stock/options/cash value + `kind`), with migration.
- **Hourly snapshot loop** records each portfolio user's account value going forward.
- **Backfill** — first `/stock graph` view lazily reconstructs a daily *stock-value* curve from the trade log using yfinance historical closes. Cash/options aren't reconstructable historically, so pre-today points are stock-value-only (noted in the embed footer); live points include everything. (Per the agreed "backfill + snapshot forward" / hourly cadence.)
- Refactored portfolio math into `_compute_portfolio()` so Overview/Today/Graph share one priced snapshot.
- `PortfolioView` buttons are restricted to the command invoker; they time out after 3 min.

## Tests
New `tests/test_portfolio_snapshots.py`: snapshot queries, the backfill share-walk (cumulative buys − sells, oversell clamp, naive-tz handling), and PNG rendering. Full suite: 91 passed (5 pre-existing baccarat failures on `main` are unrelated). Reconstruction also smoke-tested against a mocked yfinance.

Follow-up (separate PR): period buttons on `/stock leaderboard` (daily/weekly/YTD/all-time), which build on these snapshots.

author: emily2040
body:
# Add `domain-expert-collaboration-loop` data science skill

## Visual Preview

Hero shot:

![Domain Expert Collaboration Loop hero shot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Emily2040/data-science-agent-skills/add-data-science-skill-domain-expert-collaboration-loop/data-science-agent-skills/domain-expert-collaboration-loop/assets/hero-shot.png)

Reddit infographic:

![Domain Expert Collaboration Loop Reddit infographic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Emily2040/data-science-agent-skills/add-data-science-skill-domain-expert-collaboration-loop/data-science-agent-skills/domain-expert-collaboration-loop/assets/reddit-infographic.png)

## Problem It Solves

Structure collaboration between data scientists, AI agents, and domain experts when domain judgment is required.

Pain addressed: Agents and analysts can produce plausible work that misses domain constraints, tacit knowledge, and operational reality.

Why this is not covered by generic tools alone: A disciplined SME loop captures assumptions, challenge questions, evidence, review decisions, and signoff. This PR packages the judgment workflow, output contract, checks, provider guidance, tests, and visual communication assets as one independent skill.

## Research-Informed Design

- Cookiecutter-style predictable structure and reproducibility.
- Kedro-style modular workflow discipline.
- MLflow-style lifecycle, provenance, and integration awareness.
- Anthropic/OpenAI-style portable `SKILL.md` folder contract.
- Reproducible-research expectations for documentation, dependency discipline, testing, and collaboration.

## What The Skill Should Do

- Transform a vague request into an explicit Domain Expert Collaboration Loop decision with named owner, evidence, assumptions, and action threshold.
- Inspect local artifacts first: data extracts, schemas, notebooks, SQL, pipeline configs, model reports, tickets, and prior decisions.
- Separate mechanical checks from expert judgment so another reviewer can reproduce what was checked and what was inferred.
- Classify findings as stop, fix-first, monitor, accepted risk, or owner decision instead of producing generic advice.
- Preserve raw evidence and never silently mutate data, notebooks, model artifacts, or production configs.
- Return a decision artifact that can be handed to a data scientist, ML engineer, governance reviewer, or stakeholder without hidden context.

## Workflow

- List assumptions that require domain validation.
- Prepare SME questions tied to decisions, not generic review.
- Capture evidence, objections, corrections, and unresolved uncertainty.
- Update analysis plan or model design based on review.
- Return an assumption ledger and signoff record.

## Outputs

- SME interview guide
- assumption ledger
- challenge-question list
- evidence log
- signoff and open-risk record

## Cross-Agent Compatibility

Validated package contract covers Codex, ChatGPT Agents, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Gravity, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, and local LLM agents through `SKILL.md`, `MANIFEST.json`, provider-neutral references, and stdlib contract tests.

## Independent Package Contents

- `SKILL.md` with trigger metadata, execution rules, red flags, resources, and output contract.
- `README.md` as the standalone GitHub page with both visuals at the top.
- `MANIFEST.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`.
- `references/` playbook, acceptance tests, provider interop, agent portability, quality rubric, benchmark plan, research grounding.
- `tests/test_skill_contract.py` plus clean, messy, and adversarial fixtures.
- `scripts/quick_validate_skill.py` with `--strict` mode.
- `assets/hero-shot.png` and `assets/reddit-infographic.png`.

## Validation

- `python scripts/quick_validate_skill.py . --strict`
- `python tests/test_skill_contract.py .`
- `python -m py_compile` across scripts and tests
- Branch independence check: this branch changes only `data-science-agent-skills/domain-expert-collaboration-loop/`
- Visual check: hero is 1600x900 and infographic is 1080x1350

author: pbuchabqui
body:
## Summary

- **Bug 1 (sensors.cpp):** `sensors_tick_100ms()` copied `g_data_staging→g_data_committed` field-by-field without disabling interrupts. The ISR (`sensors_on_tooth` → `sample_fast_channels`) writes to `g_data_staging` concurrently, producing torn snapshots. Fixed with CPSID/CPSIE around the copy block.

- **Bug 2 (knock.cpp):** `knock_cycle_complete()` read `g.knock_count[c]` then zeroed it at the end of the function without a critical section. `knock_cmp0_isr()` could increment the counter between the read and the zero, silently losing knock events. Fixed by atomically reading and zeroing under CPSID.

- **Bug 3 (flash.cpp):** Production `nvm_load_runtime_seed()` called `runtime_seed_boot_compatible_60_2()` which checks magic/version/flags but never validates `seed.crc32`. The host-test mock already validated CRC; production silently accepted corrupted flash seeds. Fixed by moving the CRC-32 helpers out of the `#ifdef EMS_HOST_TEST` block and adding CRC validation to the production path.

- **Bug 4 (ui_protocol.cpp):** `g_tx_buf`, `g_tx_head`, and `g_tx_tail` were not `volatile`, and `tx_push()` had no critical section — unlike the RX path which had both. If `ui_tx_pop()` is called from the UART TX ISR, the compiler can cache stale head/tail values. Fixed by adding `volatile` and CPSID to `tx_push()`.

- **Bug 5 (system.cpp):** Four `while(condition){}` infinite loops ran before IWDG was initialized (HSE ready, Flash ACR, PLL1 lock, SYSCLK switch). A clock hardware failure would hang silently forever. Fixed with bounded iteration counters that trigger SYSRESETREQ on expiry.

- **Bug 6 (etb_control.cpp/h):** `calculate_pid()` had `static float filtered_deriv` — a static local shared across all calls, never reset when the ETB re-initializes. Integral anti-windup was clamp-only (always accumulates). Fixed by moving `filtered_deriv` into `etb_control_data_t` (zeroed in `memset` on init) and implementing conditional anti-windup (skips integration when output is saturated in the same direction as the error).

- **P3-A (startup_stm32h562.cpp):** `Default_Handler` was an infinite loop. An unhandled IRQ now triggers SYSRESETREQ for an immediate clean reset rather than silently hanging.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify sensors.cpp, knock.cpp, flash.cpp, ui_protocol.cpp, system.cpp, etb_control.cpp all compile without new errors under `-DEMS_HOST_TEST`
- [ ] Confirm pre-existing build errors (ign_calc.cpp, ckp.cpp, timer.cpp) are unchanged — these are not introduced by this PR
- [ ] Verify CRC fix: inject a seed with bad CRC in host-test NVM; `nvm_load_runtime_seed()` must now return `false`
- [ ] Verify knock fix: simulate `knock_cmp0_isr()` increment during `knock_cycle_complete()` (unit test); no count should be lost
- [ ] Verify sensor fix: `sensors_get()` must return a consistent snapshot where all fields belong to the same sampling instant
- [ ] Check CPSID coverage: `grep -n "cpsid\|cpsie\|CriticalSection" src/drv/sensors.cpp src/engine/knock.cpp src/app/ui_protocol.cpp`

author: baktun14
body:
## Why

Two issues seen in production with Python GPU **runs**:

1. **A run dies after ~1 min when the requested GPU is busy.** The pipeline polled bids for one GPU model for 60s, then failed with a generic `timeout waiting for bids`.
2. **The run detail page always showed "NVIDIA H100"** regardless of the GPU chosen. The selected GPU *was* deploying correctly — the summary just hardcoded the label and a flat $2.5/hr cost, and the run record never carried the GPU back.

## What changed

### Automatic GPU fallback (no-bid case)
- When the requested GPU gets no bids within `GPU_FALLBACK_BID_TIMEOUT_MS` (~20s), the run automatically closes that deployment (reclaiming its escrow deposit) and retries on the next currently-available **datacenter-class** GPU, in capability order (`JOB_GPU_PREFERENCE`), until a lease lands or candidates are exhausted.
- On exhaustion the run fails with a clear message listing what was tried instead of a bare timeout.
- The requested GPU is always attempted **first** (we honor the user's pick); there is no pre-flight substitution.

### Show the actual GPU (display-bug fix)
- The GPU is tracked on the `deployments` row per attempt (`gpu_vendor`/`gpu_model`/`gpu_attempt`, migration `0010`), surfaced on `RunRecord`, and rendered in the run summary with a class-aware cost estimate.

### UI feedback
- Sub-status shows **"Searching for another GPU · <model>…"** during fallback (rides the existing 2s run-list poll).
- A terminal **failure banner** surfaces the error message (previously plumbed but never displayed); the message also rides the SSE state frame so it shows reliably once the run goes terminal.

## How it's structured
- `pipeline.ts` is now a single-attempt primitive: `createAndAcquireLease` returns a `no-bid` result instead of throwing, plus `finishJobDeploy`. **Services and gpu-less jobs keep their exact prior single-attempt behavior.**
- The fallback loop lives in `runGpuFallback` (`routes/runs.ts`), which owns SDL rebuilds per attempt.
- GPU inventory cache + `getAvailableGpuModels`/`pickNextGpu` extracted to `akash/gpu-inventory.ts`, shared by the `/gpu-models` route and the loop.

## Concurrency / safety
- All fallback writes are guarded against a concurrent cancel. A cancel landing mid-attempt is handled: `runOutcome` (written by cancel) survives the lease primitive's `state` writes, so a post-attempt terminal check closes whatever was just created and re-finalizes — no orphaned leases.
- `MAX_ATTEMPTS × BID_TIMEOUT` (≈2.5 min) stays well under `JOB_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 min), so the reconciler won't fail a still-searching run.

## Out of scope (v1)
- Bad-lease retry: a lease that lands but reports `gpu-unavailable` (CUDA not usable on the provider) still fails as today.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean across shared / server / web
- [x] `vite build` clean
- [x] Migration `0010` applied to dev DB; new columns verified
- [ ] Live: request a busy GPU → status flips Reserving → Searching → Running on an available GPU
- [ ] Live: all candidates busy → ends Failed with the "no GPU available" banner
- [ ] Live: Cancel during "Searching" → ends Canceled, no new deployment created, in-flight deployment closed

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Phase 15 PR 2 of 6 — wires up reliability and crash-recovery infrastructure across the Rust core, the bridge, and the Electron renderer. PR 1 (#68, Performance & Startup) is the immediate predecessor; this PR targets `main` directly because the changes are orthogonal to PR 1's perf work.

**Task 7 — WAL mode + crash-safe DB writes** (`crates/tessera_core/src/db.rs`)
- `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` issued immediately after the SQLCipher key application so every subsequent write is journalled to the WAL file rather than the main DB.
- `bridge.dispose()` runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` so the WAL is folded into the main file before the process exits (no leftover WAL on disk → faster cold-start, easier backups).
- Startup runs `PRAGMA integrity_check`. On failure we attempt a single `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` recovery, retry the check, and if corruption persists surface a structured error to the renderer rather than silently proceeding with a corrupt DB.
- Rust test (`db::tests::wal_mode_survives_mid_write_kill`) simulates a mid-write crash by killing the writer thread and asserts the DB opens cleanly on the next process.

**Task 8 — Artifact auto-save recovery** (`apps/desktop/electron/artifactRecovery.ts`, `apps/desktop/electron/ipc/artifacts.ts`)
- Every editor's auto-save writes a `<artifactId>.tessera-recovery` JSON sidecar BEFORE calling `bridgeUpdateArtifactContent`. If the bridge call fails (DB locked, disk full, IPC rejection), the sidecar stays on disk and is detected on next launch.
- `artifacts:checkRecovery` (called on open) returns the sidecar envelope if it's newer than the DB row's `updated_at`, otherwise `null` — the renderer decides whether to prompt "Restore unsaved changes from <time>?".
- `artifacts:discardRecovery` lets the user dismiss the prompt without restoring.
- Vitest covers: sidecar persists after bridge rejection; sidecar cleared after successful save; malformed sidecar is treated as `null` (not a parse error); foreign-artifact sidecar is rejected by the `artifactId` cross-check.

**Task 9 — Graceful sidecar shutdown / PID registry** (`apps/desktop/electron/sidecarPidRegistry.ts`, `apps/desktop/electron/sidecar.ts`, `apps/desktop/electron/diffusionSidecar.ts`)
- Every sidecar spawn writes `{userData}/tessera-sidecar-pids/<label>.pid` containing the PID + binary name. On startup, `reapOrphanedSidecars()` scans the directory, kills any PID whose process name matches the recorded binary (PID-reuse defence), and removes the file.
- `will-quit` issues `SIGTERM`, waits up to 5s, then escalates to `SIGKILL` for any sidecar that hasn't exited.
- Vitest covers: missing PID dir → no-op; malformed PID file → file removed, no kill; PID belongs to dead process → file removed, no kill; PID belongs to live process with MISMATCHED binary name → file removed, no kill (defence against the OS reusing the PID for an unrelated process); PID belongs to live process with MATCHING name → SIGKILL delivered.

**Task 10 — Export failure recovery + retry queue** (`apps/desktop/electron/failedExportQueue.ts`, `apps/desktop/electron/ipc/artifacts.ts`)
- When an export fails (disk full, permission denied, Typst error), the failure is queued to `{userData}/failed-exports.json` with `{ id, artifactId, format, error, retryCount, lastAttemptAt }`. The queue survives restarts.
- `artifacts:failedExports` lists pending failures for the UI.
- `artifacts:retryExport(id)` re-runs the export and dequeues on success (keeps the entry with an incremented `retryCount` on repeated failure).
- Vitest covers queue persistence, retry logic, partial-failure dequeue, and concurrent-access safety.

**Task 11 — Connector sync error resilience** (`crates/tessera_connectors/src/failure_state.rs`, `apps/desktop/electron/connectorBackoff.ts`, `apps/desktop/electron/ipc/connectors/handlers.ts`)
- New `failure_state` module pins `PersistedSyncError` (JSON discriminator `transient` | `permanent`), `SyncFailureState`, and `SyncBackoffPolicy` (base 2s, cap 5min, multiplier 2.0, ±25% jitter, 8-failure permanent threshold).
- `tessera_sources::store` persists three new columns (`last_sync_error` JSON / `retry_count` u32 / `failed_permanently` bool) per source row. Manager pass-throughs + bridge napi exports let the Electron side load/save/clear failure state per `sourceId`.
- TS-side `connectorBackoff.ts` mirrors the Rust policy and computes the next-retry interval. Its `applyFailureToState()` enforces: `permanent` → flips sticky bit immediately without bumping retry count; `transient` → bumps retry count, flips sticky bit only after 8 consecutive transients. Comprehensive Vitest suite (19 tests) pins every policy decision.
- `runConnectorSync()` records failures across every source matching the failing provider's `sourceType`, and clears them on a successful sync. `isNotConnectedError` → permanent; everything else defaults to transient so a one-off provider 5xx doesn't burn the sticky bit.

**Task 12 — Audit log rotation** (`crates/tessera_audit/src/store.rs`, `crates/tessera_audit/src/logger.rs`, `crates/tessera_bridge/src/napi_exports.rs`, `apps/desktop/electron/ipc/audit.ts`)
- When the audit table exceeds 100K rows, `AuditStore::rotate` archives the oldest half to `audit-archive-<RFC3339>.jsonl.gz` (gzipped JSONL, colons replaced with dashes for cross-platform filename safety) under `{userData}/audit-archives/`. The DELETE runs inside an `IMMEDIATE` transaction that drops + recreates the append-only trigger so the trim itself doesn't trip the trigger.
- Archive write happens OUTSIDE the transaction; only the DELETE is transactional. This guarantees the archive is durable on disk before we remove any rows from the live table.
- `audit:getArchives` IPC lists archive filenames in deterministic order. `audit:rotate` triggers a manual rotation (returns `null` if the threshold isn't reached).
- Rust tests pin: rotation fires at exactly 100K+1 rows; archive parses back to valid JSONL with all original event rows; live table is trimmed to the retained half; archive filename matches the timestamp pattern; no rotation when below threshold.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Risk: **yellow** — the WAL + integrity-check path and the sidecar PID reaper both have non-trivial blast radius on misuse.

- [ ] **Verify WAL crash-recovery path on your dev box.** Run a manual smoke: open Tessera, force-kill it during a bulk-index (`kill -9` on the PID), and confirm it reopens cleanly. The integrity_check guard should never fire in a clean shutdown.
- [ ] **Verify the sidecar PID reaper isn't over-zealous.** After installing this branch, launch Tessera, note which sidecar PIDs land in `{userData}/tessera-sidecar-pids/`, close the app, and confirm those processes are gone. author: austinbhale
body:
## Problem
On Windows the Stop hook fails at session end with:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\Users\<user>\<cwd>\${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\hooks\stop-fitness-check.mjs'
```

The hook used a single-quoted shell `command` string:

```json
"command": "node '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-fitness-check.mjs'"
```

Windows runs the command through PowerShell, where single quotes are literal, so the unexpanded `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is passed to `node` and resolved relative to the user's cwd → module not found.

## Fix
Switch to the `args` exec form. Claude Code substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` per-element as a plain string and spawns `node` directly with no shell, so it works on Windows and POSIX alike.

```json
"command": "node",
"args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-fitness-check.mjs"]
```

## Verification
- `plugin.json` parses as valid JSON.
- `node <resolved path>` runs the hook and emits its normal decision JSON (exit 0).

author: sebamasaguer
body:
The Nginx container was failing to start with the error `host not found in upstream "backend:4100"`. This happens when Nginx tries to resolve the backend hostname at startup before it is available in the Docker network.

To fix this, I updated `nginx.conf` to:
1. Define a resolver (Docker's internal DNS at `127.0.0.11`).
2. Use a variable for the backend upstream URL.
3. Use the variable in the `proxy_pass` directive.

These changes force Nginx to resolve the hostname at runtime instead of startup, allowing it to start successfully even if the backend is not yet ready.

author: intel352
body:
Properly **fixes** (not risk-accepts) the two pgx CVEs from the database module — supersedes ADR 0002.

`go-db-credential-refresh@v1.2.1`'s `driver` package imports `pgx/v4/stdlib` unconditionally for an optional `pgxv4` driver, but this module only uses the `pgx` driver which the lib already maps to **pgx/v5**. So pgx/v4 + pgproto3/v2 were dead-but-linked.

- Forked to `github.com/GoCodeAlone/go-db-credential-refresh` (`v1.3.0` + nested `store/awsrds/v1.3.0`), dropping the v4 driver + import (pgx/v5/mysql/pq retained).
- database module + verbose-debug/instance-aware-db examples now **directly require** the fork (not `replace` — that doesn't propagate to consumers).
- `go mod tidy` drops pgx/v4 + pgproto3/v2 entirely. **Repo-wide grep: zero pgx/v4 / pgproto3/v2** in any go.mod/go.sum. Build + race tests pass.

No `exclude`: every pgx/v4 ≤4.18.3 + pgproto3/v2 ≤2.3.3 version is vulnerable, so exclude only forces a downgrade to another vulnerable version — removing the importer is the fix.

Resolves Dependabot alerts #23–#25 + #54–#56 (previously dismissed under ADR 0002).

author: lnlockly
body:
## Why
A bot whose token has a webhook registered — from a prior platform `/connect-telegram` integration, or an earlier deploy — makes aiogram's `getUpdates` long-polling fail with `TelegramConflictError: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active`. The bot process runs but never receives messages.

Found live during the p-tgbot-support e2e (project 1633): the goose coder-shim filled `bot.py`, wrote `.env`, `pip install`ed, and launched `nohup python bot.py &` correctly — but the reused test bot @agentflow_e2e_verify_bot had a stale webhook (`…/_agents/webhook/agentflow_e2e_verify_bot`), so `bot.out` logged the conflict on a loop until the webhook was cleared. After `deleteWebhook`, polling connected and `/start /help /faq /order` replied normally.

## Fix
Call `await bot.delete_webhook(drop_pending_updates=True)` in `main()` before `dp.start_polling(bot)`. This makes the switch to long-polling deterministic for any token, regardless of prior webhook state. `drop_pending_updates=True` gives a clean start (no stale backlog flood).

Generic, no project-specific logic. `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` passes.

## What

Fix the ~10% flake in `client-consumer`'s `eager_rebalance_reacquires_and_primes` integration test (`m1 did not re-acquire both partitions`, integration.rs:367), which only reproduced under `cargo llvm-cov`.

## Why — it was a real bug, not timing

The `Consumer` struct kept its own copy of `member_id` captured at build time, separate from the live `CoordinatorState::member_id`.

Under CPU contention (how `llvm-cov` triggers it), the departing consumer hit `UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID` during the initial settle and **rejoined from scratch with a new member_id**. The coordinator updated `state.member_id`, but the `Consumer`'s copy stayed stale. So `Consumer::close()` sent `LeaveGroup` for the **dead** id — a silent broker no-op — and the **live** member lingered as a zombie until its `session_timeout`.

Because `session_timeout` (30s) equals the test's regain deadline (30s), the survivor's re-acquire raced the zombie's eviction. Five identical failure traces confirmed it:

```
rejoin OK gen=2 assigned=2  mid=crabka-A   # survivor briefly owns both
HB->RejoinFromScratch       mid=crabka-B   # leaver re-ids under load
rejoin OK gen=3 assigned=1  mid=crabka-C   # leaver's NEW id; re-split → survivor back to 1
CLOSE LeaveGroup member_id=crabka-B Ok(0)  # close() leaves the STALE id → no-op!
```

In production this same bug means any consumer that ever rejoined-from-scratch fails to leave its group cleanly on close, stalling the rest of the group's rebalance for a full `session_timeout`.

## The fix

Move the best-effort `LeaveGroup` into the coordinator task — the entity that owns the live `member_id`. It now sends it as the last thing in `coordinator::run()` on shutdown, using `state.member_id` (bounded 5s timeout, skips an empty id). `Consumer::close()` just cancels + joins the coordinator. A from-scratch rejoin can no longer orphan the member.

## Verification

- **0 failures over 110+ runs** under heavy CPU load (was ~10–20% reproducible the same way: loop the `llvm-cov` test binary with `yes >/dev/null &` ×N background load). Isolated runs always passed — the flake genuinely needs contention.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` + `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Full `crabka-client-consumer` suite green (integration + cooperative_rebalance + unit).

## Reviewer notes

- The `Consumer::member_id()` getter still returns the build-time id (latent staleness after a from-scratch rejoin) — out of scope here, no longer on the close path.
- Under deliberately absurd 20× core oversubscription I saw one unrelated failure in the *initial split* phase (integration.rs:347) — a pre-existing setup-timing fragility that did **not** occur under realistic CI-like load (60/60). Left as-is rather than loosen the test's intentionally tight `rebalance_timeout`.

author: bdchatham
body:
## Summary

The per-pod P2P endpoint Service (PR #365) previously hardcoded `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type=ip`. That's the right call on VPC-CNI clusters (prod, dev) where pod IPs are VPC-routable — but it's a hard blocker on harbor, where Cilium cluster-pool puts pods in `100.64.0.0/14` (CGNAT, unreachable from any NLB in a VPC subnet).

This PR adds a controller-level env var (`SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE`) so each overlay picks the right mode without baking cluster-specific logic into the controller.

## Behaviour

- `SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE=ip` (default) — pod IPs registered directly with the target group; `AllocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false` so the limited 30000-32767 NodePort range is preserved.
- `SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE=instance` — NLB targets the EC2 node at its NodePort; `kube-proxy` / Cilium socket-LB does the NodePort→pod rewrite locally. `AllocateLoadBalancerNodePorts` left nil so kube allocates one.
- Anything else → controller logs `Invalid SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE` and exits 1 at startup.

Per-cluster value lives in each overlay's `manager-patch.yaml`, mirroring how `SEI_P2P_ENDPOINT_DOMAIN`, `SEI_GATEWAY_DOMAIN`, etc. are wired today.

## Validation + default placement

- Validation and default-resolution both happen at controller construction in `cmd/main.go`. The reconciler's `NLBTargetType` field is canonical — by the time any reconcile runs, the field is always either `ip` or `instance`.
- No per-reconcile branching, no "if empty" fallback in the hot path.

## Files

- `cmd/main.go` — env read + validation + default fill-in.
- `internal/controller/nodedeployment/controller.go` — new `NLBTargetType` field on `SeiNodeDeploymentReconciler`.
- `internal/controller/nodedeployment/p2p_endpoint.go` — exported constants `NLBTargetTypeIP`, `NLBTargetTypeInstance`, `DefaultNLBTargetType`. `generateP2PEndpointService` takes target-type as a parameter; `AllocateLoadBalancerNodePorts` gated on it.
- `internal/controller/nodedeployment/p2p_endpoint_test.go` — existing `ip` test asserts NodePort allocation disabled; new `TestGeneratePublishableService_InstanceTargetType` asserts the `instance` shape (annotation + nil-NodePort-allocation).

## Downstream

- **harbor overlay (platform repo)** — separate PR to add `SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE: instance` to `clusters/harbor/sei-k8s-controller/manager-patch.yaml`. After that lands and Flux applies, harbor's publishable-P2P Services will emit `target-type: instance` and the per-pod NLB → node:NodePort → Cilium-socket-LB → pod path becomes viable.
- **prod, dev** — no change; defaults to `ip` (current behaviour).

## One-way doors

- Env var name `SEI_NLB_TARGET_TYPE`. Once any overlay sets it, renaming is painful. Convention-matched to existing `SEI_*` env vars.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit + lint pass on CI.
- [ ] Manual smoke after harbor's overlay PR: harbor syncer-0-0-p2p Service annotation = `instance`, NodePort allocated.
- [ ] Prod/dev unaffected (no overlay change → default `ip` → existing behaviour).

author: addu390
body:
# Proposed changes

Issue Number: close #341

## Problem Summary:

Doris `ARRAY` columns are currently exposed to Spark as `StringType`, so SQL functions like `size(col)` fail with `DATATYPE_MISMATCH.UNEXPECTED_INPUT_TYPE`.

This PR adds an opt-in config `doris.read.array.native-type` (default `false`) that surfaces them as `ArrayType(StringType)` instead. Covers both `thrift` and `arrow` read modes. Default-off keeps existing users on the legacy JSON-string behavior.

Element-type inference (e.g. `array<int>` → `IntegerType`) is intentionally out of scope and left as a follow-up.

## Checklist(Required)

1. Does it affect the original behavior: No (gated by a default-off config)
2. Has unit tests been added: Yes (`SchemaConvertors`, `RowConvertors`, plus parameterized IT for both read modes)
3. Has document been added or modified: Yes (option description); upstream docs at `apache/doris` will be a follow-up
4. Does it need to update dependencies: No
5. Are there any changes that cannot be rolled back: No

## Further comments

Built on top of the discussion in #341 and the design feedback on the stale #345. Happy to iterate on the option name or scope.

4/4 Vampire {3}{B}{B}. Flying (KeywordAbility marker) + the damage-linked
dies trigger: "Whenever a creature dealt damage by this creature this turn
dies, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature."

Shape loaded from sengir-vampire.json via CardDefinitionLoader; Flying and
the trigger attached in code. Per-instance, per-turn victim set keyed on
InstanceId (mirrors Hope of Ghirapur's damaged-set posture). Subscribes to
BOTH DamageDealtEvent and CombatDamageDealtEvent because EventBus dispatch
keys on the static generic type, so combat damage would otherwise miss the
base-type handler — and the printed condition is "dealt damage" (CR 120),
covering combat and non-combat alike. A CardMovedEvent (Battlefield ->
Graveyard, CR 700.4) on a tracked victim places one +1/+1 counter via
CountersService.Add (CR 122.1 / 614); TurnStartedEvent clears the set
(CR 514.x "this turn").

author: agentplain-fleet[bot]
body:
# Autonomy fixes — wave 1

Five fixes from the audit shipped as PR #121 (`docs/fleet-autonomy-audit-2026-05-28.md`). Single integration branch, sequential phases inside it.

## Why these five together

They compound. Memory readable + feedback rules wired is the customization unlock; vertical routing is the autonomy unlock; QuickBooks closes the embarrassing finance gap; discipline-gate and threshold-gate make the customization surface real instead of write-only. Splitting them would leave half-promises live in customer copy.

The CC-at-trial pivot (§8 #4) and briefings generator (§8 #5) are deferred to wave 2 — too big to bundle without breaking the sequential-PR rule.

## Phase summary

### Phase 1 — Wire QuickBooks MCP into finance skills (§8 #1)

`lib/integrations/quickbooks-mcp/server.ts` was a 374-LOC production server with OAuth + token renewal wired since PR #98. Two finance skills carried `stubbed-json` flags in the registry. This adds the third `InvoiceFetcher` / `CloseFetcher` impl (per the two-implementation rule) that speaks to the workspace-scoped MCP:

- `lib/skills/invoice-chasing-realestate/quickbooks-fetcher.ts` — `QuickBooksInvoiceFetcher`
- `lib/skills/month-end-close-cpa/quickbooks-fetcher.ts` — `QuickBooksCloseFetcher`

Skill code itself is unchanged. Registry flags flip from `stubbed-json` to `built` with honest notes about coverage boundaries.

**Honest concessions baked in:**
- `closingReference` falls back to `{{operator: closing reference}}` — QuickBooks has no native field; no fabrication.
- `month-end-close` received-docs returns empty — QB doesn't track doc-portal receipts (those live in Gmail attachments + TaxDome / Karbon). Skill chases everything outstanding by `dueAt` + scope-templated checklist. TaxDome / Karbon MCPs ship received-doc detection in wave 2.
- Degraded-mode honesty seam: `CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOUND` / `TOKEN_EXPIRED` / `GRANT_REVOKED` / `UNAUTHORIZED` / `FORBIDDEN` codes from the MCP all surface as a calm `NOT_CONFIGURED` skill error with a "QuickBooks not yet connected" message. Nothing fake lands in /approvals.

### Phase 2 — Vertical webhook router (§8 #2)

Before this PR, the same generic 5-skill chain ran on every workspace regardless of vertical; the 11 vertical-specific catalog skills had zero production callers.

`lib/skills/vertical-router.ts` registers vertical-specific skills against `workspace.vertical` and fires them alongside the generic chain. Discipline-disable list gates each registration. Errors are non-fatal — the generic chain stays healthy if a vertical skill hiccups.

**Wave-1 registrations:**
- `lead-triage-realestate` for `REAL_ESTATE` workspaces — wired end-to-end via:
  - `lib/skills/lead-triage-realestate/parsed-message-fetcher.ts` (ParsedMessage → LeadRecord)
  - `lib/skills/lead-triage-realestate/prisma-approval-sink.ts` (LEAD_TRIAGE approval rows)
  - `lib/skills/lead-triage-realestate/run-for-event.ts` (production entry point)

**Honest scope concessions:**
- The other 10 vertical skills (insurance-coi, law-intake, month-end-close, mortgage, ria, recruiting, property-management, title-escrow, home-services, invoice-chasing) take CRM-shaped or LOS-shaped inputs that an inbound email cannot honestly produce. Their email-trigger adapters land in wave 2.
- Until then they stay STAGED, and customer-facing copy must not claim they fire on email events.
- Wave-1 lead-triage routes to `manual` because no agent-roster source is wired yet (FUB / kvCORE land in wave 2). Better than fake-routing to a hardcoded agent.
- No-reply senders filtered before triage (no fake leads).

Schema: adds `LEAD_TRIAGE` to `WorkApprovalKind` enum + migration `20260529000000_add_lead_triage_approval_kind`.

### Phase 3 — Wire customer FEEDBACK rules into the skill chain (§9 #1 + companion)

PR #120 shipped `readFeedbackRules` and the PREFERENCE path on `/talk`; no skill in `lib/skills/*` called the reader. PREFERENCE was write-only on the fleet side.

`lib/skills/feedback-rules.ts`:
- `buildFeedbackRulesBlock({ memory, workspaceId, scopes })` → rendered prompt block. Uses `readFeedbackRules` + `renderFeedbackRulesForPrompt`.
- `DEFAULT_RUNNER_SCOPES = ['inbox-triage', 'email-draft', 'scheduling', 'customer-comms']` — the four scopes the generic chain plausibly honors. `general` is always included implicitly.

`composePromptBundle` extended with `feedbackRulesBlock` slot — injects under a "CUSTOMER PREFERENCES" header into every chain skill's prompt (categorize / coordinate / schedule / draft).

**Honest seam:** empty rule set → empty string → NO header. The audit's "(no preferences set)" placeholder is avoided.

`runSkillChain` accepts optional `memory: IMemoryStore`. Read failure NEVER drops the loop (logged + continued with no rules). `process-webhook-event` constructs a `PrismaMemoryStore` via `SYSTEM_OPERATOR_CONTEXT` and passes it through.

### Phase 4 — Gate `runSkillChain` on disabled disciplines (§9 #3)

Before this PR, the biggest runtime path (`process-webhook-event` → `runSkillChain`) had ungated terminal output. A workspace that toggled off `customer-success` or `operations` on the Discipline panel still got drafts, scheduling proposals, and admin classifications written to /approvals.

`runSkillChain` now accepts `disabledDisciplineIds` and gates four discipline-tagged stages:
- office-admin classify → operations
- scheduling proposal → operations
- customer-facing reply draft → customer-success
- compliance scan → legal

When a discipline is disabled, the stage skips entirely — no LLM call, no approval row. The step record carries an honest `"skipped — <discipline> discipline disabled on workspace"` summary so the audit log shows what the operator turned off.

`process-webhook-event` passes `WorkspacePreference.disabledDisciplines` through. Backwards compatible: omitting the field runs the full chain.

### Phase 5 — Wire `WorkThresholdConfig` reader at approval-queue write (§9 #2)

The work-thresholds settings page persisted severity gates + an `autoApproveWhen` JSON column; zero code read them. Every queued item landed PENDING regardless of the customer's stated bar — making the "Decide what needs your eyes" promise theatrical.

`lib/skills/approval-threshold.ts`:
- `applyApprovalThreshold({ workspaceId, kind, confidence?, severity?, tx })` reads `WorkThresholdConfig` for the workspace+kind, evaluates against per-kind opt-in rules, returns a typed PENDING | AUTO_APPROVED decision with `decidedAt` + `decisionReason` populated.
- `COMPLIANCE_FLAG` kind respects the existing `requiresApprovalAboveSeverity` column (rows at-or-above stay PENDING; below auto-approve).
- DRAFT-class kinds respect `autoApproveWhen.minConfidence` — confidence meets the bar → AUTO_APPROVED; else PENDING.

**SAFE DEFAULT:** no row, no opt-in, malformed JSON, or read error all resolve to PENDING. The customer must explicitly opt in.

**Outbound contract preserved:** AUTO_APPROVED still does NOT send (per `project_no_outbound_architecture` — the customer's downstream system executes; agentplain is draft-only). AUTO_APPROVED means "the workspace has pre-blessed this draft for its downstream pickup."

`persist-artifacts.ts` calls `applyApprovalThreshold` at both write sites (chain's terminal approval row + the compliance flag row). Settings UI extended with a per-kind numeric input — default blank = no opt-in.

## Discipline scorecard — what flips, what's still rooting

| Discipline | Pre-wave-1 | Post-wave-1 | What's still needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Analytics | NOT delivering | NOT delivering | No skill produces analytics output yet (Wave 1 didn't touch this) |
| Research | NOT delivering | NOT delivering | No skill wraps `enterprise-search:search` yet |
| Legal | One real surface (compliance scanner) | One real surface — now gateable | Sentinel scans every draft; law-intake-conflict-screen still STAGED |
| Marketing | NOT delivering | NOT delivering | No `marketing:draft-content` wrapper yet |
| Sales-enablement | foll

UX: ↑ from an empty input highlights a pill; ↑/↓ navigate, Enter edits, Delete/Backspace removes, Esc exits. author: rstuhlmuller
body:
## Summary

This change updates the repo-owned Tailscale Kubernetes Operator Connector so
`homelab-exit-node` advertises the full `10.1.0.0/24` homelab LAN instead of
only the Kubernetes API host route. The exit node remains tagged as `tag:k8s`
and still advertises itself as a Tailscale exit node.

## Issue

Tailnet clients using the homelab exit-node path could reach the narrowly
advertised Kubernetes API route, but the desired operator contract did not make
the rest of the local `10.1.0.0/24` network reachable through the same
Tailscale-managed device. That left local network access dependent on manual
client-side or tailnet-side behavior rather than the repository-owned desired
state.

## Cause And Effect

The Connector was configured with `10.1.0.199/32`, which is useful for CI and
cluster API access but does not advertise the rest of the homelab LAN. Users
selecting `homelab-exit-node` as their exit node would not get an explicit
subnet route for services on nearby homelab addresses such as NAS and node
addresses in the same `/24`.

## Root Cause

The original exit-node rollout modeled the minimum route needed for GitHub
Actions to reach the Kubernetes API. The route never grew with the operational
requirement that the exit node also provide local network access across the
entire homelab LAN.

## Fix

- Changed `clusters/homelab/apps/tailscale/exit-node-connector.yaml` to
  advertise `10.1.0.0/24`.
- Updated the Tailscale README and tailnet ingress runbook to document route
  approval for `10.1.0.0/24`.
- Updated the CI/CD docs and knowledge base to keep GitHub Actions access
  constrained to `10.1.0.199:6443` even though the Connector now advertises the
  wider subnet route.

After Argo CD syncs the Tailscale application, the tailnet policy still needs
to auto-approve the `10.1.0.0/24` route for `tag:k8s`, or an admin needs to
approve the route manually in the Tailscale Machines page.

## Validation

- `git diff --cached --check`
- Ruby YAML parse check confirming `exitNode=true` and
  `advertiseRoutes=["10.1.0.0/24"]`
- `yamllint` on the Tailscale YAML files; it returned only existing
  document-start warnings for files that already omit `---`
- `checkov --quiet --compact --skip-download -f clusters/homelab/apps/tailscale/exit-node-connector.yaml`
- Commit hooks: trailing whitespace, end-of-file fix, large-file check, YAML
  check, codespell, Checkov diff, Checkov secrets, and zizmor where applicable

Full `kubectl kustomize` and Nix-backed static checks were not run locally
because this shell does not have `kubectl` or `nix` on PATH.

body:
# Add `drift-monitor-designer` data science skill

## Visual Preview

Hero shot:

![Drift Monitor Designer hero shot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Emily2040/data-science-agent-skills/add-data-science-skill-drift-monitor-designer/data-science-agent-skills/drift-monitor-designer/assets/hero-shot.png)

Reddit infographic:

![Drift Monitor Designer Reddit infographic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Emily2040/data-science-agent-skills/add-data-science-skill-drift-monitor-designer/data-science-agent-skills/drift-monitor-designer/assets/reddit-infographic.png)

## Problem It Solves

Design drift monitoring for production models and data products across data, concept, performance, and operational signals.

Pain addressed: Models degrade silently because teams monitor uptime but not input, label, behavior, or outcome change.

Why this is not covered by generic tools alone: Monitoring must match label delay, business risk, retraining options, and alert ownership. This PR packages the judgment workflow, output contract, checks, provider guidance, tests, and visual communication assets as one independent skill.

## Research-Informed Design

- Cookiecutter-style predictable structure and reproducibility.
- Kedro-style modular workflow discipline.
- MLflow-style lifecycle, provenance, and integration awareness.
- Anthropic/OpenAI-style portable `SKILL.md` folder contract.
- Reproducible-research expectations for documentation, dependency discipline, testing, and collaboration.

## What The Skill Should Do

- Transform a vague request into an explicit Drift Monitor Designer decision with named owner, evidence, assumptions, and action threshold.
- Inspect local artifacts first: data extracts, schemas, notebooks, SQL, pipeline configs, model reports, tickets, and prior decisions.
- Separate mechanical checks from expert judgment so another reviewer can reproduce what was checked and what was inferred.
- Classify findings as stop, fix-first, monitor, accepted risk, or owner decision instead of producing generic advice.
- Preserve raw evidence and never silently mutate data, notebooks, model artifacts, or production configs.
- Return a decision artifact that can be handed to a data scientist, ML engineer, governance reviewer, or stakeholder without hidden context.

## Workflow

- Classify drift risks: schema, distribution, relationship, concept, performance, and operational drift.
- Choose monitors based on data type, label delay, and actionability.
- Set thresholds, baselines, alert routing, and suppression rules.
- Define retrain, rollback, investigation, or no-action playbooks.
- Return a monitor design and incident response path.

## Outputs

- monitor catalog
- baseline definitions
- threshold plan
- alert ownership
- drift response playbook

## Cross-Agent Compatibility

Validated package contract covers Codex, ChatGPT Agents, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Gravity, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, and local LLM agents through `SKILL.md`, `MANIFEST.json`, provider-neutral references, and stdlib contract tests.

## Independent Package Contents

- `SKILL.md` with trigger metadata, execution rules, red flags, resources, and output contract.
- `README.md` as the standalone GitHub page with both visuals at the top.
- `MANIFEST.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`.
- `references/` playbook, acceptance tests, provider interop, agent portability, quality rubric, benchmark plan, research grounding.
- `tests/test_skill_contract.py` plus clean, messy, and adversarial fixtures.
- `scripts/quick_validate_skill.py` with `--strict` mode.
- `assets/hero-shot.png` and `assets/reddit-infographic.png`.

## Validation

- `python scripts/quick_validate_skill.py . --strict`
- `python tests/test_skill_contract.py .`
- `python -m py_compile` across scripts and tests
- Branch independence check: this branch changes only `data-science-agent-skills/drift-monitor-designer/`
- Visual check: hero is 1600x900 and infographic is 1080x1350

author: ai-isaiah
body:
## Summary

Closes the last B7 piece — the cross-tab / cross-version localStorage-safety topic — across the **complete** surface. Every persistent client-state site is now either on the hardened `useCrossTabStorage` primitive or a documented sanctioned exception, which is the precondition for the planned B25 raw-`localStorage` lint ban.

**Migrated onto the primitive (3 real consumers):**
- **Factsheet view-state** (`factsheet-context.tsx`): an UNVERSIONED `factsheetViewStateCodec` — `encode` is a bare `JSON.stringify`, byte-identical to the pre-B7 write, so existing saved views load unchanged. Per-field salvage + prototype-poison stripping at decode. `crossTab: false` because view-state is co-mirrored in the URL query string and hydration is intentionally one-shot (URL-wins-over-storage reconciled once).
- **CollapsibleSection** open/closed → a `defaultOpen`-aware `rawStringCodec` at the unchanged raw key.
- **ComputeJobsTable** auto-refresh boolean → a `rawStringCodec` with SSR-safe deferred hydration (was a lazy `localStorage` read in the `useState` initializer).

**Sign-out purge gap closed:** `factsheet-v2:` and `factsheet-collapse:` added to `APP_NAMESPACED_PREFIXES`. Both factsheet key families were template-literal keys that slipped past the registry and were **not purged on a shared-device sign-out** before — net-new privacy fix.

**Three sanctioned exceptions documented (not migrated):** `widget_state_v2` (non-React URL-override flag), `/for-quants` fire-once **sessionStorage** view guard (tab isolation is the intent), and the wizard async Web-Crypto HMAC envelope + per-tab nonce (the synchronous `StorageCodec` interface cannot express `await crypto.subtle.sign`). Each carries a greppable `B7 sanctioned-exception:` rationale.

**Folded audit findings:** ForQuantsCtas H-0348 (stale "update when the wizard lands" docstring) and M-0368 (the empty auth-probe `catch` now leaves a fail-loud `console.warn` + Sentry breadcrumb); M-0369 (a module-scope view guard) was already closed by the existing sessionStorage guard.

## Test Coverage

New: a `FactsheetProvider` integration test (deferred-load adoption, URL-wins-over-storage precedence, write-path byte-compat with NO version envelope), a `CollapsibleSection` no-clobber-on-hydration assertion, and the `SignOutButton` purge inventory extended with both factsheet key families. The codec is unit-tested separately (byte-compat round-trip, reset outcomes, per-field salvage, poison-strip).

## Pre-Landing Review

5-lens adversarial review (Claude-only) + per-lens adversarial verification + comment-analyzer. **No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings** — all five storage invariants hold (byte-compat, fail-loud, SSR-safety, no hydration race, exceptions genuinely unsuitable). Only L-level findings surfaced (factsheet cross-tab adoption was inert → made explicit via `crossTab:false` + honest comment; a stale `storage-namespaces.ts` doc comment → corrected), all fixed in this PR.

## Verified

- tsc 0, lint 0 errors, full vitest **5497 pass / 0 fail**.

- [x] npm run lint — 0 errors
- [x] full vitest — 5497 passed, 0 failed

## Summary

Redesigns the setup/settings ConfigWizard so it scales with its growing option set, and folds in the wizard-scoped TMDB onboarding fixes from #243.

### Layout & structure
- **Wider modal** (800px → 1040px) with **collapsible groups** (native `<details>`) in Preferences and the new tab, so the page starts short and users open only what they need.
- **New "Data Sharing" tab** (step 4, before Preferences) consolidating everything that sends data off the machine: fingerprint network, AI assistance, and (gated) TheDiscDB.
- **Data-driven stepper** — `STEP_LABELS` → `totalSteps` → `aria-label`s (was hardcoded in three places).

### UI consistency
- The inline **"Forget me"** and **"Contribute from existing library"** actions rendered as bare text because `.btn-secondary`/`.btn-primary` are scoped to `.wizard-actions` (Tailwind preflight zeroes border/background otherwise). They now use the shared `SvActionButton` primitive.
- The anonymous-contribution-ID line became a **bordered panel with a disclosure status badge**.

### Clarity
- Refreshed stale fingerprint copy (it shares now, not "in future versions"); long help text in sentence case.

### TMDB onboarding — addresses #243 (P0/P1)
- **P0:** instructional placeholder instead of the token-shaped `eyJhbGci…` trap (an empty field could be mistaken for a filled one).
- **P1:** auto-validate on blur (inline ✓/✗) + first-run gate — onboarding can't pass the TMDB step without a validated token or an explicit "continue without token".
- P2 (dashboard "TMDB not configured" banner) and P3 (backend job-level surfacing) are tracked in #262.

## Design exploration
Both mockup directions (two-column / collapsible) are committed under `docs/design_handoff_synapse/explorations/`. The implemented design is the hybrid (collapsible groups + two-column AI fields), with Data Sharing before Preferences.

## Verification
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) ✅
- `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings 0`) ✅
- Live-rendered all three tabs (Data Sharing, Preferences, TMDB gate) against the real component.
- Updated the 4 E2E specs that hardcoded the old 4-step layout / fingerprint-on-Preferences. CI runs in settings mode (`global-setup` marks `setup_complete`), so the onboarding gate doesn't affect them.

First sub-slice of the async multiplayer backend (GDD 05-async-multiplayer, REQ-048/052/054/055).

## What this ships
- Pure, JSON-serializable match model in `src/match.ts`: a server-authoritative `MatchState` (id, 2-to-6 seats, per-seat name/secret/claimed/frames, open/active/complete status, `currentSeat`/`currentFrame`) with pure `createMatch` / `joinMatch` / `seatForSecret` / `toPublicMatch` transitions.
- Serverless route `api/match.ts` backed by the existing Upstash store in a distinct `vibepins:match:` keyspace (one store, namespaced per feature). POST without an id creates and returns seat 1 plus its secret; POST with an id joins the next open seat and activates a full match; GET `?id=` resumes and resolves the caller's seat from its per-seat secret.
- Matches persist with a one-week TTL refreshed on every read so a day-long game never expires mid-play. Match ids and per-seat secrets use `crypto.randomUUID`; secrets are returned only to the claiming device and never appear in the public match view.

## Why
Async turn-based multiplayer is the headline social feature. This lands the data model and the lifecycle flows it all hangs off, sized to one reviewable slice.

## Tests
- `tests/match.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/match.api.test.ts` (route handler, mocked Redis), `tests/match.smoke.test.ts` (create/join/resume round trip). 27 new tests; full suite 422 passing. Typecheck and build clean.

Turn-order enforcement (REQ-049), per-ball submission with server scoring (REQ-053), completion locking and final standings (REQ-056), handoff plus your-turn/waiting UI (REQ-050/051), posting a finished line to the leaderboard (REQ-058).

## Summary
OpenAI routing now stops sending oversized requests to peers that have already advertised a runtime context window too small for the request.

If every known target is too small, the proxy returns a clear OpenAI-style 503 instead of falling back to a guaranteed-bad upstream. Peers without runtime context metadata remain eligible so mixed-version meshes and legacy peers keep working.

This refresh also bounds the request-budget safety margin proportionally for tiny OpenAI requests, so strict context admission does not reject the CI smoke path purely because of a fixed reserve while larger requests keep the existing conservative margin cap.

## Why
Context-aware target ordering already preferred peers that could fit the estimated request budget, but the all-known-too-small case fell back to the original candidate list. That made route admission knowingly try targets that could not fit the request, producing slower retries or confusing upstream failures instead of an immediate, actionable response.

The first CI pass also exposed an important edge case: a tiny `--ctx-size 256` smoke request could be over-budgeted by the fixed 256-token margin alone. The fix keeps strict admission, but makes the margin scale with the estimated request size and caps it at the previous maximum.

## Diff scope
- Tightens context-aware candidate ordering so all-known-too-small targets produce no eligible candidate.
- Preserves unknown-context peers as fallback candidates for mixed-version compatibility.
- Returns a controlled 503 from the OpenAI proxy when no context-compatible target remains.
- Uses a bounded proportional request margin so small smoke requests fit tiny contexts while large requests keep the full safety cap.
- Adds unit and proxy regression coverage proving known-too-small upstreams are not contacted and small request budgets remain admissible.

author: danzeroum
body:
## Summary
This PR implements a secure authentication architecture where session state (roles, workspace) is verified server-side rather than trusted from client-side JWT decoding. It introduces token refresh capability, adds input validation, and hardens API key hashing with HMAC-SHA256.

## Key Changes

### Backend (Rust API)
- **New `/auth/me` endpoint**: Protected route that returns fresh user session data (user_id, workspace_id, name, email, role) from the database — the single source of truth for authorization
- **Token refresh endpoint** (`POST /auth/refresh`): Accepts a valid (non-expired) token and issues a new one without requiring login; includes fresh role lookup from database
- **Configurable JWT expiry**: Changed from hardcoded 30 days to `JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS` environment variable (default 1 hour); enables short-lived tokens with refresh flow
- **Input validation**: Added `validator` crate with field-level validation on `RegisterDto` and `LoginDto` (email format, password length, workspace name length)
- **API key security**: New `security.rs` module with HMAC-SHA256 hashing for API keys; supports legacy SHA-256 fallback during migration window
- **Protected routes separation**: Auth routes split into public (`/auth/register`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`) and protected (`/auth/me`) groups
- **Error handling**: Added `unprocessable_entity` error variant for validation failures; `ValidationErrors` implements `From<AppError>`

### Frontend (Angular)
- **Server-side session verification**: `AuthService.verifySession()` calls `GET /auth/me` to fetch fresh user data; this is the only authoritative source for roles/workspace
- **Token refresh in interceptor**: `authInterceptor` now catches 401 responses and automatically attempts `POST /auth/refresh` with the current token; concurrent refresh requests share the same Observable (prevents thundering herd)
- **Guard refactoring**: Both `authGuard` and `adminGuard` now call `verifySession()` instead of decoding JWT locally; authorization decisions are server-verified
- **Session cleanup**: Centralized `clearSession()` function removes JWT, refresh token, and user data from localStorage
- **Markdown pipe security**: Clarified that HTML is sanitized before being returned (no `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`); re-sanitization happens on `[innerHTML]` binding

### Configuration & Security
- **Environment variables**: 
  - `JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS`: Token lifetime (default 1)
  - `API_KEY_HMAC_SECRET`: Required for API key hashing (no default)
  - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`: Shared secret for internal service-to-service calls (embedding, document processor, reranker)
  - `EMBEDDING_MODEL_REVISION`: Fixed HuggingFace commit hash to prevent supply-chain attacks when using `trust_remote_code`
  - `DATABASE_URL`: Now required (no hardcoded default) for both Rust API and Python trainer
- **CORS configuration**: Allowed origins read from `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` CSV environment variable (default: `http://localhost:4200`)
- **Python services**: Added `verify_internal_token()` dependency to embedding, document processor services; validates `X-Internal-Token` header

### Testing
- **Guard tests rewritten**: Removed JWT decoding/expiry checks; now mock `AuthService.verifySession()` and test authorization logic only
- **Test helpers**: Updated `AppState` initialization to include `api_key_hmac_secret`

## Notable Implementation Details
- **No refresh token**: The system uses short-lived access tokens (default 1h) that are renewed via `/auth/refresh` while still valid; expired tokens force re-login
- **Concurrent refresh deduplication**: Multiple simultaneous 401 responses share a single refresh Observable, preventing race conditions
- **HMAC migration path**: API key verification accepts both HMAC (current) and SHA-256 (legacy) hashes; allows gradual key rotation without downtime
- **Server-side role authority**: Guards and interceptor never trust client-side JWT decoding; all authorization decisions verified via `/auth/me` endpoint

**WS-1 of the dark-factory hands-off hardening program** (52 audit findings → 7 workstreams). This is the CRITICAL one: the operator's #1 promise — kill any loop from the UI — was broken.

## What was broken
- **`DiagramLoop` UI kill-switch was a silent no-op.** `worker_name="diagram-loop"` (hyphen) while the orchestrator registry, `worker_catalog`, `constants.js`, and `BGWorkerManager` all key `diagram_loop` (underscore). `is_enabled('diagram-loop')` hit the `.get(name, True)` default forever — the System-tab toggle, the dashboard heartbeat, **and** CostBudgetWatcher's emergency budget kill were all no-ops for the highest-autonomy loop (opens arch-regen PRs every 4h). Even its status events were mis-keyed.
- **4 loops never called the in-body `_enabled_cb` gate** (`cost_budget_watcher`, `diagram`, `entry_evidence`, `pricing_refresh`) — they gated only on an env/config `*_enabled` flag, so the UI toggle was rendered but inert on the startup-catchup and manual-trigger paths.
- **The one regression test lied.** `test_canonical_killswitch.py` `xfail(strict=False)`'d the 3 genuinely-broken loops behind a fabricated "AsyncMock fixture drift" reason and its docstring claimed all 6 respected `_enabled_cb`. The auto-discovery enforcer `dark-factory.md §5` advertises (`test_loop_kill_switch_completeness.py`) was never committed.

## Fix
- Canonicalize `DiagramLoop.worker_name` to `diagram_loop`.
- Add the ADR-0049 in-body gate as the FIRST `_do_work` statement in all 4 loops (env/config gate kept below as deploy-time defense-in-depth).
- New **`tests/test_loop_kill_switch_completeness.py`** ratchet (empty grandfather list) + a `worker_names_are_underscore_canonical` guard that catches the hyphen class of bug at the source for every loop.
- Un-muzzle `test_canonical_killswitch.py`: remove the 3 false xfails, add the omitted `entry_evidence` case, fix the docstring.

## Verification
- `make quality` green: **13700 passed, 18 skipped, 193 xfailed** in 10m26s (this PR *removes* 3 false xfails).

author: arreyder
body:
## Summary

`Compact()` builds `runCtx = context.WithTimeout(ctx, c.runDuration)` but the loop calls `doOneCompaction(ctx, ...)`. The deadline only gates the pre-flight select; individual compactions then run under the unbounded parent ctx and can blow past `c.runDuration`.

This is the sibling of the bug fixed in #893 (`WriteEnvelope` walked under an unbounded context). Same shape: a deadline-bearing context exists but inner work uses a different one, so the deadline dangles instead of bounding the work.

## Change

- `pkg/synccompactor/compactor.go`: pass `runCtx` into `doOneCompaction` so `c.runDuration` actually limits the loop.
- When `runCtx` fires *due to its own deadline* (not parent cancellation), surface the same clean **\"compaction run duration has expired\"** message the pre-flight select already uses, instead of letting a bare `context.DeadlineExceeded` bubble out of inner SQLite operations. The error is still returned so callers can decide whether to retry.

## Impact

Caller-visible behavior change for callers that pass `WithRunDuration`:

- **Before:** `c.runDuration` only checked at entry; individual compactions could run as long as the parent ctx allowed. If they did eventually fail (e.g. heartbeat timeout during a long SQLite operation), the error was a raw `context deadline exceeded` from inside `ExecContext`.
- **After:** each `doOneCompaction` is bounded by `c.runDuration`. When the deadline fires, the loop exits with `compaction run duration has expired: context deadline exceeded`, and the structured log identifies which sync was in flight and how many remain.

Callers that don't use `WithRunDuration` are unaffected — `runCtx == ctx` in that branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./pkg/synccompactor/...`
- [x] `go vet ./pkg/synccompactor/...`
- [x] `go test ./pkg/synccompactor/...` (all existing tests pass)
- [ ] CI

## Context

Surfaced by a code-review bot on a separate compaction stuck-state investigation. Lilly's Entra connector compaction was failing at ~98 min with `context deadline exceeded` from inside `CompactGrants` even though `WithRunDuration(1h)` was passed — because `runCtx` was created but not threaded into the loop, the deadline never fired cleanly; instead the activity hit its Temporal heartbeat timeout while SQLite was blocking.

This PR alone won't unblock Lilly (the compaction still doesn't fit in 1h), but it makes the failure intentional and legible, and matches the contract the option name implies.
