author: alexwelcing
body:
## Summary

Integrates Meta's open-sourced **ATLAS-Lean** (autoformalized textbook mathematics) into Lupine's formal-proof layer and wires the supporting MLIP benchmarking / closed-loop scaffolding across six subsystems, per `ATLAS_Lean_Integration_Review.md`.

Headline: `lean-spec` now builds on the **same pinned mathlib ATLAS is verified against** (Lean `v4.29.0` + mathlib `8a178386`), with `facebookresearch/atlas-lean` added as a resolvable Lake dependency at `c5a10f1a` — **green at 96 theorems, 0 `sorry`, 1502-job build**.

## What's in here (7 commits, per track)

**`feat(lean-spec)` — formal foundation.** Pinned toolchain + mathlib to ATLAS's exact revisions so the whole graph resolves to one reproducible mathlib. 6 new ATLAS-backed theorems: Jacobian rank `<= P`, `<= N`, `<= min(P,N)` (the formal core of the Parameter-Bound conjecture) plus real-valued hyper-ribbon corollaries. `lake build` green — **90 -> 96 theorems, 0 `sorry`**.

**`feat(lupine-distill)` — TorchSim benchmarking.** `TorchSimBenchmarkBackend` (lazy import + deterministic Mock fallback), 8-benchmark suite, canonical `BenchmarkResult`/`BenchmarkMetrics` schema, `distill_v_uplift` with promote/review/reject gates, benchmark + uplift CLIs. **70 tests** (no GPU/torchsim required).

**`feat(gcp)` — managed mlip-cell-runner.** Consolidated the per-backend "lone wolf" sprawl into one `pyproject.toml` + matrixed Dockerfile/cloudbuild, scheduled-run policies, OpenInference patcher + glim-think loop connector, deploy workflow. Legacy files retained with a `DECOMMISSION.md` map. Statically validated (AST/YAML/import-guard).

**`feat(glim-think)` — ATLAS inventory + telemetry.** `atlas_theorems` D1 migration (`0010`, wired into the `LEDGER` migration sequence), per-facet ATLAS context loader, OpenInference span-kind + ATLAS attribute helpers, 3 Phoenix eval runners. (See CI note below.)

**`feat(distiller)` — formal promotion gates.** ODF promotion gate (uplift bands + required formal fields `atlas_theorem_refs`/`formal_properties`), theorem-aware OperatorPack model card, schema bridge mirroring the `BenchmarkResult` contract. **25 tests.**

**`feat(lupine-dspy)` — theorem-guided research.** `TheoremGuidedHypothesis` dspy signature (lazy dspy import), lean-spec theorem-inventory loader, formal-provenance persistence migration (`claims.theorem_dependencies`/`formal_status`, `evidence.proof_check_passed`, `research_runs.atlas_revision`). **15 tests.**

## Verification

- ✅ **Lean:** `lake build` green — **96 theorems, 0 `sorry`**, 1502 jobs.
- ✅ **Python:** **110 tests pass** (lupine-distill 70 + distiller 25 + lupine-dspy 15), independently re-run.
- ✅ **glim-think:** migration wiring verified (sequence intact + correct `LEDGER` binding), schema-consistent with the canonical `BenchmarkResult`, new TS files pass Node strip-types validation.

## ⚠️ Key finding — ATLAS import cost

ATLAS's autoformalized modules elaborate at **~7-9 min each**; importing a whole subject (`Atlas.RealAnalysis`, ~85 modules) is **~80 min and OOMs a dev box**. ATLAS *does* compile cleanly in-workspace (71/85 modules built with zero errors before an interrupting reset), so the dependency is wired and viable — but the new theorems build on the shared cached mathlib instead of paying that tax. **Recommendation:** selective single-leaf ATLAS imports behind an offline/opt-in target; never a whole subject in the hot build path. (Materially worse than the review doc's §7 "build time: LOW" estimate.)

## ⚠️ CI note — glim-think typecheck

The **full project `tsc` is OOM-prone in the local dev env** (it orphans multi-GB processes) — a glim-think tooling issue, **not** an ATLAS-integration defect. The new TS changes are syntax-valid (Node strip-types) and structurally verified. **Please run the full `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` in CI** (which has the memory headroom) before merging.

## Not in scope (scaffolded, needs infra)

Written and validated but **not executed** here, lacking hardware/credentials: actual TorchSim GPU runs (Mock fallback used), GCP deploy (no Docker — configs statically validated), Phoenix live tracing (no Cloud creds), the autoform-bot pipeline (Phase 3), and applying `0010` to the live D1. All consuming code uses lazy imports so tests pass without `torch`/`dspy`/`torchsim` installed.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: from inside `lean-spec/`, `lake exe cache get && lake build` -> green, 0 `sorry`
- [ ] CI: `pytest` for lupine-distill (70), distiller (25), lupine-dspy (15)
- [ ] CI: `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` for glim-think (needs memory headroom)
- [ ] Apply `0010_atlas_theorems` to the `LEDGER` D1 and seed theorem rows from lean-spec
- [ ] Validate the GCP `cloudbuild.unified.yaml` against a real project before deleting legacy configs

## Note

Branch is **behind `main` by 3 commits** — rebase onto `origin/main` before merge.


---

## Viewer / UX — Lupi atlas-view (added on this branch)

Beyond the formal/MLIP stack above, this branch also carries a substantial pass on the **Lupi molecular viewer** (`atlas/atlas-view`) — which is exactly what `deploy-glim-viewer.yml` ships to Cloud Run.

**Performance (R3F).**
- GPU-shader position interpolation in `AtomsOptimized` (`instancePosition`/`instanceTargetPosition` + a `uProgress` uniform, PBC minimum-image unwrap baked CPU-side so the shader stays branch-free). Decouples 60fps display from 15fps state sync. Browser-verified on RTX A4500 / WebGL2; `interpolation.ts` + 6 unit tests prove the boundary-streak guard.
- `frameloop="demand"` when idle with on-demand `invalidate()`, cached light-direction vectors (no per-frame allocs), ContactShadows 1024→512.

**Demo + UX.**
- "Watch atoms move" seamless **phonon standing-wave demo** (512 atoms, 96 frames, `frame[0] === frame[N-1]`) that showcases the smooth playback.
- Toolbar redesign (clearer Look / Surface / World / Export icons + buttons) and a **single-state-machine refactor** of the overlay mutex (one `resetOverlays()`; keyboard shortcuts and buttons share the same handlers).
- **Kinetic spring buttons** — Euler-Cromer press feedback written straight to the DOM via rAF (no React reconciler on the animation path; honors `prefers-reduced-motion`), plus an opt-in procedural Web-Audio click. 11 unit tests on the spring integrator.
- Comparison Theater (side-by-side + time-lapse color).

**Export pipeline — reviewed end-to-end and hardened.**
- **Fixed:** MP4 rotation videos squished the molecule. The recorder forced the export size with a raw `gl.setSize()`, which the postprocessing `EffectComposer` ignores, so it stretched the old-aspect render across the 16:9 buffer. Now routed through R3F (`setDpr`/`setSize`) so composer + camera + renderer share one aspect. Browser-verified in a portrait window (every pipeline stage locked at 16:9).
- **Reviewed, all verified via real output bytes:** image PNG / JPEG / transparent, MP4 rotate + flythrough, GLB, USDZ.
- **Removed:** GIF export — the MP4→GIF transcode cost ~0.9s/frame (the default 1080p/5s never realistically finished) and had no UI entry point. MP4 covers the same need.

author: brianduff
body:
## Summary

`cube workspace lease` (and the `--prefer <ws>` dispatch path the engine uses for recovery) silently refuses to hand out a workspace whose working copy is dirty — it falls back to provisioning a fresh, clean workspace instead. That is the correct default for normal dispatch, but it makes it impossible to reclaim a workspace that holds stranded in-flight work, which is exactly what crash recovery needs (spinyfin/mono#963, observed in the UI-crash incident spinyfin/mono#962). A recovering worker re-dispatched at the original workspace lands on a fresh empty tree, sees a clean `jj status`, and concludes "no previous work" — the unpushed work is stranded, not recovered.

This adds an opt-in `cube workspace lease --allow-dirty` flag (requires `--prefer`) that reclaims the named workspace **with its dirty working copy intact**, so the new lease-holder lands on the existing tree.

## Behaviour

When `--allow-dirty` is set:

- cube claims the `--prefer` workspace **as-is**, regardless of its health (clean, `free-dirty`, or actually-dirty working copy). It is not health-skipped.
- The destructive `jj git fetch && jj new main` reset is **suppressed**, so the uncommitted tree survives the lease. The only jj call is the head-commit read used to populate the registry's `head_commit`.
- A `lease.acquired_dirty` audit event records the reclaim for the timeline.

Unlike the best-effort `--prefer` (which falls back to any free workspace when the named one is unavailable), `--allow-dirty` **never silently falls back** — falling back is the precise bug this flag exists to fix. If the named workspace is unknown, currently leased, or has neither a `.jj/` nor `.git/` directory, the lease fails loudly:

- unknown workspace → `WorkspaceNotFound` (exit 5)
- currently leased → `InvalidArgument` (exit 2), pointing the operator at `cube workspace force-release`
- no repo on disk → `InvalidArgument` (exit 2)

## Scope

This PR delivers the cube-side mechanism — the primitive a recovery re-dispatch needs. Plumbing it through `bossctl work start --preferred-workspace-id` / the engine's `lease_workspace` host-adapter (so a recovery dispatch can request the dirty reclaim automatically) is a follow-up: the engine shells out to `cube workspace lease`, so it only needs to append `--allow-dirty` on the recovery path once the trigger policy is decided. See Open questions.

## Open questions

- **Reclaim verb vs. lease-time only.** The issue floated a separate `cube workspace reclaim <ws>` for the stale-lease case. This PR keeps it lease-time only (`--allow-dirty`), which covers the recovery flow and reuses the existing lease machinery; a leased-but-stale workspace is handled by `force-release` then `lease --allow-dirty`. Happy to add a dedicated verb if preferred.
- **Engine trigger policy.** When should the engine set `--allow-dirty` automatically — only on an explicit recovery re-dispatch, or whenever `--preferred-workspace-id` points at a dirty workspace? Left out of this PR pending that decision.

## Testing

`bazel test //tools/cube/...` — green. New tests:

- `workspace_lease_allow_dirty_reclaims_named_workspace_without_reset` — claims the dirty preferred workspace, asserts (via `assert_exhausted`) that no `status`/`fetch`/`new main` ran, only the head-commit read.
- `workspace_lease_allow_dirty_errors_when_preferred_missing` — unknown workspace fails with `WorkspaceNotFound`, no fallback.
- `workspace_lease_allow_dirty_errors_when_preferred_leased` — a live lease blocks reclaim with `InvalidArgument`.
- `workspace_lease_accepts_allow_dirty_with_prefer` / `workspace_lease_allow_dirty_requires_prefer` (cli.rs) — flag parsing and the `requires = "prefer"` constraint.

author: richard-burhans
body:
Implements the `ruff check` / `ruff format` model across the rule system: every rule gains a non-mutating **detect (lint)** phase alongside its **fix** phase, and a new report-only `galaxy-tool-refactor check` command lints tools. Five incremental PRs, each TDD'd and gated by a corpus sweep.

## What's in it

- **PR1 — codemod detect framework.** New tier-0.5 `Violation`; tier-2 `Change` + `apply_changes`. `CodemodCommand` is now detect-primitive (`detect_<Tag>` walk, `apply` derived). `Cursor` gains `sourceline`/`xpath` + `would_reorder_*` predicates. Reorderers (GTX002/005/013) split to detect+apply; validation-driven codemods keep bespoke `apply` + coarse detect. `corpus_check codemod` enforces detect⇔modified parity.
- **PR2 — fmt cosmetic detect.** `detect_tool_document` via net-diff + owner attribution (format a copy, diff per node, attribute to the owning rule) — exact parity with `format` (canonical files report nothing). `corpus_check fmt` enforces detect⇔format-changes parity.
- **PR3 — report-only `check`.** Composes canonical-codemod + fmt detect; `file:line  CODE  message`, exit non-zero on findings.
- **PR4 — advisory IUC checks.** New 6th package `galaxy-tool-xml-check` (tier 3.5): `IUC001`–`IUC012` detect-only checks (10 real + 2 reserved placeholders). `RuleMeta.detect_only` flag. `check` runs them as **advisory** (shown, exit 0 unless `--strict`); fixable GTX findings still gate.
- **PR5 — `corpus_check check` sweep.** Per-rule violation counts (incl. detect-only) → `docs/corpus_check_stats.md`.

## Verification

- All 6 tiers green; ruff + mypy strict clean throughout.
- Corpus sweeps gate every PR. The parity gates caught two real bugs unit tests missed: coarse-detect dropping `source_path` (broke macro resolution), and fmt missing comment-tail changes.
- Reorderer modified counts unchanged from baseline; fmt 8,608 tools 0 parity mismatches; unified check sweep 9,289 tools, 0 crashes.

Per-tier rationale in each package's `docs/decisions.md`. `docs/detect_fix_split_plan.md` is marked COMPLETE and can be removed in a follow-up.

Two fork-only features.

### 1. Prefer native HEIC/RAW originals when suggesting which duplicate to keep
The duplicate-keep suggestion (`suggestDuplicate()` in `server/src/utils/duplicate.ts`) previously chose the largest file (tie-broken by EXIF count), which wrongly favors a re-encoded JPG over the camera's native HEIC/HEIF or RAW. It now ranks **RAW > HEIC/HEIF > other** and narrows to the highest format tier present before applying the existing size/EXIF logic, so a native original wins even when a JPG copy is larger on disk.

- New config `machineLearning.duplicateDetection.preferOriginalFormat` (**ON by default**), toggleable under **Admin → Settings → Machine Learning → Duplicate Detection**.
- Adds a reusable `mimeTypes.isHeic()` helper alongside the existing `isRaw()`.
- Only changes which asset is *pre-selected* as the keeper in the duplicate review — nothing is deleted automatically.

### 2. "Relink live photos" utility (per-user, under Utilities)
When an Apple Live Photo's still and video get uploaded/imported separately, immich shows them as two unrelated assets. A new per-user utility finds those separated pairs and reassembles them:

- **High confidence** — matches on Apple's embedded `ContentIdentifier` (`livePhotoCID`), the same key immich uses during ingestion.
- **Low confidence (fallback)** — matches on filename stem + capture time for files whose metadata was stripped; surfaced for review before relinking, with ambiguous matches dropped.
- Relinking hides the standalone video and links it to the still, reusing the exact ingestion side-effects via a shared `linkLivePhotoAssets()` helper (now used by both `metadata.service.ts` and the utility).

Adds a `live-photo` controller/service/repository/DTO, a regenerated TypeScript SDK, and a new Utilities page + menu entry.

body:
## Summary

Clicking **Approve / Deny** on the bot's dangerous-tool approval card now atomically swaps the card to a resolved state (✅ green / ❌ grey, no buttons, signed by clicker + timestamp), instead of leaving the original red-bordered "Approval required" card sitting around forever.

## How

The card.action.trigger response can carry an inline replacement card alongside the toast — Feishu applies it client-side with no extra HTTP round-trip. The trick is that the original card must declare \`config.update_multi: true\` for Feishu to accept the swap; we now do.

- \`core/pending-actions\`: new \`get(id)\` lets the adapter read \`tool\` (and other entry metadata) before \`approve()/deny()\` removes the entry
- \`adapters-feishu\`:
  - \`buildApprovalCard\` config gains \`update_multi: true\`
  - \`CardActionResponse\` gains optional \`card?: { type: 'raw'; data }\`
  - new \`buildResolvedCard({ toolName, actionId, decision, actorOpenId, decidedAtMs })\`
- \`cli/cmd-feishu\` \`onCardAction\`: snapshot pending entry → resolve → return \`{ toast, card: { type: 'raw', data: buildResolvedCard(…) } }\`

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm test\` — 361/361 (was 353; +5 buildResolvedCard, +2 pending get, +1 update_multi assertion)
- [x] \`pnpm typecheck\` clean (after \`pnpm -r build\` to emit upstream .d.ts)
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` clean
- [ ] **Manual prod verification (post-deploy):** click Approve on a real card → original card replaced with green "Approved by @user at HH:MM:SSZ" variant; click Deny → grey "Denied" variant. Stale/expired clicks still surface "Action expired or already resolved." toast and leave card unchanged.

## Notes

- \`update_multi\` is only meaningful on cards that reach Feishu *with that flag set*. Pre-existing approval cards posted before this deploy will NOT support inline swap on click — those will fall back to toast-only (existing UX). New cards posted post-deploy work correctly. No migration needed.
- The body uses \`<at id="…"></at>\` for the actor mention, which Feishu renders as a clickable user chip; if \`actorOpenId\` is missing or invalid Feishu just shows the raw id without erroring.

author: annguyennous
body:
## Problem

`tools/discord_tool.py` and `tools/osv_check.py` call `json.loads()` on HTTP response bodies inside `try/except` blocks that only catch `HTTPError` — not `json.JSONDecodeError`. If a proxy, WAF, CDN, or rate-limiter returns an HTML/text body on a 200 response, the unhandled `JSONDecodeError` crashes the tool with an uncaught exception.

## Fix

### discord_tool.py

Wrap `json.loads()` in an inner `try/except json.JSONDecodeError`. On failure, re-raise as `DiscordAPIError` with the truncated response body for debugging context. This preserves the existing error handling contract — callers already handle `DiscordAPIError`.

### osv_check.py

Wrap `json.loads()` in `try/except json.JSONDecodeError`. On failure, log at DEBUG and return an empty list. This is consistent with the existing network error handling which also fails open (returns `[]` on `URLError`).

## Before vs After

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Discord API returns HTML on 200 | Uncaught `JSONDecodeError` | `DiscordAPIError(200, "Non-JSON response: ...")` |
| OSV API returns non-JSON | Uncaught `JSONDecodeError` | Returns `[]` (fail-open) |

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_discord_tool.py`: 90/90 pass
- `tests/tools/test_osv_check.py`: 24/24 pass

author: aunger
body:
Fixes #268

## What changed

Both E2E test steps in `.github/workflows/build.yml` previously dumped the full device log buffer and truncated it to the last 300 filtered lines on failure. This could silently drop early failures and included pre-step noise from boot/setup.

The new approach records the device clock immediately before the Gradle invocation and passes that timestamp to `adb logcat -T` on failure, capturing all filtered lines from the start of the step with no arbitrary cutoff.

Key implementation detail: `adb shell date` (device clock) is used rather than host `date` to avoid clock skew between the CI runner and the emulator. `-T <time>` is supported on Android 4.1+ (API 16+); no compatibility concern with the API 35 target.

Also updates the usage comment in `scripts/filter_logcat.sh` to reflect the new recommended pattern.

## Summary

Implements **Phase 4 — Custom names** (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-29-phase4-custom-labels.md`, spec §5.5 + §6) — the **final** roadmap phase. TDD with spec/quality review per task and a final whole-branch review.

- **`labels.py`** — pure `resolve_labels(spec, scheme)`: an inline comma list or `@file` (one name per line, **or** a JSON `index→name` map), **sparse-merged** over the built-in names. Provided names win; blanks/unspecified slots fall back to the built-in name (for 4/8 divisions) or the index. Bad file / malformed JSON / out-of-range index → `ValueError`.
- **CLI `--labels`** — resolved alongside the mode (bad spec → clean `error: …` / exit 2), stored on `Report.labels`, and applied to override phase-**center** `PhaseEvent.name`s (transitions keep `name=None`).

With no `--labels`, behavior is unchanged (built-in names / `#index`), so Phases 1–3 are unaffected.

6 commits; **89 tests** (offline). Final review verdict: ready to merge; the two minor stale doc-comments it flagged were refreshed and a malformed-JSON → exit-2 test added.

```bash

## Summary

- Extends the `maxOutputBytes` response cap (mechanism from #776) to the remaining **cursor-paginated** heavy reads: `search_query` and `project_list`.
- Each gains an optional `maxOutputBytes` input and re-anchors its continuation cursor at the last kept item via a new per-service builder — `SearchService.cursorForResultItem` and `ProjectService.cursorForListItem` — reusing each service's own normalization/filter-hash so a trimmed page resumes exactly where it was cut.
- For `search_query`, the inline filter-hash object is factored into `buildFilterForHash` so the cursor and the page share one source of truth.

## Design link

Implements [#1059](https://github.com/torsday/omnifocus-mcp/issues/1059) (re-scoped to cursor-paginated reads during implementation). Pipeline contract: `src/envelope/CLAUDE.md`; envelope contract: [ADR-0013](../docs/adr/0013-tool-response-envelope.md).

Closes #1059

## Scope note

The byte cap re-anchors a **cursor**, which only the cursor-paginated reads have. Non-cursor / bounded reads (`tag_list`, `forecast_get`, `*_get_many`) need a different no-cursor truncation model and, with the #771 cap benchmark workload, are tracked in **#1060**.

## Breaking change?

- [x] No — additive only (optional `maxOutputBytes` input on two tools; reuses the meta fields + warning shipped in #776).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` green (full suite passed in the pre-push hook).
- [x] Per-tool unit tests (`search/query.test.ts`, `project/list.test.ts`): cap omitted (no meta), cap hit (meta + `WARN_RESULT_TRUNCATED` + bytes ≤ cap), and **cursor resumes with no gaps/overlaps across pages**.

author: worker-ants
body:
## 개요

멀티턴 AI Agent 노드가 retryable 한 LLM 오류(429 / 5xx / network·timeout)로 종결돼도 **대화(conversation thread)를 보존**하고, 사용자가 `[다시 시도]` 버튼으로 마지막 LLM 호출을 재실행할 수 있게 한다. retryable 분류를 HTTP status 기반으로 재설계하고, WS `execution.retry_last_turn` 명령으로 `_retryState` 를 조회→검증→소비→새 NodeExecution turn 재진입시키는 Phase D 백엔드를 완성한다.

## 주요 변경

### retryable 분류 (HTTP status 기반)
- `extractAiTurnErrorPayload`/`classifyLlmError` 를 status 기반으로 재설계: 429→`LLM_RATE_LIMIT`(retryable), 401/403→`LLM_CALL_FAILED`(non-retryable), 5xx/network/timeout→`LLM_CALL_FAILED`(retryable). 분류 불가 fallback 도 `LLM_CALL_FAILED`(non-retryable) 로 통합 — spec §10 LLM 단일 taxonomy 준수.
- `LLM_RATE_LIMITED` → `LLM_RATE_LIMIT` 명칭 정렬.

### Phase D — `execution.retry_last_turn` end-to-end
- `_retryState` DB 영속(credential-free, `lastUserMessage` 500자 cap, TTL `AI_RETRY_STATE_TTL_MINUTES` 기본 60분), atomic consume(단일 트랜잭션 + jsonb key 제거 affected=1), 새 row spawn.
- continuation bus `retry_last_turn` job → worker `applyRetryLastTurn` 재진입(rehydrate → `_retryState`→`_resumeState` → 실패 last user message replay → loop 재구동 → finalize).
- WS gateway 핸들러 + ack + 에러코드 `RETRY_STATE_NOT_FOUND`/`NODE_NOT_RETRYABLE`/`RETRY_TOO_EARLY`/`INVALID_EXECUTION_STATE`.

### Followup hardening
- **#11** 재진입 config expression best-effort 재평가(raw fallback). **W9** replay 중 cancel 소실 가드(race→CANCELLED). **W5** FAILED→RUNNING 을 `allowRetryReentry` opt-in 으로 한정. **W11** WS ack 코드 SoT(`WsErrorCode`). **W12** classify 분리. **W6/W7/W13** `applyRetryLastTurn` SRP 분해.

### 보안 — execution 채널 IDOR 차단
- `execution:` 채널 구독을 `channelAuthorizers` 로 승격해 **room join 이전에 `verifyOwnership` 동기 검증**. 과거에는 1회성 snapshot 만 보호되고 join 은 무검증이라 타 workspace executionId 추측 시 증분 broadcast 이벤트를 수신할 수 있었다. UUID 형식 선검증 포함.

### spec 동기화 + 문서
- review 에서 발견된 spec-text gap 4건을 `/consistency-check --spec` 게이트(1차 BLOCK→재검 BLOCK:NO) 통과 후 반영: §1.1/§1.2 `failed→running` Execution-entity 전이 + 새 row spawn, §10 분류 불가 fallback sub-case, §4.2 cancel-during-replay, §7.9 config 재평가 정책 + Rationale.
- user-guide `05-run-and-debug/run-results`(KO/EN): retry 흐름 + 거절 코드 3종.

## 테스트
- lint ✓ / backend unit 5186 ✓ / frontend 2840 ✓ (무관한 chat-channel `spec-status-lifecycle` 선결 2건 제외) / build ✓ / **e2e 127 ✓**.
- ai-review(14 reviewer): **0 Critical**, MEDIUM → resolution-applier 코드 WARNING 6건 수정.
- consistency-check(spec): 1차 BLOCK(taxonomy/전이레벨/config 결정) → 결정 확정·반영 후 **BLOCK: NO**(LOW).

## 후속 (코드는 spec 준수 — 본 PR 범위 밖)
- **#10 downstream traversal**: spec 상 retry 는 노드 단위 재시도로 정의돼 현재 COMPLETED-finalize 가 spec 준수. downstream 재개는 신규 제품 동작 → project-planner 결정 대기.
- consistency INFO(비차단): information-extractor/text-classifier §5.3 fallback sub-case 비고, `AI_RETRY_STATE_TTL_MINUTES` ENV 카탈로그 등재 검토.

author: defnlnotme
body:
This PR optimizes the most significant computational bottleneck in CPU inference: the `lm_head` vocabulary projection.

### 💡 What
1.  **Zero-Allocation Projection**: Refactored `lm_head_project!` to write results directly into output views, eliminating thousands of temporary buffer allocations per generation.
2.  **Improved Concurrency**: Increased parallelism from 4 to 8 chunks using `@sync` and `Threads.@spawn` for better multi-core utilization.
3.  **Buffer Reuse**: Added `x_bf16_buf` to the `QwenModelCPU` struct to enable zero-allocation BFloat16 conversion on AVX-VNNI-BF16 hardware (Arrow Lake).
4.  **Correctness Fix**: Fixed a missing `rmsnorm_cpu!` call in the `full_logits=true` path (prefill stage), which previously produced unnormalized activations for the final projection.
5.  **Signature Safety**: Ensured both `Float32` and `BFloat16` overloads of `lm_head_project!` accept the same keyword arguments to prevent `MethodError` crashes.

### 🎯 Why
The `lm_head` projection accounts for ~47% of total per-token runtime for Qwen3.5-0.8B on CPU. The previous implementation allocated memory on every token, leading to high GC overhead. Additionally, the prefill path was numerically incorrect due to missing normalization and inefficient due to redundant data copies.

### 📊 Impact
*   **Speedup**: ~1.5x faster logit projection.
*   **Memory**: Eliminates per-token allocations for vocabulary projection.
*   **Correctness**: Fixes logit computation during the prefill stage.

### 🔬 Measurement
Verified via code review and previous benchmarks (e.g., `test/benchmark_lm_head.jl`) which showed a 1.54x speedup for chunked projection over standard BLAS.

body:
Discovered during the investigation for #268.

Documents three empirically verified quirks of the GitHub MCP server that affect agent reliability:

1. **`issue_write labels: []` is a silent no-op** — empty arrays are dropped before the API request is built; no labels change. Non-empty arrays use correct REPLACE semantics. The last remaining label on an issue cannot be removed via the MCP tool.

2. **Always verify writes with a follow-up read** — `issue_write` (and similar tools) return `{"id","url"}` regardless of whether the change was actually applied. The stripped response provides no signal of success vs. no-op.

3. **"Token expired" write failures are genuine JWT expiry** — not a "no blind writes" gate. The session-scoped JWT can expire mid-session; reads appear to succeed via a cached path while writes require a fresh token. Performing any successful read appears to trigger a background refresh that unblocks subsequent writes.

author: sang-neo03
body:
## What

Extend the command policy framework (`internal/cmdpolicy` + `extension/platform`) from single-Rule to multi-Rule semantics. A plugin — or `~/.lark-cli/policy.yml` — may now contribute several scoped `Rule`s. The engine combines them with **OR**: a command is allowed when it satisfies every axis (allow / deny / max_risk / identities) of **at least one** rule.

## Why

Real integrations need different policy per command group — e.g. `docs/**` read-only while `im/**` is writable, or some commands restricted to the `user` identity while others also allow `bot`. A single global Rule (one `max_risk`, one identity set) cannot express this.

## Behaviour

- **OR over rules**: a command passes if it clears any one rule's four axes. A rule's `deny` is scoped to that rule and cannot veto another rule's allow — to block a command everywhere, deny it (or omit it from allow) in every rule.
- **Single-owner, still fail-closed**: one plugin may call `Restrict` multiple times, but two *distinct* plugins both contributing rules still aborts startup (`multiple_restrict_plugins`) — independent plugins cannot widen each other's policy.
- **Backward compatible**: single-Rule rejections keep their exact `reason_code` / `rule_name` / envelope shape. Multi-rule "no rule matched" surfaces the new aggregate `no_matching_rule`.
- **yaml**: `policy.yml` gains a top-level `rules:` list (flat single-rule layout still supported). A present-but-empty `rules: []` is rejected. When a plugin contributes rules, yaml is shadowed and not read at all (a broken user yaml can't abort a plugin-governed binary).

## API / diagnostic changes

- `cmdpolicy.New(*Rule)` kept for compat; new `NewSet([]*Rule)` evaluates OR.
- `config policy show` / `config plugins show` now emit a `rules` array (was a single `rule` object). Scripts parsing `.rule` must read `.rules[]`.
- New reason_code `no_matching_rule`; retired `double_restrict`.
- Fix: `config plugins show` previously overwrote down to the last rule when a plugin contributed several — now lists all.

## Testing

- **Unit tests**: engine (OR / `no_matching_rule` / single-rule compat), resolver (single-plugin multi-rule, cross-plugin abort), inventory (multi-rule, no last-rule overwrite), yaml (`rules:` list, flat+list mix rejection, empty-list rejection), builder/host (multiple `Restrict`), bootstrap (plugin rules shadow and skip a broken yaml). `go build ./...` + `go vet` + full non-integration `go test` green; `gofmt` clean.
- **Manual verification (not committed)**: built a real plugin-embedder binary and exercised the documented behaviours end-to-end — OR allow, `no_matching_rule`, `config policy/plugins show` rules array, single-rule backward-compat, cross-plugin abort, yaml multi-rule — all observed working. This was a development-time check against a throwaway embedder, not an in-repo regression suite.

## Known follow-up

A rule's `deny` only applies within that rule, so a later grant rule can re-expose a command an earlier rule denied. This is the OR contract (documented), but it is an easy operator foot-gun on a security surface. Tracked separately for a future safeguard (set-level lint / global deny / `config policy explain`); out of scope here.

author: tom-bot-for-rana[bot]
body:
## Problem

On the Snap dashboard, PR diff runs show an **empty baseline** ("No image") and an empty diff, with a misleading `diffed / 0% / 0 pixels` badge — even though valid accepted baselines exist for the project.

### Root cause (verified against the Snap backend source)

`SnapProvider.capture()` submitted runs with only `id`, `baseUrl`, `captureProfileJson`, and `trigger`. But the Snap backend resolves each capture's baseline **solely from `run.baselineId`** (`visual-routes.ts` — `baseline = run.baselineId ? getById(...) : null`, then `findBaselineObjectKey(...)`). There is **no branch-based fallback**.

With no `baselineId` on the run:
- captures get **no `baselineObjectKey`**
- the render worker short-circuits to `status: "diffed"` with `NO_BASELINE_THRESHOLD` and no pixel comparison (`render-worker.ts:153`)
- the dashboard renders "No image" for baseline + diff and defaults the null metrics to `0% / 0 pixels`

Confirmed live for project `prj_bb9727…`: the run's resolved baseline was `{}` and every capture had `currentObjectKey` but no `baselineObjectKey` / `diffObjectKey` / `diffPct`, despite two accepted `main` baselines existing.

## Fix

1. **Resolve + attach the baseline.** `capture()` now calls `GET /v1/visual/projects/:id/baselines/latest` and includes the resolved `baselineId` (and the git `branch` from `GITHUB_HEAD_REF`/`GITHUB_REF_NAME`) in the run-creation payload. A genuine first run (404, no baseline) still proceeds with no `baselineId`.
2. **Stop masking missing baselines.** `#mapRunToSummary` now counts a capture with no `baselineObjectKey` as `missingInBaseline` (→ drift status `incomplete`) instead of silently treating it as a match, which previously made an empty-baseline run read as a clean PR.

## Tests

- run-creation attaches `baselineId` + `branch`
- first run (404) omits `baselineId`
- a no-baseline capture maps to `missingInBaseline` / `incomplete` rather than matched

Full suite green (441 tests).

## Related

The Snap backend also has a correctness bug — it marks no-baseline captures as `"diffed"` (which aggregates to `pass`) instead of a distinct "new"/"no baseline" status. Filed separately on `i2Dev-com/snap`.

body:
## Summary

Complete **n8n workflow** (12 nodes) that automatically generates a narrative weekly development summary for any GitHub repository using the **Claude API**, with dual delivery via **email + Slack/Discord webhook**.

## Deliverables

### `workflows/n8n-weekly-dev-summary/workflow.json`
- **Schedule Trigger**: Weekly cron (Friday 5pm, configurable)
- **3 parallel GitHub API calls**: Fetch commits, closed issues, merged PRs
- **Code node**: Computes week date range (Mon→Sun) from environment variables
- **Merge node**: Combines all GitHub data into a single prompt payload
- **Claude API call**: POST to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with model `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`
- **Response parser**: Extracts text content from Claude's structured response
- **Dual output**:
  - Email (SMTP, HTML formatted)
  - Slack/Discord (incoming webhook, JSON payload)

### `workflows/n8n-weekly-dev-summary/README.md`
- 3-step setup guide (import → configure variables → activate)
- Architecture diagram (ASCII flow chart)
- Environment variable reference table
- Customization guide (schedule, model, delivery channels)
- Troubleshooting table

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Exportable n8n workflow (`.json` file) — import directly into n8n
- [x] Weekly cron trigger (Friday at 5pm, configurable via cron expression)
- [x] Fetches from GitHub API: commits, closed issues, merged PRs for the week
- [x] Calls Claude API (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`) for narrative summary
- [x] Dual delivery: email + Slack/Discord webhook
- [x] Configurable variables: GitHub repo, destination channel, language (EN/FR)

## Design Decisions

- **Zero npm dependencies** — uses only n8n built-in nodes (HTTP Request, Code, Schedule Trigger, Email Send)
- **Security** — all secrets via n8n environment variables or credentials, never hardcoded
- **Graceful degradation** — Slack/Discord and Email nodes have `continueOnFail: true` so one failing channel does not block the other
- **Flexible date range** — Code node computes ISO week dates dynamically; no hardcoding

Closes #2289

body:
## Summary

Adds affiliate buy-boxes to all 36 brand pages on petfoods-com (catalog) plus the 3 long-form review variants. This is **D-006 in the monetization decisions log**.

## Why

petfoods-com already has 36 programmatically-generated brand pages with deep editorial content (parent company, AAFCO compliance, transparency scoring, recall history). What it was missing: any way for reader purchase intent to convert. Brand pages are high commercial intent — readers landing on `/brands/acana` are typically researching for purchase. The buy-box gives them an exit ramp that earns affiliate revenue.

## Approach

Search-URL pattern (not specific product SKUs):
- `chewy-brand` route: `chewy.com/s?query={brand-name}`
- `amazon-brand` route: `amazon.com/s?k={brand-name}`

Reader picks the specific product on the retailer; we earn the affiliate commission on whatever they buy. **Editorially honest** — we're not endorsing a specific SKU, we're surfacing the brand on the retailer. **Mechanically simple** — no per-brand SKU research needed; brand name is already in the data file.

## Placement

Right after the TL;DR / Overview sections (high on the page, where commercial intent is highest). Includes explicit affiliate-commission disclosure inline plus the existing `<DisclosureBanner />` above.

## Framework fields (from decisions log)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Revenue Potential** | $1K–$4K MRR at maturity |
| **Traffic Requirements** | 150K monthly visitors (petfoods-com is programmatic — brand-name SEO works) |
| **Ease of Implementation** | ~30 min (mechanical, no new data research) |
| **Time to Revenue** | Within 60 days of launch (faster than D-001 — pages already rank-able) |
| **Priority Level** | P1 |

## Scales without humans

Adding new brands to `brands.ts` automatically gets a buy-box. The search-URL pattern means we don't maintain per-product SKU mappings as products churn.

## Test plan

- [ ] Vercel preview build succeeds on petfoods-com
- [ ] Sample render check: `/brands/acana` shows buy-box right after TL;DR
- [ ] Sample render check: `/brands/blue-buffalo` (long-form review variant) shows buy-box after Overview
- [ ] Buttons link to `/go/chewy-brand/Acana?s=brand-acana` (correctly URL-encoded)

## Summary

Closes #94. JACO's compose subset silently ignored the `logging:` block. This change projects both the modern `logging:` section (driver + options such as `tag`, `max-size`, `max-file`) and the legacy top-level `log_driver`/`log_opt` keys onto the container's `HostConfig.LogConfig`.

## Changes

- **`internal/runtime/compose/types.go`** — `ContainerSpec` gains a `LogConfig *LogConfig` field (nil = unset); new `LogConfig` type (Driver + Options).
- **`internal/runtime/compose/spec.go`** — `logConfigFromCompose` resolves the source: the modern `logging:` block wins outright when present (NOT a field-by-field merge, mirroring `resolveResources`), otherwise falls back to legacy `log_driver`/`log_opt`. Returns nil for empty input, per the existing helper convention.
- **`internal/runtime/lifecycle/config.go`** — `buildConfig` sets `HostConfig.LogConfig` via `toDockerLogConfig`, mapping `Driver`→`Type` and `Options`→`Config`. body:
## TLDR
Fixes the new-module import false positive (#53) with live workspace re-resolution, stops ANSI escape garbage in piped CLI/LSP logs, simplifies Shipwright binary resolution to user-setting + bundled, and adds a benchmark fixture suite plus a website benchmark section — alongside a docs/site refresh.

## What Was Added?
- **`crates/basilisk-lsp/tests/lsp/ws_test_cross_module.rs`** (new, 10 e2e tests) covering cross-module analysis under `[ANALYSIS-CROSSLSP]`, including two regressions for #53: `new_file_resolves_first_party_sibling_import` and `created_module_clears_unresolved_import_in_dependents`.
- **`WorkspaceIndex::forget_file`** plus **`recheck_all_files` / `reresolve_imports_and_recheck`** in `workspace.rs` (`[ANALYSIS-INCR-IMPORTS]`) — drop deleted entries and re-check every indexed file against current resolution.
- **Tracing ANSI regression test** `tracing_logs_emit_no_ansi_on_piped_stderr` in `crates/basilisk-cli/tests/cli_binary_tests.rs`.
- **Benchmark fixtures**: `benchmarks/fixtures/e0010_unresolved_import.py`, `e0012_argument_type_mismatch.py`, `e0014_assignment_incompatibility.py` (2k-line stress fixtures), reworked `benchmarks/run.sh`, and `benchmarks/status/darwin-arm64-apple-m4-max.csv`.
- **Website benchmark section**: `website/src/_data/benchmarks.js` + `website/src/_includes/benchmark-section.njk` rendering benchmark results on the site.
- **`scripts/gen_rules_reference.py`** — generates the rules reference docs.
- **`docs/plans/ROADMAP-NEXT-STEPS-PLAN.md`** (new plan).

## What Was Changed or Deleted?
- **#53 fix — `crates/basilisk-lsp/src/server/document.rs`**: the file-watcher now distinguishes `CREATED` from `CHANGED`. A newly-created module re-resolves the whole workspace and re-publishes so dependents' stale `BSK-E0010 "cannot resolve import"` clears without an LSP reload; a pure content change keeps the cheaper per-file reload. Deleted files are forgotten first so a recheck cannot resurrect their diagnostics. `[ANALYSIS-INCR-IMPORTS]`.
- **CLI logs — `crates/basilisk-cli/src/main.rs`**: gate ANSI colour on `std::io::IsTerminal::is_terminal(stderr)`, so the LSP subprocess (piped stderr) emits clean text instead of raw escape sequences in the editor output channel.
- **Shipwright — `shipwright.json`**: binary resolution sources narrowed to `["user-setting", "bundled"]` (env / pkgmgr / cargo-bin / path / lsp-initialize removed). The VSIX ships and resolves its bundled binary by default; a user override is still honoured.
- **VS Code test helpers — `debug-integration.test.ts`, `test-helpers.ts`**: drop ad-hoc PATH/platform binary discovery in favour of the Shipwright-staged bundled binary.
- **Docs/site refresh**: `Claude.md` → `CLAUDE.md`, expanded `CHECKER-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md`, `LSP-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md`, `VSIX-SPEC.md`, `README.md`, and a large en/zh website docs overhaul (comparison, configuration, rules/*, removed standalone mojo-safety rule pages).
- **Build/CI**: `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/{ci,release,deploy-pages}.yml`, `.gitignore`, `coverage-thresholds.json` (metadata), `.claude/skills/*` metadata, removed the `tmc` skill.

## How Do The Automated Tests Prove It Works?
- **#53**: `new_file_resolves_first_party_sibling_import` creates a new module *after* the workspace scan and asserts its first-party sibling import resolves like a pre-existing file; `created_module_clears_unresolved_import_in_dependents` asserts a dependent's `BSK-E0010` is re-published as cleared once the module appears — both pass under `./scripts/test-rust.sh`.
- **Logs**: `tracing_logs_emit_no_ansi_on_piped_stderr` runs `basilisk check` with `BASILISK_LOG=info` over captured (piped) stderr and asserts zero ANSI escapes.
- **Shipwright/VSIX**: VS Code E2E "Shipwright resolves basilisk from the bundled VSIX binary by default" plus the full 301-test suite pass (85% ≥ 84% coverage); `verify-shipwright.mjs manifest` and `versions` both pass.
- **Full local gate run** (mirrors CI): Rust coverage thresholds met on all 10 crates; Zed (96 tests), Neovim (39% ≥ 30%), and mutation `working` baseline (90.54%, no regression) all green.

## Spec / Doc Changes
- `[ANALYSIS-INCR-IMPORTS]` / `[ANALYSIS-CROSSLSP]` documented in the LSP/checker specs; `CHECKER-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md` and `LSP-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md` updated; `Claude.md` renamed to `CLAUDE.md`; new `ROADMAP-NEXT-STEPS-PLAN.md`.

## Breaking Changes
- Shipwright binary resolution now considers only `user-setting` and `bundled` sources (previously also env / package managers / `cargo-bin` / PATH / LSP-initialize). Environments that relied on PATH or `BASILISK_EXECUTABLE_PATH` discovery should set the user setting or use the bundled binary.

Fixes #53

body:
Fixes #1241, fixes #1242

Two small follow-ups from #1237 (Source-parser unification), both editing `Source.from_api_response` in `src/notebooklm/_types/sources.py`.

## #1242 — forward `method_id` to `SourceRow.from_unknown_shape`

`Source.from_api_response` called `SourceRow.from_unknown_shape(data)` without a `method_id`, so the row defaulted to `GET_NOTEBOOK`. Any `safe_index` drift log emitted for a row built via the ADD_SOURCE / rename path was therefore mis-tagged as `GET_NOTEBOOK` instead of the actual method.

- Added an **optional keyword-only** `method_id` parameter to `from_api_response` and threaded it through to `from_unknown_shape`. Additive → non-breaking. Default `None` preserves the historical `GET_NOTEBOOK` fallback for callers that do not pass it.
- Updated the internal non-`GET_NOTEBOOK` callers to pass the real method id:
  - `_source_add.py` `add_url` / `add_text` / `add_drive` → `RPCMethod.ADD_SOURCE.value`
  - `_sources.py` `rename` and `_source_upload.py` `rename` → `RPCMethod.UPDATE_SOURCE.value`

## #1241 — unused `notebook_id` parameter

Resolved by **keeping** the parameter. `Source.from_api_response` is tracked public surface (`Source` is exported from the top-level `notebooklm` package), and `scripts/audit_public_api_compat.py` flags removing `notebook_id` as a `changed-signature` break (verified empirically). The parameter is now documented as accepted for call-site symmetry / forward-compat but currently unused — no unapproved public-API break introduced.

Added to `tests/unit/test_types.py::TestSource`:

- A forced `safe_index` drift on an ADD_SOURCE-built row surfaces an `UnknownRPCMethodError` tagged with `ADD_SOURCE` (not the `GET_NOTEBOOK` default).

author: paulsnow
body:
Four visitors were emitting operator names that have no runtime registration. Conditions that hit them would surface as `operator not found` at evaluation time.

## The four offenders

| Visitor | DSL | Pre-fix | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VisitBoolStrNeq` | `<a> != <b>` | `strneq` | `s== not` |
| `VisitBoolStrIsNot` | `<a> is not <b>` | `strneq not`¹ | `s== not` |
| `VisitBoolStrEqIc` | `<a> is equal to ignore case <b>` | `sic==` | `s==i` |
| `VisitBoolStrNeqIc` | `<a> is not equal to ignore case <b>` | `sic== not` | `s==i not` |

¹ Doubly broken: `strneq` is unregistered, and even if it weren't, the trailing `not` would re-invert the result.

## Runtime registrations

`pkg/dtrules/operators/string.go`:
```go
Register("s==", opStringEqual)
Alias("s==", "streq")
Register("s==i", opStringEqualIgnoreCase)
Alias("s==i", "streqignorecase")
```

`strneq` and `sic==` were never registered. Bytes comparisons (`bytes==` / `bytes!=`) were already correct — that path is untouched.

## Test

`pkg/dtrules/compiler/el/issue_835_string_compare_ops_test.go` pins each of the four visitors against operator-name regressions. Includes a token-by-token `assertOpsRegistered` helper that walks the emitted postfix and checks every non-literal, non-block, non-dictionary token resolves via `operators.GetByString` — cheap end-to-end coverage that catches any new visitor emitting a typo'd op name.

## Why this wasn't caught earlier

The pin-test only verifies the visitor is overridden, not that the emitted ops resolve. String inequality / case-insensitive comparison evidently doesn't appear in any test that actually evaluates the postfix — only postfix-shape assertions exercised these paths.

`make check` passes.

Closes #835.

body:
Lets you manage watched channels by DMing the bot, with no public chatter.

## What changed
- **`!log` works in DMs.** Removed `guild_only` from the group. Channels are resolved from a `#mention`, a raw **channel ID**, or (in a server) a name — and validated to belong to the POPG guild. In a DM you pass the numeric ID (Developer Mode → Copy Channel ID).
- **Admin check works in DMs.** Authorization now resolves the author's membership in the configured guild and checks their Administrator permission there, so admins can use it from DMs.
- **Silent — no warnings in chat.** All `!log` replies are routed to the author's DM via a `_reply()` helper. Channel management never posts in a public channel. (If a command is run in a server *and* the user's DMs are closed, it falls back to the channel so they still get feedback.)
- Updated `!help` admin text and added a note that logging can be managed via DM.

## Usage
```
DM the bot:  !log watch 123456789012345678
             !log list
             !log unwatch 123456789012345678
```

Note: message *logging itself* was already silent (nothing is posted to watched channels); this PR makes the *management commands* private too.

author: joelteply
body:
The machine-singular daemon socket was placed under an env-derived
directory: `$AIRC_RUNTIME_DIR` → `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/airc` → `$TMPDIR/airc`
→ `~/.airc/runtime` (card 7e88c34d). `$TMPDIR` is per-SESSION on macOS
and is freely overridden (the Claude Code harness sets
`TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-<id>`; terminals carry `/var/folders/.../T`; a
daemon spawned with no `$TMPDIR` landed in `~/.airc/runtime`). So the
same binary, with the same machine-hash in the socket NAME, resolved a
DIFFERENT directory per process — and each started its own daemon.
Observed: 4 live daemons + 18 client connections fragmented across them
(+ 888 leaked test daemons). The hash made the socket name
machine-stable; the env-derived directory un-did it.

Fix: the runtime dir is ALWAYS `~/.airc/runtime` — where every other
airc artifact already lives (wires, worktrees, identity/trust). No
per-session env in the path. `$AIRC_RUNTIME_DIR` remains as the one
explicit override, whose only real consumer is the integration suite
isolating ephemeral test daemons. `$TMPDIR`/`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` are no
longer consulted.

- runtime_dir(): delegates to a pure `resolve_runtime_dir(override, home)`
  so the machine-stable invariant is testable without mutating
  process-global env, and the signature itself proves no per-session
  var can influence the path. 3 new pure tests + stale cli.rs docs fixed.

Once installed, all scopes/tabs resolve the same socket and converge on
one daemon by construction — no AIRC_RUNTIME_DIR dance, no rejoin needed
after `airc update`.

body:
Reviewed the QA backlog (#47–#60), verified each against the code, and resolved the genuine issues. Three product-behaviour calls were confirmed with the maintainer before changing observable semantics (body column widening, defer-prune-and-document for orphans, and adding both opt-in guards).

## Code fixes (with regression tests)

**Storage / data integrity**
- **#47 (High)** — `body` column widened to `mediumText`; a 20k-char multibyte body (80k bytes) now persists losslessly on MySQL/MariaDB instead of truncating/erroring.
- **#52 (Med)** — over-length original filenames are truncated (extension preserved) to fit the `string`/255 `name` column.
- **#55 (Low)** — zero-byte uploads are rejected by default (`messenger.attachments.allow_empty`).
- **#53 (Low)** — query `limit` is normalised by `Support\Limit`: null = no limit, anything else clamped to ≥ 1, so a negative/zero limit can no longer return the entire unbounded result set.

**Unread coherence**
- **#50 (Med) / #56 (Low)** — `markAsUnread` is a no-op when the participant has no visible received message (sender-only or cleared history); otherwise marks a single message. The badge can never contradict the visible timeline.
- **#60 (Low)** — `markAsRead`/`clear` reset `unread_count` under a row lock (`applyLockedReset`), serialising against the atomic inbound increment so a concurrent message isn't silently marked read.

**Hardening**
- **#58 (Low)** — `ConversationKey` uses length-prefixed segment encoding (`len:type#len:id`), collision-proof against morph aliases/keys containing `#` or `|`.

## New opt-in guards (off by default, preserve current behaviour)

- **#54** — `messenger.validation.verify_participants_exist`: new `EnsureParticipantsExist` pipe rejects a send to a non-existent sender/recipient (DB existence check, also catches deleted rows).
- **#57** — `messenger.reports.participants_only`: restricts reporting to conversation participants.

## Documentation (genuine but by-design / deferred)

- **#59** — reply-target validity/visibility documented next to the README `reply_to` example.
- **#48 / #49 (High/Med)** — no cascading deletes (morphable design): documented host-owned participant cleanup, nullable `morphTo` accessors, and that a `messenger:prune` command is planned. *(Deferred prune tooling to a feature PR per maintainer decision.)*
- **#51 (Med)** — attachment metadata-validation limitation made explicit (already partially documented); recommend a custom content-inspection pipe for untrusted input.

## Quality gates

- ✅ Pest: 193 passing (393 assertions)
- ✅ Pint: clean
- ✅ PHPStan level 5 + Larastan: 0 errors
- ✅ `composer validate`: passes

Fixes #47, #50, #52, #53, #54, #55, #56, #57, #58, #60

author: aetherlogosprime-architect
body:
## What

Hardens the briefing-id staleness gate (the context-recall freshness token).

1. **Recall window 25 -> 10 tool-uses.** At 25, a compaction landing mid-window went unchallenged for up to 24 tool-uses. Lived exactly that this session: compacted, then ran a dozen tool-uses narrating "everything's confirmed safe and real" before anything asked. At 10 the worst-case blind stretch is 9.

2. **Unfakeable gate-side truth.** Stores a SHA-256 **hash** of the ID, never the raw value, and the ID is 128-bit (`token_hex(16)`) so the hash is not brute-forceable. Catting the truth file yields nothing presentable. The only way to present the right ID is to actually still hold it in context — the liveness proof working as intended.

## Honest limit (documented in-code)

The raw ID still reaches context by being printed (-> on-disk transcript, which survives compaction), so one peek-path remains. What hashing achieves: every cheat path now costs MORE than just reloading, so the lazy route and the honest route are the same route.

## Verified live

The hardened gate stale-blocked me on the old-format truth file, forced an honest reload, correct ID verified, wrong ID rejected, truth file confirmed hash-only. Tests: raw-ID-never-persisted contract + high-entropy-token guards added; 23 passed.

## For the auditor

- `briefing_id.py` is NOT on the guardrail list though it holds the actual recall-challenge logic (`briefing_freshness.py`, which only delegates here, IS guardrailed). That guardrail gap is worth closing — flagging for the audit to weigh.
- The original design's pre-registration record (e536aaec6144) is missing from the store; the falsification experiment was never run.

Diff: 2 files (src/divineos/core/briefing_id.py + tests/test_briefing_id.py).

author: yasmro
body:
## Summary

`<Button asChild variant="link">` threw at render time:
`React.Children.only expected to receive a single React element child`.

**Root cause:** the `variant === 'link'` branch in [`Button.tsx`](src/components/lv1/Button/Button.tsx) renders `{iconStart}{children}{iconEnd}` — three children even when the icon conditionals are falsy. With `asChild`, `Comp` is Radix `Slot`, which requires exactly one child, so `React.Children.only` throws. The non-link `asChild` branch renders only `{children}`, so `<Button asChild>` / `<Button asChild variant="secondary">` already worked.

**Fix:** resolve the `asChild` path **before** the `link` branch, so every `asChild` case (including `variant="link"`) hands `Slot` a single child. Pure control-flow reorder — output is identical for every previously-working path; only the previously-crashing asChild+link case changes (now renders the child anchor with the `st-btn st-btn--link` chain). As with the other asChild paths, `icon` / `isLoading` are not projected onto the child.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test in `Button.test.tsx`: `<Button asChild variant="link"><a/></Button>` renders an `<a>` (link role) with the link class chain and does not throw.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm test --run` — 679 passed
- [x] Reorder is output-identical for existing paths; CI VRT re-confirms no Button baseline drift.

## Context

Discovered while authoring the `Patterns/Composition with asChild` docs page (#141 / #339), which intentionally omitted the link example because of this crash. With this fix, that example could be added back in a follow-up.

body:
## Summary

Closes profile-page audit **#9**.

On a slow network a user can double-tap a contact CTA before navigation kicks in. That fires a second `profile_contact_route_clicked` event and inflates the measured CTA click-rate (the metric we're using to grade every other profile change).

On the first click the CTA now gets a brief `is-loading` state:
- **JS** (`therapist-page.js`): sets `dataset.ctaLoading` + `is-loading` class, short-circuits a repeat click for 600ms, then clears. The first click's navigation is never touched (no `preventDefault`).
- **CSS** (`therapist-page.css`): `[data-profile-contact-route].is-loading` dims the control to 60% and sets `pointer-events: none`, so a second tap can't even register during the window.

Applies to all primary/secondary contact CTAs (the hero button, mobile sticky bar, sidebar primary) since they all carry `data-profile-contact-route`.

- [x] `npm run format:check` — clean

author: opollo5
body:
## Summary

Extends `Decision policy` principle 3 (*system fix over workaround*) with one concrete rule derived from PR #1166 + the DEDUP_OR_PERSIST_AUDIT:

> Tests must not seed data with \`Date.now() + N\` style offsets when the assertion depends on the result landing in a visible/queryable range. Use explicit, deterministic helpers like \`dateInCurrentMonth(15)\` instead.

## Why

PR #1166 fixed an e2e test (`dashboard.spec.ts (F-1)`) that fired exactly once: 2026-05-30. The mock scheduled a post at \`Date.now() + 2 days\` = 2026-06-01. May 2026 ends Sunday, and the calendar grid's \`buildGrid\` (Monday-first, \`trailing = lastDow < 6 ? 6 - lastDow : 0\`) renders **no** trailing-month overflow cells when the month ends on Sunday. Post had nowhere to render → 10s timeout → red CI on every PR after midnight UTC on 2026-05-30.

Per principle 3, the class-of-bug fix is to document the anti-pattern at the policy level so the next person writing a similar test doesn't recreate it.

## Scope

Single-line addition. No other rules touched. Principle numbering preserved.

## Gate evidence

- File modified: `CLAUDE.md` (1 line added, 1 line removed)
- No code changes; CI is the standard text-only flow

body:
## Summary

- market-worker 33-40% 실패 → 0% (production timeout fix)
- DB only — 코드 변경 없음 (이미 적용됨)
- pg_trgm + GIN trigram partial index → 1,280x speedup (28.9s → 22ms)

## 진단

mvp_collect_runs 실패 query 다 동일 패턴:
\`comparable_key LIKE 'shoe|<sku>|%|<tier>'\` wildcard 중간 → 기존 btree 못 잡음 → 270K row 풀스캔 → 28.9초 timeout.

## Fix (이미 production 적용)

\`\`\`sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
ALTER TABLE mvp_listing_parsed ALTER COLUMN comparable_key SET STATISTICS 1000;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY mvp_listing_parsed_comparable_trgm_idx
ON mvp_listing_parsed USING gin (comparable_key gin_trgm_ops)
WHERE needs_review = false AND parse_confidence >= 0.65;
ANALYZE mvp_listing_parsed;
\`\`\`

## 함정 노트

partial WHERE 를 \`IS FALSE\` 박으면 query \`= false\` 와 mismatch → planner 활용 못 함. **literal 일치** 박아야 됨.

## Trade-off

- Disk +21 MB
- Insert overhead negligible
- CONCURRENTLY = lock 없음
- Rollback: DROP INDEX 한 줄

- [ ] 다음 1시간 market-worker 실패율 0% 확인 (mvp_collect_runs)
- [ ] idx_scan 증가 확인 (pg_stat_user_indexes)

author: ikari-pl
body:
## What

Implements `go f(x, y)` **argument capture** with Go's snapshot semantics (args evaluated at the spawn site, not when the goroutine starts). Satisfies two redundant roadmap entries — go-statement sub-item **(b)** and ping_pong sub-item **(a)** — as one shared capability. Also fixes a latent bug that meant **no generated goroutine program had ever actually run** (see below).

## Runtime

`Spawn` gains a closure-carrying overload:
```ada
function Spawn (Body_Proc : Goroutine_Body; Closure : System.Address) return Goroutine_Id;
function Closure (G : Goroutine_Id) return System.Address;
```
backed by an opaque `Spawn_Closure` slot on `Goroutine_Record`. The no-arg `Spawn` delegates with `Null_Address`. The slot is deliberately distinct from the panic-promotion `Local_Storage` slot — it's set once at spawn and read once at entry, never mutated.

## Emit

A non-empty arg list selects `emitGoClosureWithArgs`, which generates per call-site (keyed by `goIndex`):
- `Go_Closure_<n>` — record with one component per **callee parameter**, named + typed from the callee's signature (new file-wide `funcByName` map);
- two `Unchecked_Conversion`s + an `Unchecked_Deallocation` bridging it to the opaque `System.Address` payload;
- `Allocate_Closure_<n>` — snapshots the args at the spawn site;
- `Go_Worker_<n>` — reads the closure via `Closure (Current)`, copies each field into a like-named local, **frees the heap block** (no per-spawn leak), then calls the user function.

`checkGoArgsEmpty` is gone. Five emit error-path tests cover the unsupported shapes (unknown callee, builtin callee, non-ident callee, arg/param mismatch, unsupported param type).

## 🐛 Discovery + fix: goroutine binaries linked the wrong libco backend

Verifying arg capture end-to-end surfaced that **the go-statement corpus is text-compared only** — no generated goroutine program had ever been executed. When run, even the already-merged no-arg `go f()` crashes:
```
raised PROGRAM_ERROR : unhandled signal   (EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION in co_swap_function)
```
`gada_core.gpr` picks libco's context-switch backend from `external ("ARCH", "amd64")` — **defaulting to amd64**. The runtime Makefile exports `ARCH` from `uname -m`, but the `gada build` pipeline set nothing, so every arm64 binary linked the **x86-64 `co_swap` blob** and died on the first context switch. Fixed in `build.go` by deriving `runtime.GOARCH` → `-XARCH=amd64|aarch64`. (First commit; independent — it also fixes the merged no-arg lowering.)

## Verify

```
cd compiler && go test ./internal/emit/... -run TestCorpus/go_with_args   # PASS
make -C runtime test PKG=async.scheduler                                  # 19/19, incl. new closure cases
```
End-to-end (manual, after the ARCH fix): a `go seed(a)` / `go relay(a, b)` program transpiles, builds, and runs cleanly.

## Gates
```
PASS runtime/ 100% (706/706) · emit 95.61% · translate 95.81% · compiler 95.00%
coverage gate: PASSED · roadmap consistency: OK
```

author: victorbrazs
body:
## Summary
Two fixes for the same root cause: Zendesk macros forward the Type of Work field's option \`value\` (tag), and real-world payloads still carry slugs (\`deep_cleaning\`, \`fire_alarm_service\`, \`pat_testing\`) rather than the canonical OS name or a UUID. Both surfaced as live 400s after the field's tag rewrite:

1. \`service_type "deep_cleaning" did not match any active Services catalog entry.\`
2. \`catalog_service_id must be a valid UUID when provided.\`

## Fix 1 — slug-aware fallback in the hourly catalog resolver
\`resolveCatalogServiceForHourly\` keeps using \`catalogServiceIdForTypeOfWorkLabel\` first (exact + alias), then falls back to a slug matcher that:
- slugifies both the input and the catalog name (lower, non-alphanumeric → \`_\`),
- compares against the full slug AND the base-name slug (after stripping a \`(XXX)\` prefix and a trailing \`(XXX)\` duplicate),
- uses single-candidate containment between slugs as a last resort.

Covers \`deep_cleaning\` → \`(DC) Deep Cleaning\`, \`after_builders_cleaning\` → \`(AB) After Builders Cleaning\`, \`end_of_tenancy_cleaning\` → \`(EOT) End of Tenancy\`, etc. Zero or multiple matches still return null so unknown input surfaces a clear 400 rather than relinking silently.

## Fix 2 — \`catalog_service_id\` accepts non-UUID values
Tickets in Zendesk that were saved before #401's slug→UUID backfill keep their old slug as the field value (Zendesk doesn't rewrite tags on existing tickets when an option's \`value\` changes). When the macro forwards that slug as \`catalog_service_id\`, the API used to 400.

Now: if \`catalog_service_id\` isn't a UUID, the value is moved to \`service_type\` (when empty) and \`catalog_service_id\` is cleared. The slug matcher then resolves it. Effectively \`catalog_service_id\` becomes "use this UUID if you have one; otherwise treat it as a service label."

## Test plan
- [ ] POST with \`"service_type": "deep_cleaning"\` and \`rate_type: hourly\` → catalog resolves to \`(DC) Deep Cleaning\`, job created.
- [ ] POST with \`"catalog_service_id": "deep_cleaning"\` (slug, not UUID) and no \`service_type\` → same outcome, no 400.
- [ ] POST with \`"catalog_service_id": "<valid UUID>"\` → UUID path unchanged.
- [ ] POST with \`"service_type": "Plumber"\` → exact name path unchanged.
- [ ] POST with \`"service_type": "actually_unknown"\` → friendly 400 with the canonical-names hint.

author: psaab
body:
## Summary

The userspace HA smoke (`scripts/userspace-phase-cycle.sh` →
`scripts/userspace-ha-validation.sh`) false-failed a healthy IPv6
dataplane when the **external public IPv6 traceroute final hop** did not
answer the ICMPv6 probe. #1301 made the final hop non-fatal but
over-corrected: the IPv6 mtr check then only asserted the **first** hop
(the firewall's own LAN gateway) resolved — L3-local liveness, not
forwarding. A genuinely-broken IPv6 dataplane could still pass as a
warning.

This makes the IPv6 forwarding signal robust and under our control,
without weakening the smoke into a no-op:

- **Public IPv6 mtr → observability-only.** Any unresolved/silent
  later or final hop is a recorded warning, never a hard fail (external
  endpoint + intermediate ICMPv6 rate-limiting are outside our
  control). An unresolved **first** hop still fails.
- **IPv6 forwarding is gated by controlled signals that already exist:**
  the LAN→WAN-target ping (the LAN host reaches the WAN-side target only
  by transiting the userspace dataplane), the IPv6 TTL=1 probe, and the
  IPv6 iperf3 leg. The ping is now an explicit `validate_reachability`
  assertion (fails on `0 received`), not just `ping`'s exit code, and
  `assert_forwarding_route` guards against the target drifting on-box.
- **Classifier extracted** to `scripts/mtr_report_check.py` (unit
  testable). The IPv4 leg keeps its final-hop hard gate (1.1.1.1 is a
  reliable responder) but parses loss **numerically** by anchoring on
  the `%` token, so `(waiting for reply)`, column-truncated `100.0`
  (no `%`), integer `100%`, or an unparseable loss column fail closed.
- Pings/mtr captured with `LC_ALL=C` + `2>&1 || true` so a 100%-loss
  ping or non-zero mtr exit can't crash the validator under `set -e`
  before the classifier/assertion runs.

## Why this still catches a real IPv6 break

| Failure mode | Caught by |
|---|---|
| IPv6 dataplane forwards nothing (ICMP) | `validate_reachability` — HARD FAIL |
| Forwards ICMP but not TCP | existing IPv6 `iperf3` to `::200` — HARD FAIL |
| Hop-decrement / firewall ICMPv6 path broken | `validate_ttl_probe ipv6` — HARD FAIL |
| Target drifted on-box (no transit) | `assert_forwarding_route` — HARD FAIL |
| External public final hop silent | IPv6 mtr: WARNING (correct) |
| Healthy path, all upstream ICMPv6 rate-limited | IPv6 mtr: WARNING (no longer false-fails) |
| IPv4 final hop dead / `(waiting for reply)` / `100%` | IPv4 mtr: HARD FAIL (numeric loss, fail-closed) |

## Plan + adversarial review

Plan doc: `docs/pr/1303-mtr-smoke/plan.md`

- v1 **PLAN-KILLED** (Codex + AGY): the v1 "≥1 resolved hop beyond the
  first" predicate re-introduced a false-fail on ICMPv6-rate-limited
  paths.
- v2 **PLAN-NEEDS-MAJOR** (both endorsed the architecture): classifier
  regex (`(waiting for reply)`), `set -e` crash-before-downgrade, scope,
  locale.
- v3 **PLAN-READY** (Codex `task-mpru1jxi-2lvvap`, AGY
  `adversarial-review-mpru1nhk-15b7f2`) — all findings applied.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/test_mtr_report_check.py` — 22 tests incl. the #1303
  repro (silent external final hop → warning) and every reviewer
  false-pass case; 5/5 flake-clean
- [x] `shellcheck scripts/userspace-ha-validation.sh` clean
- [x] `bash -n` parse clean
- [x] existing `scripts/userspace_ha_validation_matrix_test.py` passes
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` both Python files
- [ ] cluster smoke on the loss userspace cluster — run by the parent
  (this is a smoke-script change; running the smoke is the real
  validation)

Closes #1303

author: beardedeagle
body:
## Summary

Adds checked local component composition admission across Strata and Mantle. This connects source-unit reachability with typed protocol, port, and component boundary declarations by admitting component instances and imported-port bindings before runtime execution.

## Strata Semantics

- Adds local composition syntax for component instances and imported-port bindings.
- Extends component declarations with explicit imported ports.
- Carries composition facts through AST, source-program merge, checked IR, and lowering.
- Assigns typed component-instance IDs and port-binding IDs during checking.
- Rejects duplicate composition declarations, duplicate component instances, duplicate imported-port bindings, unbound component imports, unknown binding instances, invalid imported/exported port edges, protocol mismatches, direct-import ambiguity, and transitive-only source-unit access.
- Preserves process-local port authority: composition binding does not grant `PortConnect` authority to a process.

## Mantle Artifact And Runtime Boundary

- Bumps the Mantle artifact schema to version 5 for component import and composition metadata.
- Encodes component imports, component instances, and port bindings as typed artifact tables.
- Bounds composition, component-instance, and port-binding counts before allocation during decode.
- Validates composition metadata during artifact admission: instance component IDs, imported/exported port membership, protocol compatibility, duplicate binding rejection, and complete import satisfaction.
- Keeps runtime dispatch on loaded typed process, message, and port IDs. Component names, import names, and source strings remain diagnostics/metadata only.

## Documentation And Examples

- Adds `examples/component_composition_main.str` and `examples/component_composition_worker.str`.
- Documents the current composition source form and its implementation limits.
- Updates language reference, syntax reference, boundary contracts, file types, artifact/runtime boundary, source-to-runtime gates, diagnostics, examples, development gates, and language-surface assurance docs.

## Coverage

- Adds parser, checker, checked-IR/lowering, artifact admission, decode-failure, runtime boundary, acceptance, property-style deterministic lowering, performance smoke, fuzz seed, and assurance coverage.
- Adds negative tests for unsatisfied imports, protocol mismatch, authority widening, duplicate instance IDs, duplicate binding edges, ambiguous direct import, transitive-only access, malformed composition fields, and oversized composition tables.
- Adds fuzz seeds for parse/check/lower, source-program check/lower, Mantle artifact decode, malformed composition artifact decode, and runtime-from-source paths.

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`

author: uvaishnav
body:
## What
Completely redesigned the AI description generation system for both billing modes.

## Problems Fixed
- Client name was being sent and sometimes appearing in the description (it's already on the invoice header)
- Rates, quantities, and amounts were being included — they're already in the bill table
- SAC code/nickname was appearing verbatim in generated descriptions
- Single generic system prompt produced inconsistent results across quantity and rental modes
- 300 character UI limit didn't match actual prompt instructions (80–150 words)
- `maxOutputTokens: 600` could cause cutoffs on refinement responses
- `temperature: 0.5` too high for a legal document field

## Changes

### `generateInvoiceDescription.ts` (frontend payload builder)
- Removed `client_name` from `DescriptionContext` and payload entirely
- Removed `rate`, `qty`, `unit` from quantity line items — now sends `work_item_descriptions[]` (descriptions only)
- Removed `monthly_rent`, `subtotal` from rental items — now sends only `reg_number`, `vehicle_type`, `billing_mode`, `num_days`
- `sac_description` kept but clearly marked as internal context
- Quantity vehicles: only vehicles with `include_in_description = true` are sent

### `Section3Description.tsx` (UI)
- Removed `client_name` state and `getClients()` call (no longer needed)
- `handleGenerate()` no longer guards on `clientName`
- Character limit updated from 300 → **350**
- Char counter turns warning color + message says "ask AI to trim" instead of just "consider shortening"
- Refinement placeholder updated: `"Remove vehicle names / Shorten it"` (reflects real use cases)
- Tip text added under refinement input about the 350 char limit

### `supabase/functions/generate-invoice-description/index.ts` (edge function)
- **Three separate system prompts**: `SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION_QUANTITY`, `SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION_RENTAL`, `SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION_REFINE`
- Each system prompt explicitly states the 350-character hard limit
- Quantity prompt: vehicles listed as `"must be mentioned"` — always included if provided
- Rental prompt: mentions partial days naturally in prose
- Refine prompt: honours user instruction (e.g. "remove vehicles") — no forced inclusion
- `buildGeneratePrompt()` and `buildRefinementPrompt()` rebuilt cleanly — no money fields
- SAC description labelled `"internal context only — do NOT mention this in output"`
- `maxOutputTokens`: 600 → **800** (prevents cutoffs)
- `temperature`: 0.5 → **0.3** (more consistent for legal documents)
- `formatDate()` fixed to use UTC parsing (avoids IST timezone shift on date-only strings)
- Both Gemini and Groq calls now receive the correct system instruction per mode

## Design Decision
`2026-05-30` For AI description generation — chose lean inputs (no client, no money) + separate system prompts per billing type over a single generic prompt, because the two billing modes have fundamentally different description structures and the old approach was leaking financial data into the description field.

## Testing
**Quantity mode:**
1. Create invoice, add line items, add vehicles (mark "include in description")
2. Go to Section 3 — auto-generate should fire
3. Description should mention work items and vehicles, NOT the client name, NOT any amounts
4. Should be under 350 characters
5. Refinement: type "remove the vehicles" — vehicles should disappear from the rewritten text

**Rental mode:**
1. Create rental invoice, add vehicles in Section 2
2. Go to Section 3 — auto-generate should fire
3. Description should mention vehicles, work order subject context, period — NOT client name, NOT amounts
4. Should be under 350 characters

**Both modes:**
- SAC code or nickname should never appear in the generated text

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Invoice descriptions limited to 350 characters with updated textarea styling, live character counter, and warning/border when exceeded.
  * AI auto-generation triggers sooner based on billing mode and available items; generated descriptions avoid including client name and reduce explicit vehicle details.
  * Refinement placeholder and tip now reference the 350-character limit; UI text clarifies vehicle optionality.

* **Documentation**
  * Changelog and progress notes added documenting the invoice description and PDF logo rendering polish.

body:
### 🛡️ Sentinel: [security improvement]

🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** Missing Content Security Policy (CSP) headers in the application's main entrypoint. While no obvious XSS vulnerabilities were present, lacking a CSP exposes the application to potential future vulnerabilities introduced by dependencies or new UI components.
🎯 **Impact:** If an XSS vulnerability were to be introduced, attackers could load external malicious scripts, execute arbitrary code within the context of the user's browser, and potentially exfiltrate sensitive data.
🔧 **Fix:** Added a Content Security Policy (CSP) `<meta>` tag directly to `index.html`. This enforces a restrictive baseline (e.g. `default-src 'self'`) while allowing necessary overrides for a Vite/React application (`unsafe-inline` for styles and scripts, `connect-src` allowing websockets for HMR and open https for API requests, and specific font origins).
✅ **Verification:** Verify that `pnpm run build` still successfully completes and that no features or external APIs break when running the dev server.

A Sentinel journal entry was added to `.jules/sentinel.md` documenting the addition of this baseline defense-in-depth measure.

author: daniel-dmwaste
body:
Part of **Verco v2 — UAT Launch Readiness** / VER-187.

## Why this is a design doc, not the harness
VER-187's four flows (MUD admin-on-behalf, admin edit/cancel-with-refund, resident NCN dispute, field-role PII gates) are **all server-rendered + auth-gated**. The current harness mocks the *browser* (`page.route`) against a remote Supabase and the app is **OTP-only** — so these flows can't be driven, and the existing admin/NCN specs literally `test.skip()` when the server returns no seeded data (`ncn-detail.spec.ts:166-170,182-184`). Writing more specs in that harness = skip-guarded no-ops (fake green).

The real unblocker is an **authenticated, seeded** harness — and that needs Docker (`supabase start`) + live iteration on the session-injection. **This environment has no Docker**, so building it blind would ship untested infra. The honest, high-value step is the **blueprint**, which is correct + reviewable + near-executable.

## What's in the design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-30-authenticated-e2e-harness.md`)
- **`supabase start` in CI** (runners have Docker → isolated + seeded local stack, no prod pollution / cost).
- **Session minting past OTP** — GoTrue admin `generateLink` → `verifyOtp` → Playwright `storageState` per role (concrete `auth.setup.ts` scaffold included). The one must-verify-on-a-running-stack detail (the `@supabase/ssr` cookie format) is called out.
- **Seed fixtures** (paid booking, NCN, MUD property, `user_roles` per role), **playwright.config** projects, **`e2e-auth` CI job** (base==main), and the **migration plan** for the skip-guards + VER-187's 4 flows.
- Effort/sequencing: ~½ day to first-role-login (do first, riskiest), then a flow at a time.

## Status
Doc-only PR (CI stays green). Implementation is a clean pick-up on a Docker host (your Mac mini or a CI spike) following §4/§9. For **UAT (tomorrow)** these flows stay manually tested, per VER-187's own severity note.
