author: alexpmichelet
body:
@
Closes #152

## Summary

B-MENU-PUBLICATION slice 1 of the menu publication chantier (epic #132, ADR 0015).

Introduces the **[[Instantané publié]]** table `publishedMenus` (one doc per tenant) and the three sanctioned seam helpers in `lib/tenancy/menuStore.ts` — `getPublishedMenu` / `writePublishedMenu` / `deletePublishedMenu` — that the next slices (publish mutation, public read pivot, lifecycle cleanup) will consume. No Convex function is registered in this slice; the table + the store seam only.

## Decisions

- **One doc per tenant** (uniqueness is a structural invariant of `writePublishedMenu`: it deletes any existing row before inserting the new one in the same Convex tx). Keeps `getPublicMenu` read O(1) and lets a republish be atomic in a single tx.
- **Snapshot does NOT carry `available`** (ADR 0015 pivot — « la rupture ne doit pas exiger une republication globale »). Pinned at the schema level + a type-level assertion in `menuStore.test.ts`.
- **Photos stored as `photoStorageId`** (not resolved URLs) so the snapshot stays immutable; the read pivot resolves URLs via `ctx.storage.getUrl` at PWA read time.
- **Tenant-scoped via the `by_tenant` index**, reached ONLY through the sanctioned `lib/tenancy/menuStore` seam (ADR 0010 + `no-untenanted-query` lint).

## How tested

`packages/backend/convex/lib/tenancy/menuStore.test.ts` — 9 tests covering: never-published returns null, write then read returns the payload, republish replaces atomically (exactly one row remains, not two), delete wipes, delete on a never-published tenant is a no-op, cross-tenant fuzz (write A invisible to B, two tenants side-by-side, delete A does not touch B), and the type-level assertion that `available` cannot live on the snapshot item.

Full triple green locally: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` (1002 backend tests pass, no new warnings).

## Schema delta

New table `publishedMenus` wired into `convex/schema.ts`. Codegen output (`convex/_generated/api.d.ts`) is committed alongside per the work-next-agent-issue contract.

## Scope

- `packages/backend/convex/table/publishedMenus.ts` — new schema file.
- `packages/backend/convex/lib/tenancy/menuStore.ts` — three helpers appended at the end.
- `packages/backend/convex/lib/tenancy/index.ts` — barrel re-exports.
- `packages/backend/convex/schema.ts` — wire the new table.
- `packages/backend/convex/lib/tenancy/menuStore.test.ts` — new test file.
- `packages/backend/convex/_generated/api.d.ts` — codegen delta.

ZERO edits in `apps/web` or `apps/native`.

## Tests E2E proposés

N/A — pure schema + store seam delta, no user-observable surface yet. The user-observable parcours (publish a menu, see it on the PWA, toggle out-of-stock without republishing, never-published edge) will be exercised by the next slices that wire `publishMenu` + the `getPublicMenu` pivot.

author: eltiokarma
body:
## Summary
Bug que reportaste: streams conectados a bloques `Ambient` (nube/atmósfera) quedaban con la P upstream propagada — p.ej. el purge de Haber entrando a la "nube" a 200 bar — lo cual no es físico (hay una válvula de let-down implícita entre la planta presurizada y la atmósfera).

### Fix
- Nuevo `flowsheet_solver.anchor_ambient_pressures(fs)`: recorre los streams conectados a bloques `Ambient` (sea como src=intake o dst=vent) y los fija a **1.013 bar** con `pressure_locked=True`. Respeta locks previos del user.
- Se llama **DESPUÉS** de `solve_pressure_hydraulic`, no antes. Si se llama antes, los locks que añade activan `solve_pressure_propagation` (que de otra forma retornaría vacío por `has_pressure_specs=False`), y esa propagation pisa gradientes que setean los unit-op solvers — p.ej. el +0.1 bar del bottom de columna en `_example_reactor_flash_column`.

### Resultado del audit en los 41 ejemplos
- **7 venteos a alta P** (purge / vent / blowdown / H₂O vapor de evaporador): TODOS anclados a 1.013 bar
- **0 intakes con problema** (los ejemplos no tienen aire/feed desde atmósfera no-auto_aux)

| Ejemplo | Stream | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|---|
| haber_recycle | S-purge | 200 bar | 1.013 bar |
| industrial_complete | S-vent | 80 bar | 1.013 bar |
| industrial_complete | S-purge | 80 bar | 1.013 bar |
| urea | S-purga | 150 bar | 1.013 bar |
| urea | S-H2O | 150 bar | 1.013 bar |
| acetic_acid | S-purga | 35 bar | 1.013 bar |
| hno3_ostwald | A13c-bleach-vent | 11 bar | 1.013 bar |

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest -q` → 276 passed (incluido `test_column_propagates_T` que verifica el gradiente +0.1 bar del bottom)
- [x] `validate_ui.py` → todos pasan

author: stormer78
body:
## Summary

Adds the **second step-up gate** — `build_approve_response_did_signed` — completing the cross-device step-up (the WebAuthn gate landed in #158). Builds an `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.1` with `evidence.kind = did-signed` and attaches a **Data Integrity proof** (`eddsa-jcs-2022`) over the document.

## Key-custody-preserving design (no hand-rolled crypto)

The holder/subject private key **never enters Rust**:
1. `affinidi-data-integrity::prepare_sign_input` does the `eddsa-jcs-2022` canonicalization + hashing (its documented remote-signer entry point).
2. the native enclave `Signer` (the #151 callback) signs the returned bytes;
3. we set `proofValue = multibase(base58btc, signature)` and attach the proof.

So canonicalization/encoding come from the blessed DI library, not from us.

## What's here (`stepup.rs`)

- `build_approve_response_did_signed(draft, signer)`.
- Shared `assemble_doc()` now backs both builders; `did_key_vm()` derives the `verificationMethod` for the did:key holder.
- Deps: `affinidi-data-integrity` + `multibase` (prod), `ed25519-dalek` (dev).

## Verification (full local CI, isolated worktree)

- `cargo test -p vta-mobile-core` → **14 passed**, including an **end-to-end crypto test**: sign with a stand-in Ed25519 key, then `affinidi-data-integrity::verify_with_public_key` **accepts** the produced proof — proving the canonicalization + proofValue assembly are byte-correct (an RP verifies the same way). Plus a non-`did:key`-signer rejection. ✓
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean ✓
- `cargo deny check` exit 0, no errors ✓
- Kotlin + Swift bindings generate (`buildApproveResponseDidSigned`) ✓

## Status

Both step-up gates now build end-to-end on-device: parse request (#156) → consent → WebAuthn (#158) **or** DID-signed (this PR) response. Next: **Slice 3** — async `vta-sdk` session + DIDComm pack/unpack.

The change addresses the visual collision between the "T" (trivial) badge and the "T<n>" task ID prefix on kanban cards, which made it difficult to distinguish effort level at a glance. The new sizing system is more intuitive and aligns with industry-standard notation.

## Changes

- Updated EffortChip.letter mapping: trivial→XS, small→S, medium→M, large→L, max→XL
- Removed fixed `frame(minWidth: 18)` constraint to allow 2-character badges (XS/XL) to render naturally
- Added comprehensive unit tests (EffortChipTests) verifying the complete mapping and badge sizing

## Verification

- Compiled and added unit test coverage for all effort levels
- Tooltip and accessibility labels continue to read full words ("Trivial", "Small", etc.)
- Badge pill sizing adapts to 2-character content (XS/XL) without clipping
- No changes to underlying enum values, CLI arguments, or database schema—display-only change

## Test Coverage

EffortChipTests validates:
- All 5 effort levels map to correct badge characters
- Single-character badges remain single-character
- XS/XL are properly 2-character strings without being clipped
- Full-word labels are preserved for accessibility

The score was saved to DB only once on first detail-page visit, then blocked by a 'if (hike.cachedBeautyScore) return' guard that prevented any update. Result: the list showed an outdated/wrong score forever.

Fixes:
1. Set poisFullyLoaded=true in the cached-POIs branch so the save effect fires even when data comes from the DB cache (not just fresh fetch)

3. Gate the save on poisFullyLoaded (all POI + wiki data present) to ensure the score is always computed from complete data, not a partial mid-load state

## Problem

`recap.shared.hook_io.LOG_FILE` is computed at import time from `~/.local/state/knowledge-gardener/auto-recap.log`. In-process tests that hit an error path triggering `log()` — notably `test_daily_note_apply_block_cleans_tmp_on_replace_failure` (the atomic-write failure test added in #24) — appended to the **developer's real auto-recap log**, leaving misleading `daily write failed: OSError('cross-device move')` entries that look like production failures.

Found while verifying the v0.16.0 plugin in the live environment.

## Fix

Add `tests/conftest.py` with an autouse fixture that redirects `hook_io.LOG_FILE` to a per-test temp path. Subprocess tests already isolate this via a fake `HOME`; this covers the in-process gap and prevents the whole class of pollution.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Removes dead code and fixes possible bugs found in the enroll/cart flow. All 35 Feature tests pass.

**Dead code / dedup**
- `ImageController::upload`: dropped the unreachable `if (!$event)` block after `Event::findOrFail($eventId)` (findOrFail already 404s).
- Consolidated the two duplicated `generateUniqueCode()` helpers (in `CartController` + `EventParticipantController`) into one static `EventParticipant::generateUniqueCode(Event $event)`; removed both local copies and the now-unused `Str` imports.

**Bug fixes (logic changes)**
- **Capacity race on enroll** — the capacity check ran *outside* the transaction, so concurrent requests could both pass it and overflow `max_participants`. `EventParticipantController::store` now does the capacity check + insert inside `DB::transaction`, serialized by a `lockForUpdate` on the event row:
  ```
  DB::transaction(fn () => {
    Event::whereKey($event->id)->lockForUpdate()->first(); // serialize enrollers
    // existing-participant lock, capacity count, then create/re-enroll
  })
  ```
  Response codes/messages preserved (409 already-enrolled, 422 full, 200 re-enroll, 201 new).
- **Deadline off-by-a-day** — backend rejected enrollment after midnight at the *start* of the deadline day, while the frontend treats the deadline as end-of-day (`setHours(23,59,59)`). Both `store` and `checkout` now compare against `Carbon::parse($event->registration_deadline)->endOfDay()`.

**Cart `quantity` removal (vestigial)**
Checkout always enrolled exactly once regardless of `quantity`, so the field was dead. Removed it end-to-end: `store` validation + accumulation logic, the `update` method and its `PUT/PATCH /carts/{cart}` route, the `Cart` fillable, and the seeder. Added migration dropping the `quantity` column and adding `unique(user_id, event_id)` so a cart can't hold duplicate rows for the same event.

## Notes / intentionally NOT changed
- **Event date casts (flagged item) skipped on purpose.** Casting `start_date`/`end_date` to `datetime` would serialize the naive DB value (`14:00`) as UTC (`...Z`); the frontend renders via `new Date(...).toLocaleTimeString('id-ID')`, which would shift the displayed time (e.g. 14:00 → 21:00 in WIB). That would be a display regression, so dates are left as-is and the deadline fix uses explicit `Carbon::parse(...)`.
- `participants_count` (`withCount`) is already present on `stable`, so no change was needed there.

## Verification
- `php artisan test --testsuite=Feature`: **35 passed, 216 assertions**.
- Composer install + migrations run clean on sqlite.

author: etendue
body:
## 总结

Stage 11 实现 **image-space 深度监督**（LiDAR 投影稀疏深度 + DepthAnythingV2 稠密 metric depth），作为 **opt-in yaml 选项**（默认全 OFF，baseline 字节等价）。

**关键结论（A800 30k sym5cam 实测）**：工程链路完整且正确，但 **depth 监督对 novel-view 无可观测提升**，主 KPI（+3.0）未达成 —— 量化（LPIPS Δ-0.0015）+ 视觉 A/B（viser 3dgut 肉眼无差别）一致。reconstructed 不退化（cc_psnr_masked 25.98 vs baseline 26.04）。代码沉淀为可配置选项供后续调参/复用。

## 实测对比 (vs baseline `v3_kpi_sym5cam_30k`)

| 指标 | baseline | Stage11(+depth) | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|
| cc_psnr_masked | 26.04 | 25.98 (Δ-0.06) | 不退化 ✓ |
| novel-view LPIPS (4模式avg) | 0.6022 | 0.6007 (Δ-0.0015) | 无提升 ✗ |
| 视觉 A/B | — | 肉眼无差别 | 印证 |
| mean_lidar_psnr | — | 20.68 (<25 ref) | 口径未校准 |
| it/s | — | 4.68 (30k≈107min) | — |

## 根因（疑）
`lidar_w_decay=1.0` 让 LiDAR λ 到 30k 衰到 ~2.4% + depth_prior inverse-depth 早饱和（27→0 by step 1000）→ 监督训练中途消失；30k/5cam 下 RGB 信号已 pin 住几何（高斯 LiDAR 初始化），先验改进空间小。呼应 plan 风险 R13/R14。

## 改动
**新增**
- `threedgrut/correction/depth_prior.py` — `DepthLoss`(l1/l2/smooth_l1 + normalize + inverse-depth) + `compute_bg_lidar_loss`
- `threedgrut/utils/eval_metrics.py` — `compute_lidar_psnr` (mean_lidar_psnr, render.py+trainer 双路)
- `scripts/dump_lidar_depth_map.py` — LiDAR→image 投影 dump (FthetaForwardProjector 复用)
- `scripts/dump_depth_priors.py` + `scripts/download_depth_anything_v2.sh` — DepthV2 dump
- 7 个测试文件（47 单测）

**修改**
- `threedgrut/trainer.py` — 3 loss head 接入 (`use_lidar_depth`/`use_depth_prior` gated) + per-head TB 记录
- `threedgrut/datasets/datasetNcore.py` + `__init__.py` — lidar_depth_map/depth_prior 注入 (train/val/test 三路)
- `threedgrut/render.py` (top-level + class) — mean_lidar_psnr eval
- `configs/apps/ncore_3dgut_mcmc_multilayer.yaml` — opt-in 配置块（默认 OFF）

## 启用方式
\`\`\`bash
python train.py --config-name apps/ncore_3dgut_mcmc_multilayer \
  trainer.use_lidar_depth=true trainer.use_depth_prior=true \
  dataset.load_lidar_depth_map=true dataset.load_depth_prior=true ...
# 需先 scripts/dump_lidar_depth_map.py + dump_depth_priors.py 预 dump 深度图
\`\`\`

## 调参待验方向（未来）
`lidar_w_decay=0`（全程监督）+ 提 `lambda_depth_prior` + depth_prior 换不饱和 loss。

## 验证
- 47 Mac CPU 单测全过（loss/grad-check/projection/reader/eval-metric/regression-guards）
- A800 1k smoke (LiDAR-only + 三 loss) + 30k 出口 + render.py eval 全跑通
- Hydra compose + yaml.safe_load 确认 opt-in 选项默认 OFF

⚠️ 分支自 `4c7635b`，merge 前需 rebase on 当前 main（v3_plan.md 有 divergence，附加式改动应可自动合并）。

body:
## Summary

`apps/application-admin-console/src/api/audit-log-client.ts` (Issue #1292 — the Tenant Admin Console self-tenant audit-log read client) was at **46% statements**. Added `test/audit-log-client.test.ts` that stubs global `fetch` and, for the hook, mocks `useAuth` via `renderHook`:

- `buildTenantAuditQuery`: empty → `""`, and every filter serialized (incl. `limit=0`).
- `createTenantAuditClient.list` / `exportCsv`: route + query, `Bearer` header, trailing-slash base normalization, leading-slash path strip, `Blob` return, and the **cross-tenant contract** — no `tenantId` ever appears in the URL (backend pins it from the JWT claim).
- `request()` non-ok → `TenantAuditApiError` with `errorCode` parsed from `body.error`, plus the non-JSON-body and missing-`"error"`-field fallbacks (`errorCode` undefined).
- `useTenantAuditClient`: returns a client when `auth.tokens` present, `null` otherwise.
- `TenantAuditApiError` message + `describeTenantAuditError` for every switch arm (403 / 503 / 401 / 400 `invalid_from`|`invalid_to`|`invalid_limit`|other / default).

audit-log-client.ts now reports **100% statements / branches / functions / lines** (14 tests).

## Test plan
- `vitest run test/audit-log-client.test.ts --coverage --coverage.include=src/api/audit-log-client.ts` → 14 tests pass, 100% across all four dimensions.
- Full application-admin-console suite: 421 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean; biome clean; `make harness` no findings; pre-commit `before-commit` gate green.

## Regression analysis
- Test-only. No `src/**` change → no runtime / CFn behavior shift. `fetch` and the AuthProvider mock are restored by `vi.restoreAllMocks()` afterEach; the module mock is file-scoped.

## Physical impact
- NO-OP on CFn / deployed artifacts. Test file only; not bundled into any Lambda or SPA dist.

> Note: this client is structurally a near-twin of admin-console's `audit-client.ts` (different plane, routes, error codes). Cross-plane consolidation is a separate design question tracked under the code-quality umbrella (#1418); not in scope here.

author: jan-kubica
body:
## Summary

Render-pipeline follow-up to PR #513, which wired `Image.opacity` through
the model layer (parse + serialize of `<a:alphaModFix amt>` inside
`<a:blip>`) but did not thread the value into the layout / painter. Result
before this PR: a partially-transparent image still painted fully opaque.

- Add `opacity?: number` to `ImageRun`, `ImageBlock`, `ImageAttrs`,
  `ImageExtension` attrs, and the page-level `PageFloatingImage` (body
  and header / footer floating-image collectors).
- Thread the value through `toFlowBlocks.buildImageRun` / `convertImage`,
  `toProseDoc.convertImage`, and `fromProseDoc` so save / load round-trips
  preserve it.
- Introduce shared `ImageVisualAttrs` + `hasImageVisualAttrs` +
  `applyImageVisualAttrs` helpers in `renderImage.ts`, used by the
  floating fragment, inline image, block image, body floating layer, and
  header / footer floating loop. Mirrors eigenpal's `ImageVisualAttrs`
  shape so crop or other per-image visual attrs can extend the same gate
  later without churning every call site.
- `ImageExtension.toDOM` also emits the CSS opacity (and `data-opacity`
  hint) so the PM-rendered editor DOM matches what the painter draws.

## Null-default gate

The helpers use `!= null` rather than `!== undefined`, intentionally.
ProseMirror schema defaults are `null`, that `null` survives the
`as number | undefined` cast in the bridge, and `null < 1` is `true`
while `Math.max(0, null)` is `0`. With `!== undefined`, every plain
image would have rendered at `opacity: 0` -- the regression eigenpal hit
and fixed in `c605277c9`'s final follow-up. Three of the new tests pin
this contract directly.

## Tests

New file: `packages/folio/src/core/layout-painter/renderImage-opacity.test.ts`
(8 tests, all green).

- `renderImageFragment opacity (floating block path)` -- emits CSS
  opacity for `opacity: 0.5`; emits no CSS opacity when the attribute is
  absent.
- `renderLine inline image opacity` -- emits CSS opacity for an inline
  `ImageRun` with `opacity: 0.5`; emits no CSS opacity for a plain inline
  image (the null-default regression guard).
- `ImageVisualAttrs helpers` -- `hasImageVisualAttrs` returns `true` for
  `opacity: 0.5`, `false` for `opacity: 1`, `false` for `opacity: null`
  (PM schema default); `applyImageVisualAttrs` skips the CSS write for a
  null PM default.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun --filter @stll/folio test` -- 1022 pass (up from 1014; +8 new).
- [x] `bun --filter @stll/folio typecheck` -- clean.
- [x] `bun --filter @stll/folio lint` -- clean.
- [ ] Manual visual sanity check on a DOCX with `<a:alphaModFix amt>` set
      to a partial value once #513 lands and this rebases onto main.

## Dependency note

This PR depends on PR #513 (`fix(folio): close 3 image OOXML round-trip
gaps`), which adds `Image.opacity` to the model. Once #513 merges into
main, this branch becomes a clean single-commit delta against main.

author: geoffe-ga
body:
Closes #98
Refs #3

## Summary

Replace the per-slot `med.doseEvents.contains(...)` traversal in `PendingQueueSelector` — which hydrated every historical `DoseEvent` for each maintenance med on every watch app open — with a single bounded SwiftData fetch + O(1) lookup. This is the exact cascading-fetch hazard SPEC §5.2 calls out (and the reason `DoseEvent.ingredientAmounts` is denormalized).

### Design

- **Single `FetchDescriptor<DoseEvent>` bounded by `takenAt`** ∈ `[yesterday-start, day-after-tomorrow-start)`. Uses the existing `takenAt` index. Worst-case ~36 events at the documented 12-pills/day budget regardless of total history length.
- **`scheduledFor` is filtered in memory** to today's window before building the lookup. The ±1 day takenAt window catches a proactively-logged dose (taken late yesterday for today's slot) so the bound stays correct under all the realistic edge cases the old relationship-traversal approach handled.
- **`SlotKey(medicationID, hour, minute)`** value type for O(1) "already logged" lookups. Day is implicit in the bounded fetch, so the key doesn't need to carry it.

### `#Predicate` caveat

The reviewer's sketch in the issue used `event.scheduledFor! >= startOfDay && event.scheduledFor! < nextDay`. That compiles but fails at fetch time with `unsupportedPredicate` ("The 'Foundation.PredicateExpressions.ForcedUnwrap' operator is not supported") on iOS 26's SwiftData — verified by an interim attempt that broke 6 existing tests. Hence the fallback to `takenAt` (which is non-optional) plus the in-memory `scheduledFor` filter. Documented inline so the next reader doesn't reach for the same expression.

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` — clean.
- [x] `xcodebuild test` on iPhone 17 — full `PendingQueueSelectorTests` suite passes (15 existing + 1 new) without modification.
- [x] `xcodebuild build` on Apple Watch Series 11 — clean.
- [x] New `outOfWindowHistoryDoesNotAffectResult`: seeds 60 prior-day events on the same slot and asserts today's slot is still pending. Behavior parity with the old relationship traversal; the new bounded fetch preserves it.
- [ ] Paired simulator manual check (deferred for reviewer): create a maintenance med, log a few prior-day doses, observe today's slot still appears as pending in the Right Now view and the response feels indistinguishable from before.

- Updated `MainLevelFlow.gd` to prefer calling `_ensure_global_background_backdrop` and fall back to the legacy `_ensure_global_sand_tile_backdrop` when present, and kept a shim for loading resort sand tile textures via `_load_resort_sand_tile_textures`.

### Testing

author: chatelao
body:
I have completed the analysis of the performance loss between v9.5 and v10.0 and documented the findings in `PERF_LOSS_10.md`.

Key findings include:
- **Flag Redefinition**: In v9.5, `-p` meant `--parallel`, but in v10.0 it enables `--ptx-debug`, causing a shift from parallel to sequential execution.
- **I/O Flushing**: Enabling `--ptx-debug` in v10.0 causes the XML writer to flush after every PTOCA control sequence (over 300,000 times in the test case).
- **Monitoring Overhead**: The `MnemonicPerformanceMonitor` and its associated StAX wrapper introduce significant unmeasured overhead when processing millions of XML elements.
- **Jackson Reflection**: Many fields are serialized using Jackson's reflective `writeValue`, which is slower than manual StAX writing.
- **MMAP Overhead**: For many small files, the overhead of memory mapping outweighs the benefits.

The document includes a table breaking down the 61-second execution time into measured and unmeasured categories.

Fixes #1266

author: sijanthapa171
body:
This pull request introduces a migration of the authentication and user account storage system from a file-based approach to an H2 SQL database, along with a new configuration management system. It includes new infrastructure for database support, updates to configuration loading, and refactors the authentication service to use persistent storage. Additionally, it adds a unit test for the new database-backed authentication service.

**Database Integration and Authentication Refactor:**

- Introduced a new `DatabaseSupport` class to manage database connections, schema initialization, and ensure the database directory exists. This class is responsible for setting up required tables for user accounts, students, teachers, and classrooms.
- Refactored `InMemoryAuthService` to store and retrieve user accounts from the H2 database using SQL queries instead of in-memory maps and properties files. All account operations (authentication, creation, retrieval) now interact with the database. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e5374aa0a4dff78c1504f25159504ffa351fd3e65ae896c15b33bd38d3035e34L3-L30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e5374aa0a4dff78c1504f25159504ffa351fd3e65ae896c15b33bd38d3035e34L43-L52) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e5374aa0a4dff78c1504f25159504ffa351fd3e65ae896c15b33bd38d3035e34L61-R126)

**Configuration Management:**

- Implemented a singleton `AppConfig` class to load application and database configuration from an `application.properties` file and system properties, providing default values when properties are missing.
- Updated application startup to use the application name from configuration instead of a hardcoded value. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bfd9b1caca492cb47c5e1cca276236bebf5e84fc81026186866f8c00becbf29cR5-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bfd9b1caca492cb47c5e1cca276236bebf5e84fc81026186866f8c00becbf29cL15-R17)
- Added a sample `application.properties` file with database connection settings and application name.

**Dependency and Build Updates:**

- Added the H2 database dependency to `pom.xml` and updated the module descriptor to require `java.sql` and `com.h2database`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9c5fb3d1b7e3b0f54bc5c4182965c4fe1f9023d449017cece3005d3f90e8e4d8R31-R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ed4152fc79c851ea436af640f5fc06984df0f45c56e0a74a39ff3fa8cb55fcf4R4-R5)

**Testing:**

- Added a unit test for `InMemoryAuthService` to verify account creation, duplicate prevention, and authentication using an in-memory H2 database.

body:
## Description

This PR introduces a Personalized Experiment Difficulty Prediction System that helps students understand how challenging an experiment may be based on their learning progress, quiz performance, and subject mastery.

The system generates personalized readiness insights and success probability predictions before students begin an experiment.

---

## Backend Implementation

### Prediction Engine

Added:

* `Backend/app/services/prediction_service.py`

The prediction engine analyzes:

* Subject mastery
* Quiz performance
* Completed experiments
* Prerequisite completion
* Learning streaks

to calculate:

* Success probability
* Difficulty rating
* Readiness level
* Personalized recommendations

---

### Prediction API

Added:

* `Backend/app/api/predictions.py`

Endpoints provide:

* Experiment readiness analysis
* Success probability calculations
* Difficulty predictions
* Recommended preparation steps

---

### Schema Updates

Updated:

* `Backend/app/models/schemas.py`

to support prediction-related response structures and readiness metrics.

---

## Frontend Implementation

### Success Probability Badges

Added:

* `SuccessProbabilityBadge.jsx`

Features:

* Visual success indicators
* Quick readiness overview
* Dynamic probability display

Example:

```text
🎯 82% Success Probability
```

---

### Difficulty Prediction Modal

Added:

* `DifficultyPredictionModal.jsx`

Displays:

* Expected difficulty
* Estimated completion time
* Success probability
* Readiness level
* Personalized recommendations

---

### Prediction Context

Added:

* `PredictionContext.jsx`

Handles:

* Prediction state management
* API communication
* Caching and updates

---

author: buzu84
body:
## Summary Adds 55 unit tests for the `decisionReviewOutputSchema` Zod schema in `src/lib/decisions/review-schemas.ts`. This schema is the final validation boundary for structured AI output before it reaches the database and UI. These tests verify the schema contract is neither too strict (rejecting valid AI output) nor too loose (accepting malformed data that could corrupt stored records or crash the UI). ## Why This Matters The Decision Review pipeline processes AI-generated JSON through three stages: ``` raw AI output → normalizer → Zod schema → DB/UI ``` Blocks 1–2 (PRs #34, #35) covered JSONB parser and normalizer tests. This PR completes the validation layer by testing the Zod schema itself — the last safety gate before data is persisted to `product_decision_options`, `product_assumptions`, `product_decision_recommendations`, and related tables. Without schema tests, a loosened or broken constraint could silently accept malformed AI output, leading to corrupt database rows, broken UI rendering, or runtime crashes in downstream components. ## What Changed ### New file: `src/lib/decisions/__tests__/review-schemas.test.ts` **55 tests** organized into 10 behavior-focused groups: **Valid inputs (9 tests)** - Complete valid fixture acceptance - Minimal fixture with only required fields (all optionals omitted) - Optional fields (`validationMethod`, `supportingCitationIds`, `expectedImpact`, `mitigation`) accepted when present - Boundary values: 4 options (max), confidenceScore 0 and 100 - All enum values for assumption type (8), effort (4), reversibility (4) - Empty option description documented as intentionally accepted (UI guards with `&&`) **Missing required fields (7 tests)** - Each top-level required field: `summary`, `confidenceScore`, `assumptions`, `options`, `risks`, `recommendation` - Nested required field: `recommendation.reasoning` **Invalid enum values (6 tests)** - One test per enum: assumption type, riskLevel, evidenceStatus, effortEstimate, reversibility, severity **Confidence score validation (7 tests)** - Out-of-range: below 0, above 100 - Wrong type: string (schema does not coerce) - Edge cases: `NaN`, `Infinity` - Nested: option-level and recommendation-level confidence out of range **Array constraints (7 tests)** - Empty arrays where min ≥ 1: assumptions, risks, pros, cons, reasoning - Options count: fewer than 3, more than 4 **String length constraints (4 tests)** - Min-length violations: summary (< 10), assumption statement (< 5), option title (< 2), recommendation text (< 10) **Malformed structures (11 tests)** - Top-level: `null`, primitive string, array wrapper - Nested: `null` in arrays, primitives in arrays, partially malformed objects - Type mismatches: recommendation as string, recommendation as `null`, assumptions as string - Missing nested fields: option without title **Unknown fields (2 tests)** - Top-level unknown fields stripped (default Zod behavior) - Nested unknown fields stripped **Normalizer → Schema boundary (3 tests)** - Schema rejects snake_case keys (normalizer responsibility) - Schema rejects numeric string confidenceScore (normalizer coerces) - Schema rejects non-canonical enum aliases like `"legal"` (normalizer maps to `"business"`) ### Test infrastructure - `makeValidReview()` — typed fixture factory using `Partial` overrides - `makeOption()` — option sub-fixture factory - `makeUntypedReview()` — `Record` factory for injecting invalid values without `as any` ## What Was Not Changed - **No production code modified** — `review-schemas.ts` is unchanged - No route handlers, UI components, or API endpoints touched - No Supabase types or database schema changes - No package.json or config changes - No mocks (OpenAI, Supabase, or otherwise) ## Validation ```bash npx vitest run # 152 tests, 4 files, all passing npx tsc --noEmit # clean npm run lint # clean (pre-existing warnings only) npm run build # successful ``` ## Design Decisions **Empty option description accepted**: `option.description` has `max(5000)` but no `min()`. Investigation confirmed the UI guards with `{opt.description && (

...

)}`, so empty string is falsy and simply hides the paragraph. No schema change needed. **No `as any` in tests**: All 15 original `as any` casts were eliminated using `makeUntypedReview()`, which returns `Record` for `safeParse` (which accepts `unknown`). One safe `as Record` widening cast remains for the nested unknown-field strip test. **Strip vs strict mode**: Schema uses default Zod strip behavior (unknown fields silently removed). This is intentional for AI output, which may include extra fields like `metadata` or `model` that are harmless and should not cause validation failure. ## Follow-ups - Consider adding `min(1)` to `option.description` if future UI changes make empty descriptions user-visible - Schema max constraints (e.g., assumptions max 15) could be stress-tested with max-boundary fixtures in a future hardening pass - `recommendation.supportingEvidence`, `assumptions`, `risks`, `alternatives`, `nextValidationSteps` arrays have no `min()` — intentional for AI flexibility but worth documenting

author: passcod
body:
🤖 Phase 1 of consolidating monitoring (TODO #10, plan in `docs/plans/healthchecks-into-alertd.md`). Behaviour-preserving refactor — no check logic changes.

The doctor/healthcheck subsystem was split across three crates: the `Check` type and checks in `bestool-tamanu`, the sweep orchestration + canopy posting in `bestool`, and the daemon framework in `bestool-alertd`. This moves the whole subsystem into `bestool-alertd` so the monitoring engine owns both the framework and the checks, with `bestool-alertd` now depending on `bestool-tamanu` for common Tamanu domain code (config, discovery, services, server-info DB queries). No dependency cycle — `bestool-tamanu` never depends on alertd.

- `bestool-tamanu` → `bestool-alertd`: the entire `doctor` module (`check`, `checks`, `checks/*`, `progress`, `server_info` facts), mounted at `crate::doctor`.
- `bestool` → `bestool-alertd`: `SweepResult`, `perform_sweep`, `collect_server_facts`, `build_payload`, `overall_from_payload` (now `doctor/sweep.rs`) and `DoctorTask` (now `doctor/task.rs`), with their tests. `bestool` keeps the `tamanu doctor` CLI, rendering, and daemon-fetch, calling `bestool_alertd::doctor`.
- `bestool-tamanu` loses its `doctor` feature and the deps only it used (`bestool-kopia`, `hickory-resolver`, `owo-colors`, `reqwest`), which move to `bestool-alertd`.

The one mechanical change: `perform_sweep` now takes the running binary's version as a parameter instead of `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (which would otherwise resolve to alertd's version once moved). Both callers pass bestool's version, so the wire payload is unchanged.

Subsequent phases migrate the YAML alerts to checks (in alertd), retire the YAML alert engine + standalone CLI, and review thresholds.

author: alas-poor-ophelia
body: ## Summary - Replaces Cytoscape's bezier genealogy edges with right-angle SVG path connectors in `family-graph` mode, producing the classic family tree visual - Adds spouse-lockstep drag: grabbing one partner moves the other via `grab/drag/free` event handlers - Zero new runtime dependencies — connectors are pure SVG `M/H/V` path commands drawn on a transparent overlay synced to Cytoscape's viewport ## What it looks like Classic family tree connectors: vertical drops from parent pairs, horizontal distribution bars across siblings, and individual drops to each child. Pair/spouse edges remain rendered by Cytoscape as before. ``` Parent1 ─── Parent2 │ ┌───┼───┐ │ │ │ Child1 Child2 Child3 ``` ## How it works New `src/family-connectors.ts` (245 lines) with a single export `drawFamilyConnectors()`, called after `applyGenerationLayout()` positions nodes: 1. **Hides** Cytoscape genealogy edges (opacity: 0) via a new `.genealogy` CSS class 2. **Draws** orthogonal SVG paths for each family unit (parent-set → children group) 3. **Syncs** the SVG overlay transform with Cytoscape's pan/zoom/resize 4. **Redraws** connectors on node position changes, coalesced to one repaint per animation frame 5. **Moves** pair-connected partners in lockstep when any node is dragged Connector geometry is robust to drag: clamped gaps prevent inversion when parents are dragged below children, the distribution bar always extends to include the parent drop point, and midpoint averaging handles parents at different Y levels. ## Changes | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/family-connectors.ts` | **New** — SVG connector overlay + spouse drag | | `src/render.ts` | +3 lines: import, call site, `.genealogy` class on edges | | `main.js` | Rebuilt bundle | ## Test plan - [x] Open a vault with `family-graph: true` code blocks — connectors should render as right-angle paths - [x] Test with 1 child, 2 children, 3+ children from one couple - [x] Test multi-generation trees (grandparents → parents → children) - [x] Drag a married node — spouse should follow in lockstep - [x] Drag an unmarried node — should move independently with connectors redrawing - [x] Pan and zoom — SVG overlay should stay in sync - [x] Verify non-family-graph modes (force-directed, dagre) are unaffected - [x] Test compact/embedded code blocks (mini/small/large sizes)

body:
**What:** Added explicit `aria-label` attributes to the Guide and Preset select dropdowns and the input `textarea` within `PlaygroundView`. Also added distinct visual focus states (`focus-visible:outline-[var(--strand-color-accent-lede)]`) to these controls.
**Why:** The custom form wrappers do not implicitly link labels via `id`/`htmlFor`, causing screen readers to announce unlabelled controls. Additionally, using `focus:outline-none` stripped default keyboard focus indicators making navigation harder for sighted keyboard users.
**Before/After:** Form elements used to drop their default outline without applying a custom one when focused; they now show a clear strand-colored accent ring upon focus via `focus-visible`.

body:
## Summary
- Beachhead deliverable for the options track: ready-made hedge structures backtestable end-to-end over a price path, with no live option feed (synthetic fixture).
- gammaScalp: hold an option (long gamma, short theta) and keep the book delta-neutral by trading a perp at a rebalance band. Each step marks the option with Black-Scholes and its delta with the greeks module, rehedges on band breach, and accrues transaction + funding cost. Profits when realized vol exceeds the implied vol it was marked at.
- protectivePut: hold the underlying plus a long put as insurance; the put caps downside on a crash.
- HedgeBacktestResult attributes every dollar into option / hedge / transaction / funding, so net() = optionPnl + hedgePnl - transactionCost - fundingCost. optionPnl is mark-to-market (theta decay already embedded), so theta is not double-counted.

body:
## Sprint 3 of epic #933 — stuck-session liveness detector

Refs #930. Builds on Sprint 1 design (`docs/design/sprint-runner-liveness-detector-2026-05-30.md`) and Sprint 2 probes. **Observe-only** this sprint: the tick now computes + logs a liveness verdict and records attempt-state, but every path still `exit 0`/skips launch. The actual reap/relaunch is Sprint 4 (#931).

### What landed
- **`fuse_verdict`** (pure) — `HUSK` (conclusive single) → HUSK; `>=2 STALL` → STUCK (corroborated); `==1` → SUSPECT (no reap, the false-positive guard); else HEALTHY. UNKNOWN never counts as STALL.
- **jq-backed attempt-state store** (`$WORKTREE_BASE/.runner-state.json`, override `RUNNER_STATE_FILE`) — atomic `mktemp`+`mv`, fail-safe (missing/corrupt → 0 attempts), convergent `state_prune`. The one fact runner truth can't rebuild after a reap.
- **`evaluate_liveness`** — the sampling edge (git/pgrep/ps/stat → probes → fuse), returning verdict + per-probe breakdown via globals.
- **Tick wiring** — `mode_run`'s OPEN-active-session branch now logs `verdict=… [commit=… process=… log=… attempts=N/3]` and records state; STUCK/HUSK logs the Sprint-4 handoff. The CLOSED-reap and foreign-session paths are untouched.

### TDD / DoD
- Red→Green for both layers; `/simplify` + fresh-context `review` passes applied.
- **Review caught a real bug:** `evaluate_liveness` was called in `$(...)`, so its breakdown globals died in the subshell and the log line printed blank `[commit= process= log=]`. Fixed (call as a statement; read `$LIVENESS_VERDICT`); test strengthened to assert the populated breakdown → [Lesson 138](../blob/sprint-930-liveness-fusion/tasks/lessons/138-a-function-returning-data-via-globals-must-not-be-called-in-command-substitution.md).
- New tests: `scripts/tests/sprint-runner-fusion-state.test.sh` (fusion truth table + state) and `sprint-runner-liveness-tick.test.sh` (tick integration). **Full shell suite: 7/7 green, zero regressions.**

### Verification note (no PR preview surface)
This PR touches `scripts/**` only — not `frontend/**`/`packages/{shared-contracts,analytics-core}/**`/firebase — so `pr-preview.yml` is path-filtered out (no live preview channel). The sprint-runner is a **macOS-local launchd tool**, so its bash tests are intentionally not in the Linux CI (BSD `stat -f`/`date -j`/`ps -o lstart=`). Verification is the hermetic shell suite (7/7) + captured production log lines; the change adds **zero** JS/TS surface, so the CI suite is unaffected.

### Discovered constraint (flagged)
macOS system `screen 4.00.03` lacks `-Logfile` (design open-Q #2 assumed 4.06+), so production screen-logfile wiring is deferred — the log probe reads UNKNOWN until a later sprint wires it (hardcopy fallback). Fusion degrades safely (UNKNOWN never STALL). Full #871 end-to-end catch is Sprint 5 (#932).

author: iamovi
body:
This PR fixes the issue where the background would show as white even in dark mode during the initial boot phase or until a refresh.

The root cause was a CSS specificity conflict:
1. In `index.html`, there was a style: `html.dark body { background: var(--boot-background, #09090b); }`.
2. In `src/index.css`, the app applies theme colors to `body { background-color: hsl(var(--background)); }`.
3. Because `html.dark body` is a more specific selector than just `body`, the boot-time style (which defaults to a generic dark gray) could override the more complex theme-aware backgrounds applied by the React app once it loaded.
4. Additionally, since browsers use the `html` background color to fill the viewport before the `body` is fully painted, setting a base `html` background of white caused a visible flash.

By moving the background application to the `html` element and making the `body` transparent during boot, we ensure the correct color is shown immediately and that the application's CSS can take over cleanly once loaded.

## Summary

Adds the bundled **weekly-report** plugin (`extensions/weekly-report/`): a cron-triggered Feishu/Lark weekly-report flow. A scheduled `systemEvent` fires `begin_weekly_report`, the agent drafts a first-person report from three fact sources (session messages, git activity, recent group messages), delivers it as a CardKit form card, and on confirm writes it **non-destructively** to a Lark doc.

Key pieces:

- **Non-destructive doc write** (`src/doc-writer.ts`) — official `lark-cli docs +update` block ops. Fetches the outline, replaces the same-ISO-week `## <week_title>` H2 section in place (or inserts at the document head on first run), and cleans up legacy sentinel comments. Replaces the old destructive `mode:overwrite` path that clobbered images/comments on every write.
- **Doc title bump** — after a successful write, bumps the doc's `（updated at MMDD）` marker to today's date.
- **Plugin-owned drafting contract** (`src/drafting-contract.ts`) — ships a first-person ("我"/I), facts-not-chat-recap drafting contract so a colleague can install the plugin and add a one-line cron trigger without hand-authoring a prompt.
- **Card callback fix** — the confirm handler acks Feishu's ~3s card callback immediately (info toast) and runs the doc write detached, so the write (which exceeds the ack deadline) no longer logs error 200530 "callback timeout".
- `begin_weekly_report` kickoff tool + `contracts.tools` manifest entry; CardKit form-card delivery (`src/card-sender.ts`); managed-flow timeout sweeper.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/weekly-report` — green (149 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- oxlint + oxfmt clean on touched files.
- esbuild bundle (`dist/index.js`) rebuilt and committed.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: non-destructive top-insert doc write, same-week replace, doc-title date bump, and the card-callback-timeout fix on a live gateway.
- Real environment tested: prod OpenClaw gateway node `instance-1n7ut600-25` (10.0.3.84), deployed via `openclaw plugins install --force` + `systemctl --user restart`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: triggered the weekly-report flow; confirmed the card; re-confirmed the same week; inspected the target Lark doc and gateway logs.
- Evidence after fix: new week section appears at the top with all prior weeks/images/comments intact; re-confirm replaces (does not duplicate) the same-week section; doc title marker bumped (e.g. `0524`→`0530`); after the detached-write change the gateway no longer logs 200530, and `[gateway] http server listening (… weekly-report)` / `ready` with `NRestarts=0`, all 6 crons intact.
- Observed result after fix: confirm → doc updated non-destructively, title bumped, card acked within deadline.
- What was not tested: automated end-to-end CI for the Lark CLI path (host CLI auth is environment-specific and unverifiable from the dev checkout); the `--as user` doc identity (this node runs `--as bot` with the doc shared to the bot).

author: lithial
body:
## Phase 4 — Merger Phase + Basic Emission

Drives a run `merging → merge_gate → done`. On entering `merging`, the orchestrator gathers the surviving worker branches (status `done`) and their summaries, spawns one merger subprocess in a retained `wrap/<run>/merge` worktree, and on `report_done` + exit 0 records a `merge_done` event and advances to `merge_gate`. Under the `AutoAdvanceGates` scaffold, `merge_gate → done` auto-resolves and a `run_done` event is recorded. The merged branch + summary are queryable via `GET /runs/{id}`.

**Emission scope: Minimal** (events table + `run_done` event + API exposure) — the spec's step-7 adapter long-poll subscription is deferred.

### What landed (all test-first / TDD)
| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/fsm` | `merging→merge_gate`, `merging→failed`, `merge_gate→done` transitions |
| `internal/store` | `events` table helpers (`InsertEvent`/`ListEventsByRun`/`LatestEventByKind`) |
| `internal/orchestrator` | `merger.go` (`driveMerger` + `driveMergeGate`); `worker_done`/`worker_blocked`/`worker_failed` events with summaries |
| `cmd/wrapd` | `--merger-cmd`/`--merger-env` |
| `internal/api` | `GET /runs/{id}` exposes `merge_branch`/`merge_summary` (from the `merge_done` event) |
| `internal/testutil` | `StartInProcessServerWithStore` (seed events in handler tests) |
| tests + docs | full happy path → `done` + merger-failure integration tests; CLAUDE.md + phase plan |

### Key design decisions (documented in CLAUDE.md)
- **No `merges` table** — the merge result lives in the `events` log (`merge_done` event); the merged branch is `wrap/<run>/merge` (derivable). Worker outcomes are events too, giving the merger per-branch context.
- **`merging` is driven unconditionally** (self-guards on nil `MergerCmd`); only the `plan_gate→working` and `merge_gate→done` gate crossings are behind `--auto-advance-gates`.
- **The daemon never runs `verification_command`** — the merger subprocess does, per "daemon never parses output for meaning." `driveMerger` reuses `interpretWorkerOutcome` (identical done-predicate).
- **Merger worktree/branch retained** (the output artifact).

### Verification
- `go test ./... -race` — all green
- `go test -tags=integration ./test/integration/...` — green (full run → `done`, merger-failure → `failed`, plus prior phases)

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-31-phase-4-merger.md`

author: jason-zane
body:
## The bug
After the long-input fix, the **matching** step failed (`POST /assessments` 500, `[runArchitectMatch.match] …`).

Root cause: the `competency_matching` model config was a pre-Architect default — **`minimax/minimax-m2.5`**, a reasoning model. The matcher was never exercised before Architect shipped, so this was never caught. Reasoning models emit thinking/prose and don't reliably honour strict JSON mode, so the structured ranking response failed to parse. (Brief extraction works because it runs on Claude.)

## Fix
- **Migration**: point `competency_matching` at `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` (the same proven, JSON-reliable model brief extraction uses), `max_tokens` 8000 for ranking ~20 factors. **Applied to live** — already effective, since the model is resolved from the DB at call time (no deploy needed for the config itself).
- **Harden** the matcher's JSON parser: if a model wraps the JSON in reasoning/prose, extract the outermost `{ … }` object and retry — so a future model swap degrades gracefully instead of 500ing.

Editable later in **Settings → AI Configuration → Competency Matching**.

`tsc` / `eslint` / `next build` green.

author: ooiyeefei
body:
## The bug (found in real demo prep)
`stage_pending_decisions` named files `pending_<call-timestamp>_<index>.md`, where the index resets to `000` every call. The timestamp alone isn't unique, so **two stage calls sharing a timestamp silently overwrote each other**:
- two calls in the same instant, or
- re-staging a batch that already carried a fixed timestamp (e.g. copying previously-extracted records).

No error — records just disappeared. Concretely: copying 12 records that shared one extraction timestamp left only ~9 on disk.

## Fix
Filename is now `pending_<timestamp>_<ULID>.md`:
- **ULID** = globally unique per record, across calls and instants → no collision ever.
- **timestamp prefix** kept → files stay chronologically sortable.
- ULID was already a dependency (`util/ulid.py`).

Example: `pending_2026-05-30T12-15-13.182084p00-00_01K9XT9TXEH2GVJW73WT8XR4FW.md`

## TDD
Regression test **pins `datetime.now`** so both stage calls get the identical timestamp — the exact collision trigger — then asserts all 4 records from two batches survive on disk.
- **RED** (current code): `assert 2 == 4` — batch B clobbered batch A.
- **GREEN** (fixed): 4 distinct files.

(The first version of this test passed without the fix — because sequential `datetime.now()` calls get different microseconds — so I rewrote it to pin the timestamp and actually reproduce the bug. Anti-pattern avoided.)

**Verified:** full suite **379 passed**, ruff clean, pyright 0 errors.

body:
Fixes #4740

#### Changes proposed in this Pull Request

The settings forms stay editable while a save is in progress, which is confusing on a slow connection.

The form now dims while the request is being made, and any edits made mid-save are discarded once it is completed (so you don't end up with changes that look saved but never actually reached the server).

Applies to "Payments > Settings", the express checkout method pages, advanced fraud protection, and the multi-currency store and single-currency settings.

#### Testing instructions

1. Go to **Payments > Settings**.
2. Throttle the connection (DevTools → Network → Slow 3G) so the save is slow enough to watch.
3. Change a setting and click **Save changes**. The form dims while it saves.
4. Repeat on the other settings screens:
    - any express checkout method page (e.g. Apple Pay / Google Pay)
    - Fraud protection → Advanced

author: jayashbhandary
body:
## Problem
Every platform job in `release.yml` failed at `dart run build_runner build`.

**Root cause:** `analyzer_plugin 0.12.0` (pulled transitively via `riverpod_generator 2.6.x → riverpod_analyzer_utils → custom_lint_core`) is incompatible with `analyzer 7.6.0` shipped by Flutter 3.44. The riverpod-2 codegen toolchain has **no self-consistent resolution** against that analyzer — `analyzer_plugin 0.12.0` needs analyzer ≤7.3.0 while `custom_lint_visitor 1.0.0+7.7.0` needs ≥7.7.0.

**Key finding:** the project uses **no codegen** — no `part '*.g.dart'`, no `@freezed`/`@riverpod`/`@JsonSerializable`. The build_runner step generated nothing (`wrote 0 outputs`). It was pure dead weight and the sole point of failure.

## Changes
- **release.yml**: remove `build_runner` from all jobs; pin Flutter `3.44.0`; add `workflow_dispatch` `tag` input + version-resolution step; version-stamp all artifacts; macOS ships DMGs (universal/arm64/x64); Linux stages desktop entry + icon.
- **install.sh / install.ps1**: rewired to `JayashBhandary/dexter`, suffix-match versioned assets, sudo install with launcher / Start Menu integration (modeled on Notilus).
- add `linux/packaging/dexter.desktop` + `assets/icon/icon.png`.

## Verified locally
- `flutter build linux --release` succeeds without build_runner.
- workflow YAML parses.

author: wagnerra23
body:
## Sintoma (Wagner, 2026-05-30)
> "whatsapp não lê mensagens enviadas pela equipe pelo WhatsApp oficial"

O número fica pareado ao oimpresso via daemon **whatsmeow** (QR), mas a equipe continua respondendo clientes pelo **WhatsApp Web / app oficial**. Essas respostas **nunca apareciam** na Caixa Unificada → conversa parecia eternamente sem resposta.

## Causa raiz
`ProcessIncomingWebhookJob::extractFromWhatsmeow` descartava todo evento `IsFromMe=true`:

```php
if (($info['IsFromMe'] ?? false) === true) {
    return []; // ← jogava fora a resposta da equipe
}
```

O multi-device do WhatsApp **replica** os envios de qualquer aparelho pareado (incl. WhatsApp Web oficial) pra sessão do daemon, com `IsFromMe=true`. O filtro era largo demais: além do eco dos envios do próprio oimpresso, descartava as respostas manuais da equipe. O Baileys já tinha resolvido isso no PR #688; o whatsmeow (ADR 0204, substituiu o Baileys em 27/05) **não herdou** o fix.

## Fix
- **Não descarta `fromMe`** — persiste como `direction=outbound`, `status=sent`.
- **Keyed no cliente** (`Chat`), não no nosso número: pra outbound, `Sender/SenderAlt` é o **nosso** número, então o contato é o destinatário (`Chat`).
- **Não incrementa unread** e **não sobrescreve `contact_name`** (o `PushName` de um evento fromMe é o nome do operador).
- **Idempotência** por `provider_message_id` UNIQUE deduplica o eco dos envios feitos pelo próprio composer do oimpresso.
- **Realtime**: publica `message.sent` (o frontend `CaixaUnificada/Index.tsx` já escuta) → a bolha aparece ao vivo; a direção vem do DB no `router.reload()`.
- **Caminho inbound fica byte-idêntico** ao original (não introduz coluna nova no fluxo que os testes legados de inbound cobrem → zero regressão).

## Testes
- ✅ `WhatsmeowOutboundFromMeRegressionTest` (novo, 4): outbound/sent + keyed no cliente; idempotência 2×=1 row; inbound não-regressão; fromMe em conversa existente não zera unread nem troca o nome.
- ✅ `WhatsmeowBroadcastFilterTest` (6): inclui o **`BROADCAST-006` que estava vermelho** desde o fix M1 de mídia (28/05) — realinhei o schema mínimo de `messages` do teste com as colunas reais (`media_*`).
- ✅ `WhatsmeowMediaInboundTest` (5): inalterado (baseline = modified).

## Fora de escopo (follow-ups conhecidos)
1. **Outbound pelo composer do oimpresso ainda quebrado no whatsmeow** (`InboxController::send` com gate hardcoded Baileys — [AUDITORIA-MIDIA-OUTBOUND P0 #3](memory/requisitos/Whatsapp/AUDITORIA-MIDIA-OUTBOUND-2026-05-28.md)). Enquanto isso, a captura via WhatsApp oficial (este PR) já dá visibilidade.
2. `sender_kind`/`sender_user_id` ficam NULL na captura (o daemon não sabe QUAL atendente respondeu) — enriquecer junto do fix do composer.
3. Testes `ProcessIncomingWebhookJobTest` e `MediaInboundProcessedTest` têm falhas **pré-existentes** (tabela `activity_log` ausente no schema do teste) — não tocadas aqui.

⚠️ Módulo Whatsapp é Tier 0 — **aguardando review/merge do Wagner**.

author: og-wura
body:
Close #173 

## Summary

This PR implements a **Grace Period for Reputation Updates** to prevent last-minute reputation manipulation in the TruthBounty voting system.

Previously, users could artificially increase their voting influence by updating their reputation immediately before participating in claim verification. This change introduces a configurable grace period window that restricts recently updated reputation scores from affecting voting power.

When a reputation update occurs within the configured grace period relative to a claim’s creation timestamp, the voter’s effective reputation defaults to the baseline score instead of using the updated value.

Default grace period: **2 days**

---

## Problem

Users were able to:

1. Create or identify an active claim
2. Boost their reputation score immediately before voting
3. Vote with inflated voting power
4. Manipulate weighted claim outcomes

This created a vulnerability in the reputation-weighted verification model.

---

## Solution

Implemented a symmetric grace period window around claim creation:

```solidity
timeSinceUpdate = |lastReputationUpdateTime - claimCreatedAt|
withinGracePeriod = timeSinceUpdate <= reputationUpdateGracePeriod
```

### Behavior

* Reputation updates within the grace period → use default reputation
* Reputation updates outside the grace period → use actual reputation

This applies independently per voter.

---

## Contracts Updated

### `IReputationOracle.sol`

* Added:

  * `getLastReputationUpdate(address user)`

### `MockReputationOracle.sol`

* Added timestamp tracking for reputation updates
* Added:

  * `lastUpdateTimestamp`
  * `getLastReputationUpdate()`

### `TruthBountyWeighted.sol`

* Added grace period configuration constants
* Added:

  * `reputationUpdateGracePeriod`
  * `_getReputationScoreWithGracePeriod()`
  * `setReputationUpdateGracePeriod()`
* Updated `vote()` to enforce grace period checks
* Added governance events and validation errors

---

## Governance Configuration

### Defaults

* Default: `2 days`
* Minimum: `1 hour`
* Maximum: `30 days`

### Governance Setter

```solidity
setReputationUpdateGracePeriod(uint256 newGracePeriod)
```

---

## Testing

### Unit Tests

Added comprehensive unit coverage for:

* Grace period configuration
* Last-minute boost prevention
* Reputation window calculations
* Multi-voter scenarios
* Boundary conditions
* Backward compatibility

### Invariant Tests

Added Foundry invariants ensuring:

* Grace period enforcement
* Symmetric window behavior
* Independent voter evaluation
* Effective stake integrity
* Governance bounds enforcement

---

## Security Impact

### Prevented Attacks

* Last-minute reputation boosts
* Coordinated voting manipulation
* Timing-based weighted voting exploits

### Guarantees

* Legitimate long-standing reputation remains valid
* Deterministic enforcement
* Governance-controlled but bounded configuration
* Full backward compatibility

---

## Backward Compatibility

This implementation maintains backward compatibility through graceful degradation using `try/catch` for oracle implementations that do not yet support reputation update timestamps.

Existing integrations remain functional.

---

## Performance Impact

* Minimal gas overhead (1–2 additional oracle reads per vote)
* Negligible storage increase
* No impact on settlement flow scalability

---

## Test Commands

```bash
npx hardhat test test/ReputationGracePeriod.test.ts

forge test test/invariant/ReputationGracePeriodInvariant.t.sol -v

npm run test
```

author: wikithoughts
body:
## Why

PR 5 of the v0.5.1 correctness sweep — embedding/LLM adapter robustness.

## Fixes

1. **Cloud HTTP clients had no request timeout** *(HIGH)* — OpenAI/Google embedders and OpenAI-compat/Anthropic LLMs used bare `reqwest::Client::new()`. A stalled connection (no FIN, no bytes) hung `embed()`/`generate()` forever — inside the indexing worker and web/MCP request paths. New shared `http_client()` (per crate) sets a request + 10s connect timeout (30s embed, 180s generate). It also replaces the Ollama `.unwrap_or_default()` builder, which silently produced a **no-timeout** client on build failure.
2. **Configured `base_url` ignored for cloud embedders** *(MEDIUM)* — `from_config` routed OpenAI/Google through `from_env_or_config`, which hardcoded `resolve_base_url(None)`, so a configured OpenAI-compatible gateway was dropped. `base_url` is now threaded through.
3. **Ollama swallowed `error` responses** *(MEDIUM)* — Ollama can return HTTP 200 then an `{"error": …}` body (e.g. OOM). `generate`/stream now bail with the error instead of returning an empty buffer as success; a stream ending without `done=true` is treated as a truncation error.

## Tests (new)

- `resp_captures_error_field`, `stream_chunk_captures_error_and_done` (Ollama wire contract).

## Deferred (ENHANCE — out of the chosen sweep scope)

Retry/backoff on 429/5xx, error-body truncation/scrub, and cloud `generate_stream` (SSE deltas) — tracked for a later "scale & retrieval quality" milestone.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check` ✓ · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✓ · `cargo test --workspace` ✓.

## Problem

Railpack detects the project as a staticfile app because of `index.html` in the root directory, installing Caddy instead of a JDK. This causes the build to fail with `sh: 1: javac: not found` (exit code 127) when the dashboard-configured build command `javac SkillBridgeServer.java` runs.

## Solution

Added `railpack.json` with `"provider": "java"` to the `SkillBridge Prototype v2` directory. This explicitly tells Railpack to use the Java provider regardless of file detection heuristics, ensuring a JDK is installed so both `javac` (build) and `java` (start) are available.

### Motivation

- Close a cross-tenant authorization bypass that allowed platform-tenant users with only `audit:operation:view` to request AI audit logs for arbitrary `tenantId` and access sensitive payloads.
- Prevent leakage of `request_payload_json` and `response_payload_json` by ensuring cross-tenant AI audit reads require proper wildcard/super-admin permission.

### Description

- Route `listAiCallLogs` through `resolveAuthorizedAiAuditTenantId(currentUser, tenantId)` instead of `resolveAuditTenantId(..., true)` to enforce AI-specific authorization rules.
- Remove the permissive `allowPlatformTenantScope` branch from the shared `resolveAuditTenantId` so that platform-tenant membership alone no longer grants cross-tenant audit reads.
- Tighten `isPlatformAuditUser` so it requires both the platform tenant (`DEFAULT_PUBLIC_TENANT_ID`) and wildcard permission (`"*"`).
- Add regression coverage in `SystemManagementAppServiceAiAuditTenantAuthorizationTest` to assert that a platform-scoped user without wildcard permission is denied when requesting another tenant's AI audit logs and that a wildcard platform admin can still filter by tenant.

author: sroussey
body:
## Summary

Two high-priority correctness fixes for `ServerCredentialStore` in `packages/storage/src/credentials/`.

### Fix 1 — `orphanReason` discriminator on orphan markers

`CredentialMetadataRow.orphanedAt` previously left operators guessing which failure branch produced a sticky orphan marker. This change adds an optional `orphanReason` field with one of three string-literal values:

- `"vault-write-failed"` — `put()` new-entry rollback path: metadata row written, `vault.setSecret` threw, and the follow-up `metadata.delete` also threw, so the pending row was rewritten as a sticky marker.
- `"metadata-commit-failed"` — `put()` new-entry commit path: `vault.setSecret` succeeded but the `pending: true -> false` flip threw, so the vault holds bytes the metadata can no longer expose.
- `"vault-delete-failed"` — `delete()` path (introduced by Fix 2 below): `metadata.delete` succeeded but `vault.deleteSecret` threw, so the vault may still hold bytes for a key no metadata row exposes.

A `OrphanReason` type alias is exported (`NonNullable<CredentialMetadataRow["orphanReason"]>`) for downstream consumers (reconciliation tooling, dashboards). The JSDoc on `orphanedAt` now points at `orphanReason` for branch semantics.

### Fix 2 — `delete()` is metadata-first; `deleteAll()` aggregates per-id failures

Previously, `delete()` called `vault.deleteSecret` first and `metadata.delete` second. If the vault call threw, the row remained visible to readers but its secret was already gone — a torn state. The new ordering is:

1. Read the existing row; return `false` if absent.
2. `await this.metadata.delete(id)` — failure bubbles, vault untouched.
3. `await this.vault.deleteSecret(id)` — failure triggers a best-effort orphan marker (`orphanReason: "vault-delete-failed"`) and throws a wrapped `Error` whose `cause` is the vault error.

`delete()` itself is now a thin wrapper around a private `deleteById(id, key)`, and `deleteAll()` iterates `scopedIds()` calling the same path. Per-id errors are collected and surfaced as an `AggregateError` once every id has been attempted, so one bad row no longer aborts cleanup of the rest. The failing ids retain sticky orphan markers for operator reconciliation; succeeding ids are fully removed.

`get()` and `has()` self-eviction calls (`await this.delete(key)` on expiry) are now wrapped in `try { ... } catch {}` so the new throwy `delete()` cannot turn an expired-read miss into a thrown error for callers — preserving the prior swallow-on-eviction behaviour.

## Backward compatibility

- `orphanReason` is **optional**. Legacy persisted rows with `orphanedAt` but no `orphanReason` continue to be treated as orphan markers (they are `pending: true`, so they were already invisible to readers). A regression test covers this case.
- **Behaviour change**: `deleteAll()` now throws `AggregateError` on per-id failure instead of throwing the first vault error and aborting the rest of the cleanup. Callers that previously only `await`-ed `deleteAll()` continue to see a throw on failure; callers that depended on early-abort semantics will need to update.
- **Behaviour change**: `delete()` now throws a wrapped `Error` (with `cause`) when `vault.deleteSecret` fails after metadata removal, instead of leaving a visible-but-empty row. The previous behaviour was a silent torn state; callers must now be prepared to handle this throw.

## Files modified

- `packages/storage/src/credentials/ServerCredentialStore.ts` — orphanReason field + OrphanReason export, both put() branches tagged, new private `deleteById()`, rewritten `delete()` / `deleteAll()`, swallow-wrapped self-eviction in `get()` / `has()`.
- `packages/storage/src/credentials/ServerCredentialStore.test.ts` — extended two existing orphan-path tests to assert `orphanReason`, added four new tests (`delete()` vault-failure, `delete()` metadata-failure, `deleteAll()` AggregateError, legacy orphan compatibility), updated the existing `delete removes both` test to verify metadata-before-vault ordering via spy call-order.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test packages/storage/src/credentials/ServerCredentialStore.test.ts` passes locally
- [ ] Type-check (`tsc --noEmit`) clean across the package
- [ ] Lint clean on the two touched files
- [ ] Spot-check downstream consumers of `CredentialMetadataRow` for compile compatibility with the new optional field
- [ ] Confirm no caller in the repo depends on `deleteAll()` throwing the first vault error rather than `AggregateError`

author: fengmk2
body:
## What

Lower the global `vp` version-retention limit from **5 → 3** across all three install paths that manage `~/.vite-plus`:

| Path | Location |
|------|----------|
| Rust (installer binary + `vp upgrade`) | `crates/vite_setup/src/lib.rs` — `MAX_VERSIONS_KEEP` |
| Shell bootstrap (`curl … \| sh`) | `packages/cli/install.sh` — `max_versions` |
| PowerShell bootstrap (`irm … \| iex`) | `packages/cli/install.ps1` — `$maxVersions` |

## Why

The `5` was an undocumented default. Keeping 3 cuts `~/.vite-plus` disk usage (~60–90MB instead of ~100–150MB) while still leaving rollback headroom. The cleanup logic is fully parameterized and the **protected-versions safeguard is unchanged** — the active and previous versions are never pruned regardless of the limit, so a downgrade/rollback target is always preserved.

Behavior change applies to **future** cleanup runs only (next install / `vp upgrade`); it does not retroactively prune existing machines.

## Also updated

- **RFCs** synced to the new number: `rfcs/global-cli-rust-binary.md`, `rfcs/upgrade-command.md` (incl. the disk-math line), `rfcs/windows-installer.md`.
- **Docs**: added a concise *Rollback* section to `docs/guide/upgrade.md` documenting the 3-version retention and `vp upgrade --rollback`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p vite_setup` → 14/14 passing. The existing `cleanup_old_versions` tests pass explicit `max_keep` values, so they exercise the generic logic independently of the constant.
- Doc/RFC edits are text-only.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Config and documentation only; cleanup semantics and protected-version safeguards are unchanged, so rollback safety is preserved with slightly less disk headroom.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Retained global `vp` versions drop from 5 → 3** everywhere post-install cleanup runs: `MAX_VERSIONS_KEEP` in `vite_setup` (used by `vp upgrade` and `vp-setup.exe`), plus `max_versions` / `$maxVersions` in `install.sh` and `install.ps1`. Pruning still only targets semver dirs under `~/.vite-plus`; **active and previous versions stay protected** for rollback—the limit only caps how many *other* old copies remain.
> 
> **Docs:** `docs/guide/upgrade.md` now documents `vp upgrade --check`, a **Rollback** subsection (`vp upgrade --rollback`, 3-version retention), and clarifies upgrade command examples.
> 
> **RFCs** (`global-cli-rust-binary`, `upgrade-command`, `windows-installer`) are updated to say “keep max 3” and the lower disk estimate (~60–90MB vs ~100–150MB). Behavior change applies on the **next** install or upgrade, not as a one-time migration on existing machines.
>

## Proposed amendment: Charter v1.3 → v1.4

**Date:** 2026-05-30
**Type:** Minor textual revision (per the README amendment procedure — `v1.x` for minor textual revisions).

### Rationale
Editorial pass for plainer, more commercial language aimed at external readers, plus two clarifications that reduce misreading by prospective B2B/B2G customers and partners. No change to any binding commitment.

### What changed
- Reframed **Purpose**, **Working as intended**, and **Failure mode** into plainer language.
- **Scope:** added a line noting AILedger supports certification partners with evidence but does not itself certify.
- **Use cases we decline** (header formerly "Customers we refuse"): added a lead line making explicit that AILedger sells across B2B and B2G and declines specific use cases, not sectors or company types. Header renamed (label only); board-review cross-reference updated to match.
- **Public commitment:** one sentence on why the revision history is open.
- Changelog entry + version bump to v1.4.

### What did NOT change — binding commitments, verified byte-identical to v1.3
- The four declined use-cases (predictive policing / social scoring / deceptive targeting; suppression-designed configs; paperwork-only; bad-faith litigation defense).
- The four refused features.
- Board-review triggers, exit conditions, STANDARDS anchoring, amendment rules.

### Approval
Per the Charter, amendment requires unanimous Board of Directors approval before merge.

author: union-crax
body:
The starter app was a two-screen mock (dashboard grid + a fake Now Playing
that only ticked a timer) and leaned on remote artwork that needs a network.
This reworks it into a cohesive, Apple Music–inspired 10-foot experience that
is fully self-contained and genuinely plays audio.

UI / UX
- New persistent left sidebar shell: Listen Now, Browse, Radio, Library, Search.
- Shelf-based browsing with a featured hero, pure-black Apple palette, and
  consistent D-pad focus treatments (lift + play badge, accent highlight).
- Always-on Now Playing bar plus an immersive full-screen player that slides up,
  with a D-pad scrubber (◀/▶ to seek), shuffle/repeat, volume, and time-synced
  lyrics that scale and auto-scroll.
- Live search across songs and playlists.

It actually works
- ToneAudioEngine: a small real-time PCM synth on AudioTrack. Each track's mood
  maps to a chord progression with pads, arpeggio, bass, optional beat, and a
  stereo feedback delay — pressing Play produces real sound, no network/media.
- Procedurally generated gradient cover art (deterministic per item), so the UI
  looks designed and loads instantly offline.
- PlayerViewModel: a single activity-scoped source of truth for queue, position
  clock, and transport, shared by the bar and the full player. Hardware media
  keys are routed to it; audio pauses when the app goes to the background.

Cleanup
- Remove navigation-compose and Coil; drop the old Screen/AppNavigation,
  DashboardScreen, and NowPlayingViewModel.
- Expand MockData into a catalogue with stations, playlists, and search, and
  rewrite the unit tests around it (catalogue integrity, lookups, search): 18 tests.

author: blackgauss
body:
## Summary

Combined PR 0 + PR 1 from the sandbox infrastructure plan into a single PR for faster iteration.

## PR 0 — MCP Gap Fillings (7 new tools)

All tools call existing `CaasClient` methods — zero dispatcher code changes needed:

| Tool | Endpoint | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `browse_files` | GET /v1/host-files | List host directory files |
| `get_job_by_id` | GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} | Fetch single job record |
| `delete_template` | DELETE /v1/templates/{id} | Remove a template |
| `check_image` | GET /v1/images/check | Verify image availability |
| `staging_list` | GET /v1/staging | List staging areas |
| `staging_create` | POST /v1/staging | Create staging area |
| `staging_delete` | DELETE /v1/staging/{id} | Remove staging area |

## PR 1 — Sandbox Infrastructure

### Concurrency Landmine Fixes

- **`resource_type: str = 'cpu'`** on `JobRecord\) — deterministic slot tracking even if container is obliterated
- **`sandbox_hydrate_container()`** — scan for `caas.sandbox=true` containers at startup, acquire correct slot (GPU/CPU)
- **`_release_sandbox_slots()`** — uses `job.resource_type` instead of inspecting Docker at release time
- **`_enrich_job_data()`** hook — releases slot when sandbox container exits or is removed out-of-band

### New Endpoints

- **`POST /v1/sandbox`** — create persistent sandbox (acquire slot → pre\_create → run container → register → release slot)
- **`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/exec`** — execute commands incrementally inside sandbox

### Background Reaper

- Checks every 60 seconds, kills sandboxes idle beyond `SANDBOX_TTL_SECS` (default 30 min)
- Releases slots, triggers `on_job_complete`, logs reaped sandboxes

### Lifecycle

- `lifespan()` recovers sandbox containers on restart, starts schedule scanner + reaper task
- `DELETE` handler releases sandbox slot + triggers `on_job_complete` hook

## Tests

- 26 new sandbox-specific tests covering: creation, exec, slot lifecycle, enrichment exit detection, resource_type storage, slot exhaustion
- All 208 tests pass

author: andrijapanicsb
body:
Companion main/4.23 PR: #13270

This PR is intended to keep the 4.22 and main branches aligned for the VDDK-to-RBD import feature.

### Description

This PR extends the existing VMware-to-KVM VDDK import flow with Ceph RBD support, while preserving the current VDDK/QCOW2 behaviour.

The existing VDDK/QCOW2 writer remains supported in both existing modes:

- With `forceconverttopool=true`, CloudStack continues to let `virt-v2v` write QCOW2 output directly into the selected supported primary storage pool using `-o local -os <pool-path> -of qcow2`.
- With `forceconverttopool=false`, CloudStack continues to use the staged flow: `virt-v2v` writes finalized QCOW2 disks to temporary conversion storage, and the import step then moves/copies those disks to the final destination pool.

This change adds a destination-aware writer model for VDDK imports. The current file/QCOW2 writer path remains, and a new Ceph RBD/raw writer path is added. This gives the VDDK import flow a cleaner foundation for adding more destination-specific writers later.

For Ceph RBD, two modes are supported:

1. Direct RBD mode

   When `usevddk=true`, `forceconverttopool=true`, and `convertinstancepoolid` points to an RBD primary storage pool, CloudStack can write the VMware disk data directly into raw RBD images.

   This path does not use the normal `virt-v2v -o local -of qcow2` writer, because RBD is not a local filesystem target. Instead, the conversion host:

   - exposes the VMware source disks through VDDK/`nbdkit`
   - writes the data directly into raw RBD images using `qemu-img convert`
   - runs guest finalization in place on the newly-created RBD images using `virt-v2v-in-place`, or `virt-v2v --in-place` when supported

   The in-place finalization happens only on the destination RBD images. The VMware source disks are not modified.

2. Staged RBD mode

   When `usevddk=true` and `forceconverttopool=false`, RBD can still be used as the final destination through the existing staged model.

   In this mode:

   - regular VDDK/`virt-v2v` creates finalized QCOW2 disks on temporary conversion storage
   - the import step then converts/copies those QCOW2 disks into raw RBD images

   This mode does not require in-place `virt-v2v`, because regular `virt-v2v` has already finalized the guest while creating the temporary QCOW2 disks.

Direct RBD mode requires newer conversion-host tooling. The practical recommended baseline is EL9-family KVM hosts, such as Oracle Linux 9, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 9, or RHEL 9, and Ubuntu 24.04-style hosts where `virt-v2v-in-place` or `virt-v2v --in-place` is available. EL8 and Ubuntu 22.04-style hosts should use staged RBD import unless compatible in-place tooling has been explicitly installed and detected by CloudStack.

The implementation adds KVM host capability detection for:

- VDDK RBD direct import support
- in-place `virt-v2v` support
- `qemu-img` RBD support
- qemu-based RBD copy support

Direct RBD mode is rejected early when the selected conversion host does not support the required in-place finalization path. Staged RBD remains available in that case.

### Types of changes

- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] Enhancement (improves an existing feature and functionality)
- [ ] Cleanup (Code refactoring and cleanup, that may add test cases)
- [ ] Build/CI
- [ ] Test (unit or integration test code)

### Feature/Enhancement Scale or Bug Severity

#### Feature/Enhancement Scale

- [ ] Major
- [x] Minor

#### Bug Severity

- [ ] BLOCKER
- [ ] Critical
- [ ] Major
- [ ] Minor
- [ ] Trivial

### Screenshots (if appropriate):

N/A

### How Has This Been Tested?

Focused compile and unit test coverage was run for the changed API/core/server/KVM paths, including:

```text
git diff --check
mvn -pl api,core -am -DskipTests -Dcheckstyle.skip=true compile
mvn -pl engine/orchestration -am -DskipTests -Dcheckstyle.skip=true compile
mvn -pl plugins/hypervisors/kvm -am -DskipTests -Dcheckstyle.skip=true compile
mvn -pl plugins/hypervisors/kvm -am -Dtest=LibvirtCheckConvertInstanceCommandWrapperTest,LibvirtConvertInstanceCommandWrapperTest,LibvirtImportConvertedInstanceCommandWrapperTest -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test
mvn -pl server -am -Dtest=UnmanagedVMsManagerImplTest# -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test
```

The tests cover direct RBD host capability checks, rejection when direct RBD support is missing, staged RBD destination handling, RBD destination pool type propagation, RBD disk metadata, and server-side validation for RBD storage pools.

#### How did you try to break this feature and the system with this change?

Negative tests were added for hosts without direct VDDK/RBD support, and staged RBD import is validated separately so that lack of in-place `virt-v2v` blocks only direct RBD mode, not RBD import as a whole. Existing VDDK/QCOW2 direct and staged flows are kept on the existing writer path unless the selected forced conversion pool is RBD.
