body:
## Summary

Builds the **Repeat-Offender Tracker** — the persistent layer that turns one-shot drift signals from `#2` (drift detector) + `#11` (CheckID) into *"this keeps happening"* intel across sessions. Input to `#13` take-a-hint escalation + orchestrator prioritization.

Signal-agnostic. Pure-core + thin FS-shim. Stores an append-only event log at `.faf-drift-index.json`. Decay is timestamp filtering on **query** — not lossy mutation; the same log is queryable at any window width.

## The locked spec (every field traceable)

Spec source: `~/PLANET-FAF/docs/GROK-FAF-MCP-1.5-CODING-SESSION-BREAKDOWN-2026-05-30.md` §#12.

| Lock | Implementation | Test assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Persistent index, per-slot drift-count | ✅ JSON event log + `computeRepeatOffenders` | ENGINE: "repeated recordDrift increments count" |
| Decay over time (e.g., last 30 days) | ✅ rolling window on query, default 30, configurable | AERO: "decay drops outside-window events" |
| Query: `getRepeatOffenders(): { slot, count, last_drift }[]` | ✅ exact shape | AERO: "output shape matches spec §#12 exactly" |
| Blocked by `#2` (drift detection signals) | ✅ both `#2` and `#11` consumed via bridges | ENGINE: bridge tests |
| Files: `src/orchestrator/repeat-offender.ts` + `tests/wjttc-repeat-offender.test.ts` | ✅ verbatim paths | — |
| WJTTC tier: **ENGINE + AERO (multi-session simulation)** | ✅ AERO suite includes 3-session-across-30-days simulation | AERO: "multi-session simulation" |

## The signal-agnostic call (HOW)

Spec says *"incremented when #2 detects drift on that slot"* but `#2`'s output is `{ repeated_anchors: string[] }` — phrases, not slot identifiers. `#11`'s `ContradictionReport` has crisp slot semantics (each `contradiction.check` is naturally a slot).

**Resolution:** the tracker is signal-agnostic — accepts any string slot identifier. **Two bridges** make consumption explicit, namespace-separated so they can't collide:

```ts
recordFromDriftSignal(signal)         // slot = `anchor:${repeated_anchor}`
recordFromContradictionReport(report) // slot = `check:${contradiction.check}`
```

Both bridges silently no-op when the input has zero items — no empty file gets created just for being called (caught + fixed mid-iteration; see below).

## Storage call

Spec listed three options as TBD. I chose **dedicated `.faf-drift-index.json`** because:
- inline `.fafm` metadata → couples telemetry with memory content (wrong layer)
- registry layer → over-engineering for MVP
- dedicated JSON → debuggable, recomputable, no schema dependency

Details:
- Cwd-relative by default · configurable via constructor
- Append-only JSON array of `{ slot, timestamp }`
- Atomic writes via temp-file + rename
- Visible (not gitignored) — receipts > silent state, same logic as `soul.fafm`
- Tracker writes only when something is actually recorded (silent no-op on empty bridges)

## Pure-core + FS-shim split

```ts
// Pure — testable without FS, deterministic for fixed `now`
function computeRepeatOffenders(events: DriftEvent[], options): RepeatOffender[]

// Thin FS wrapper — knows how to read/write the on-disk format
class RepeatOffenderTracker {
  recordDrift(slot, timestamp?)
  recordFromDriftSignal(signal)
  recordFromContradictionReport(report, timestamp?)
  getRepeatOffenders(options?)
}
```

Most logic stays testable without FS. AERO determinism test exercises `computeRepeatOffenders` directly — no temp dirs, no file I/O, repeatable across runs.

## Ranking (useful for downstream `#13`)

`count desc, then last_drift desc` — highest count first, ties broken by most-recent recurrence. Newest-recurring offenders surface at the top. Proven by ENGINE test "ranking: highest count first; ties broken by most-recent last_drift first".

## Changes

- `src/orchestrator/repeat-offender.ts` (NEW) — 227 lines
- `tests/wjttc-repeat-offender.test.ts` (NEW) — 337 lines

## One real bug caught + fixed mid-iteration (visible, not hidden)

Both bridges initially wrote the event log even when the input had zero items — creating an empty file just for being called. Caught by the explicit BRAKE tests for empty-input no-op behavior. Fix: track appended count, skip write when zero. Mirrors `detectFafmDrift`'s silent-on-clean rhythm.

**The test caught the bug, not me.** Same pattern as the bugs caught in `#11` (SEMVER regex, coverage honesty) — BRAKE/AERO tests earning their keep across the 1.5 substrate.

## Test Plan

- [x] Tests pass locally — **24/24 new** tests pass (37 expect() calls)
- [x] BRAKE (8) — missing file · corrupt JSON · non-array JSON · partially-corrupt log (drops corrupt, keeps valid) · empty-slot rejected · invalid-timestamp rejected · bridge no-ops × 2
- [x] ENGINE (8) — record + query · increment same slot · ranking · minCount filter · both bridges + namespace-collision proof · output shape spec-verbatim
- [x] AERO (6) — compute determinism · persistence round-trip (two tracker instances, one file) · decay drops outside-window · decay does NOT mutate log · multi-session simulation (3 sessions, 30 days, mixed signal sources) · empty log → empty array
- [x] TYRE/PIT (2) — pass-through (local FS only, no cred; storage = JSON, no schema gate)
- [x] No regression — full suite **314 pass / 1 skip / 1 todo / 0 fail** (was 290 → +24 new, zero regression)
- [x] Tested with Grok/xAI integration — N/A (library code; consumed by future orchestrator/telemetry)
- [x] No breaking changes — strictly additive

## What is NOT in this PR (scope discipline)

- **`#13` take-a-hint escalation logic** — blocked on this; separate ship
- **`#10` orchestrator tool** that surfaces repeat-offenders to the agent — separate ship
- **`#7` wiring drift detection → tracker invocation (telemetry + receipts)** — separate ship
- **MCP tool surface** for the tracker — library code first, surface decision later

One concern per PR per `[[feedback-pr-rhythm-beats-branch-only]]`.

## Related artifacts

- `memory/grok-drift-requirements.md` — Grok's drift-management spec (drift = degradation + confident-wrongness; the tracker's "recurring slot" lens is one slice)
- `memory/silent-drift-equals-fail-equals-forbidden.md` — recurring drift is silent-drift's compound interest; the tracker makes it loud
- `memory/build-precedent-understand-gather.md` — gather → propose → code applied, with the spec ambiguity surfaced before implementation

## Related Issues

Task `#12` from the 1.5 coding session breakdown. Unblocks `#13` (take-a-hint escalation) and provides the persistent layer `#7` (telemetry) will write to.

author: xiayan0118
body:
## Summary
Fixes the B200 partial-M MXFP4 MoE failure on the NGC 26.04 / CUDA 13.2 stack **without** the `expandable_segments` allocator mask.

For partial-M tiles (`M < BLOCK_M`, non-ragged, non-gather) the swizzled **dense X TMA** over-fetches past the X allocation — benign under CUDA 13.0's layout, unmapped under 13.2 → illegal memory access. The fix keeps the numerically-correct dense X TMA path and zero-pads the X allocation up to `BLOCK_M` rows so the over-fetch stays mapped, then restores any stride-0 broadcast dims. Logical `M` is unchanged (only `M` output rows are produced); X values are plain row-major so the pad is trivial.

```python
if a_has_tma and ragged_dimension != "K" and not has_gather_tma and M < opt_flags.block_m:
    a_data = a.storage.data
    padded = torch.nn.functional.pad(a_data, (0, 0, 0, opt_flags.block_m - M))
    # F.pad makes the tensor contiguous, dropping the stride-0 broadcast dims from the
    # 2D->3D canonicalization; carry the zeros over so batch broadcast still aliases slice 0.
    restored = [0 if s == 0 else ps for s, ps in zip(a_data.stride(), padded.stride())]
    a.storage.data = padded.as_strided(padded.shape, restored)
```

## Why not the pointer-path fallback
An earlier approach set `a_has_tma = False` for partial-M (route X values through the pointer path). But the swizzled **X-scale** stays on TMA, and its row offset in `_p_matmul` branches on `X_TMA_MODE` (`"dense"` vs `else`). Switching X off TMA silently selects the wrong `off_m_scale` formula → values multiplied by the wrong MX scale block → TP/partial-M MXFP4 MoE diverged (`test_dist/models/test_openai_multi.py::test_mxfp4_moe`, cosine ~0.84). Padding keeps the value+scale offsets consistent.

## Stride-0 broadcast (Bugbot r3329397531)
A 2D X canonicalized to 3D gets a leading `stride[0]=0` (batch broadcast). A plain `F.pad` returns a contiguous tensor (`stride[0]=BLOCK_M*K`), which would make the dense-TMA descriptor read real (OOB) memory for `off_x_z>0` instead of re-aliasing slice 0. The `as_strided` step above carries the zero strides back so broadcast semantics are preserved.

## Validation (B200, NGC 26.04, CUDA 13.2, default allocator, no `expandable_segments`)
- **single-GPU** `test/models/test_openai.py::TestOpenAI::test_mxfp4_moe`: pass, no IMA
- **TP** `test_dist/models/test_openai_multi.py::TestOpenAIDistributed::test_mxfp4_moe`: pass (was cosine 0.84)
- **full `test/models/` suite** (cumulative, the IMA only surfaces cumulatively): 573 passed, 0 IMA / 0 CUDA errors (only a pre-existing unrelated `test_kimi_k25` cosine-margin failure)
- **`triton_kernels` `tests/test_matmul.py -k batched`** (regression gate for the broadcast path): **648 passed, 1128 skipped, 0 failed**
- **unit check** (broadcast preservation): after the fix the padded X keeps `stride[0]=0`, pads M to `BLOCK_M`, leaves the first M rows intact, and `off_x_z>0` aliases slice 0

## Notes
Supersedes the reverted PR #1 approach (pointer fallback). Draft for review.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Mutates activation storage in-place on a hot matmul path for a narrow partial-M + dense TMA case; logic is localized but correctness depends on padding and stride-0 broadcast handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **illegal memory access** on CUDA 13.2 (e.g. B200 / NGC 26.04) when **MXFP4 MoE** matmul uses the **persistent dense X TMA** with **`M < BLOCK_M`**, by **zero-padding** the activation buffer’s **M** rows up to **`BLOCK_M`** before building the TMA descriptor—instead of disabling TMA for X.
> 
> **`_pad_partial_m_dense_x`** extends **`a.storage.data`** so swizzled full-tile loads stay inside real memory; padded rows are zeros and do not affect the result. Hardware **OOB fill** is not used for **16U4_ALIGN16B** MXFP4. When the batch dimension is **stride-0 broadcast**, only the real **`[M, K]`** slice is padded and **`as_strided`** restores **`stride(0)=0`** so batch aliasing is unchanged after **`F.pad`** makes the tensor contiguous.
> 
> The hook runs when **`a_has_tma`**, not ragged-K, no gather TMA, and **`M < opt_flags.block_m`**, immediately before **`make_tma`**—keeping **dense `X_TMA_MODE`** aligned with **X-scale TMA** offsets (avoids the wrong-scale bug from a pointer fallback).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ee3f127db22121476fa181207ba989fa5c057880. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

<!-- First of all, THANK YOU for your contribution. -->

## Changes Proposed:

This PR proposes changes to:
- [x] Core (units, players, creatures, game systems).
- [ ] Scripts (bosses, spell scripts, creature scripts).
- [ ] Database (SAI, creatures, etc).

Reorders `sScriptMgr->OnBattlefieldWarEnd(...)` to fire **before** `OnBattleEnd(...)` inside `Battlefield::EndBattle`, and updates the inline doc on `BATTLEFIELDHOOK_ON_WAR_END` to match the new timing.

Until now, the hook fired *after* the virtual `OnBattleEnd`, at which point `BattlefieldWG::OnBattleEnd` had already iterated `PlayersInWar` to hand out rewards and then cleared both teams' sets. Subscribers that needed to enumerate who actually participated in the war (e.g. to restore per-player state for crossfaction modules) had no authoritative source to iterate, and were forced to mirror `PlayersInWar` themselves through `OnBattlefieldPlayerJoinWar` / `OnBattlefieldPlayerLeaveWar` / `OnBattlefieldPlayerLeaveZone`.

After this PR, subscribers can read `bf->GetPlayersInWarSet(team)` directly inside `OnBattlefieldWarEnd` and drop the parallel state. mod-cfbg's WG crossfaction support is the first beneficiary (paired PR: azerothcore/mod-cfbg#154).

#### Behavioral note

`OnBattleEnd`'s reward distribution still runs in the same `EndBattle` call, just after the hook instead of before. Reward effects are unaffected by subscribers that mutate player faction inside the hook:

- `SPELL_VICTORY_REWARD` / `SPELL_DEFEAT_REWARD` / `SPELL_ESSENCE_OF_WINTERGRASP` / tower spells: self-cast, faction-neutral effects.
- `AreaExploredOrEventHappens(13183 | 13181)`: keys on whether the player already holds the quest, not on current faction.
- Post-capture phase-shift aura: keys on `DefenderTeam`, not on player faction.

### AI-assisted Pull Requests

>
> Contributors are also expected to fully understand the changes they are submitting and must be able to explain and justify those changes when requested by maintainers.

## Tests Performed:

- [ ] Tested in-game by other community members/someone else other than the author/has been live on production servers.
- [x] This pull request requires further testing and may have edge cases to be tested.


## How to Test the Changes:

- [ ] This pull request can be tested by following the reproduction steps provided in the linked issue
- [x] This pull request requires further testing. Provide steps to test your changes. If it requires any specific setup e.g multiple players please specify it as well.

1. Build the core with this PR applied. No module changes are required for core-only verification; for the end-to-end test, build with the paired mod-cfbg PR (azerothcore/mod-cfbg#154).
2. Start Wintergrasp and let a war run to completion. Test both timer-expiry (defender wins by clock) and an attacker-wins (relic captured) scenario.
3. Confirm victory/defeat rewards, win-quest credits, damaged/destroyed tower spells, and the post-capture phase-shift aura are still applied to every war participant. Compare honor and Wintergrasp Mark of Honor tallies to a master baseline if available.

author: ameyashan
body:
## Summary
Adds a lightweight "Another angle" feature that lets users quickly rewrite existing drafts with preset directives (shorter, different angle, more founder-like, etc.) without re-running research or email lookup. This complements the full draft pipeline with a fast in-place rewrite capability.

## Key Changes

- **New `redraft()` API in `src/lib/claude.ts`**: Implements draft rewriting with a single directive while preserving facts, the ask, and sender voice. Includes the same anti-AI scrub as fresh drafts to prevent tells from reappearing.

- **New `signOffInstruction()` helper**: Extracted sign-off logic so fresh drafts, humanize rewrites, and redrafts all sign off consistently. Appends sender's LinkedIn URL to email signatures (on its own line under the name) but skips it for LinkedIn/X DMs.

- **Added `sender_linkedin` field to `DraftInput`**: Captures the sender's LinkedIn URL from their profile for inclusion in email signatures.

- **New `/api/compose/redraft` endpoint** (`src/app/api/compose/redraft/route.ts`): Lightweight POST handler that accepts a draft body, channel, and directive, then returns the rewritten subject/body. Validates inputs and applies the same user context as other compose endpoints.

- **"Another angle" UI component** (`src/app/app/compose/page.tsx`): 
  - New `AnotherAngle` button with dropdown menu of 5 preset directives (another angle, shorter, more founder-like, warmer, more formal)
  - Integrated into both PersonPackage and JobPackage email cards
  - Shows loading state and error feedback from the run store
  - Calls `regenerateDraft()` to swap rewritten copy into the run's drafts

- **Run store updates** (`src/lib/runs-store.ts`):
  - Added `redrafting` and `redraftError` fields to track rewrite state per channel
  - New `regenerateDraft()` function that hits the redraft endpoint and updates drafts in place via `upsertDraft()`
  - Helper `upsertDraft()` to replace or insert a draft for a channel while preserving array identity

## Implementation Details

- Redrafts preserve all concrete facts, names, and the single ask—they never invent new claims or references
- The same `antiAiWritingGuide()` linter runs on redrafts as on fresh drafts; if violations are found, `humanizeDraft()` attempts a fix
- LinkedIn URLs are only appended to email signatures, not to LinkedIn/X DM sign-offs
- The UI channel names ('email', 'linkedin', 'x') are mapped to API channel names ('email', 'linkedin', 'x_dm') for consistency with the draft pipeline

author: abdelrahmen-zaouidi
body:
## Summary

Senior-engineer security audit of `vision_based_access_control` plus a 15-commit
remediation that resolves every CRITICAL and HIGH finding and most MEDIUM/LOW ones.

`main` was orphan-reset before this PR was opened to remove biometric data and
admin password hashes (`app.db`, `face_recog.log`, `face_engine.log`,
`encodings_report.json`) from git history. **Any data that ever lived in the
pre-PR history must be treated as permanently compromised** — anyone who
cloned before the rewrite still has copies.

See [`AUDIT_REPORT.md`](AUDIT_REPORT.md) for the full audit. Highlights below.

## Critical + high findings resolved

| Finding | Fix | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| C1 Leaked `app.db` / face logs / encodings in history | Orphan-reset of `main` | (pre-PR) |
| C2 No CSRF protection on any POST endpoint | Flask-WTF CSRFProtect + tokens in 13 forms + jQuery X-CSRFToken auto-attach | `b2a2ace` |
| C3 Hardcoded `admin/adminpass` auto-created on first run | Removed; replaced with `--bootstrap-admin` CLI reading env vars | `d86fddd` |
| C4 `Flask debug=True` on `host=0.0.0.0` | Debug off; HOST/PORT env-driven, default `127.0.0.1` | `d86fddd` |
| H1 Path traversal in `enroll_person_image` | `werkzeug.secure_filename` + `pathlib` | `86a9352` |
| H2 `SECRET_KEY='dev-secret-key'` fallback | Removed; `create_app` raises if env var missing | `adefbd4` |
| H3 `pickle.loads` on DB-stored face encodings (RCE) | `numpy.tobytes`/`frombuffer` with shape validation | `c05ca42` |
| H4 No brute-force protection on `/login` | Flask-Limiter: 5/min, 20/h | `3b206a3` |
| H5 No session-cookie security flags | `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` by default | `3b206a3` |

Plus: `.gitignore`, pinned `requirements.txt`, security headers (X-Frame-Options
/ X-Content-Type-Options / Referrer-Policy), `README.md`, Apache 2.0 LICENSE,
GitHub Actions CI (ruff + smoke), non-root Docker setup, SECURITY.md,
CONTRIBUTING.md.

## ⚠️ Breaking changes for existing deployments

1. **Pickle → numpy encoding format**. Existing `app.db` rows with enrolled
   personnel won't deserialize. Re-enroll personnel after upgrade, or write
   a one-off migration that `pickle.loads`-then-`set_encoding`-then-commits.
2. **Server binds `127.0.0.1` by default** (was `0.0.0.0`). Set `HOST=0.0.0.0`
   for LAN access.
3. **No default admin auto-created.** Run `python run.py --bootstrap-admin`
   once with `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME` and `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` set.
4. **`SECRET_KEY` env var is now required.** App refuses to start without it.

## Health score (estimated)

| Dimension | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Security | 2 / 10 | 7 / 10 |
| Maintainability | 4 | 5 |
| Professionalism | 1 | 8 |
| Documentation | 1 | 8 |
| Deployment readiness | 1 | 7 |
| **Overall** | **2.5** | **6.5** |

## Recommended next steps (out of scope for this PR)

1. Rotate any credentials that ever lived in the original git history.
2. Re-enroll personnel after deploying (pickle → numpy format change).
3. Add unit tests for `engine._run_recognition_core` decision branches.
4. Refactor `engine.py` (544 lines) into `preprocess.py` / `detector.py` / `decision_loop.py` once tests exist.
5. Lock-guard `RECOG_STATE` in `authorization/routes.py` (race condition).
6. Add a Content-Security-Policy header tuned to the dashboard's CDN origins.
7. Migrate to Postgres + Redis for multi-user / multi-worker deployments.

## Verification

- CI: `lint` and `smoke-import` jobs green.
- `ruff check access_control` exits 0 on the pinned `ruff==0.6.9`.
- No merge conflicts vs `main`.

author: joaoh82
body:
## What & why

The SQL playground (`sqlrite-desktop`) read its `ask` config exclusively from `SQLRITE_LLM_API_KEY` in the environment. Launched from Finder / the Dock — which don't inherit a shell's env — the **Ask…** button just errored. This ports the in-app settings pattern we shipped for the journal example app ([SQLR-41 / #145](https://github.com/joaoh82/rust_sqlite/pull/145)) into the playground, so a user can paste a key in a ⚙ dialog and it persists across restarts. Env var still works as a fallback for existing dev workflows.

## Changes

**Rust (`desktop/src-tauri/`)**
- `src/settings.rs` (new) — `AskSettings` persisted as JSON to `$APP_DATA/com.sqlrite.desktop/settings.json`; scrubbed `AskSettingsDto` (`has_api_key: bool` — the raw key never crosses to the webview); three-valued `AskSettingsUpdate`; `build_ask_config()` (prefers saved key, falls back to `SQLRITE_LLM_API_KEY`); `settings_path()`. 5 unit tests.
- `src/main.rs` — `AppState` gains `settings_path` (resolved from `app_data_dir()` in `setup`); `ask_sql` builds config from saved settings instead of `AskConfig::from_env()`; new `get_ask_settings` / `update_ask_settings` commands registered.

**Frontend (`desktop/src/`)**
- `lib/SettingsPanel.svelte` (new) — gear-modal, rewritten in the playground's plain-CSS idiom (the playground uses global `app.css` vars, not Tailwind like the journal). Password field, model, max-tokens, "Clear saved key", status line, Esc-to-close, security note.
- `lib/api.ts` (new) — `getAskSettings` / `updateAskSettings` wrappers with null→absent normalisation.
- `App.svelte` — ⚙ header button mounts the panel. `app.css` — `.settings-button` rule.

**`desktop/README.md`** (new) — "Configuring `ask`" section + security note (no README existed).

## Deviations from the journal port
- `build_ask_config` is **unconditional** — the desktop crate has no `ask` feature gate and always builds the engine with `ask` on (matching the existing unconditional `ask_sql`). So all 5 tests always run.
- `tempdir()` in tests uses a process-wide `AtomicU64` counter instead of `subsec_nanos()` — the journal's version has a latent parallel-run collision that surfaced here (fixed; see follow-up).

## Test plan — all green locally
- `npm install` + `npm run build` (vite) + `npm run check` (svelte-check: 0 errors/warnings)
- `cargo test -p sqlrite-desktop` → **5/5 pass**, stable across 3 runs
- `cargo build -p sqlrite-desktop --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` → new code has 0 warnings (remaining clippy hits are pre-existing)

Not verified: live end-to-end LLM call (needs a real key + network) and the literal Finder-launch scenario (headless run). Both are covered indirectly by unit tests + the binary compiling against the embedded `dist/`.

## Follow-up
The journal app's `examples/desktop-journal/src-tauri/src/settings.rs` has the identical flaky `tempdir()` — worth a small ticket to port this fix back.

**Phase 8** is the only one left — parity QA on a deploy preview, **your live Stripe card test**, then the `netlify.toml` flip (remove the Vite SPA-fallback rewrites, keep the webhook rewrite + headers, re-point the immutable-cache header at `/_next/static/*` — all recorded in the plan). author: theteepeenetwork
body:
## Summary

A code- and schema-grounded **vendor onboarding audit** (Phases 1–5 of the brief), plus the implementation of its **highest impact-to-risk improvement**: vendors can now declare a service's **capacity, logistics and on-site requirements** — fields that previously could not be represented at all.

### 1. Audit — `VENDOR_ONBOARDING_AUDIT.md`
Every finding is verified against the live schema and the controllers/views/models. Highlights:
- **Taxonomy (Phase 4): strong** — data-driven `categories` tree (23 top-level + ~1,400 children, 3 levels); no code change needed to add supplier types.
- **Pricing (Phase 2): 6 structured models** present (guest/duration/package/quantity/public-pitch/corporate + travel). **Absent:** custom-quote/POA, session rate, seasonal, venue-based, true multi-day.
- **Configuration (Phase 3): major gaps** — no capacity, no requirements (power/water/access/indoor-outdoor), no setup/breakdown, and **availability is unmanageable** (`addAvailability()` is unrouted, `unavailable_dates` has no UI, calendar is read-only).
- **Discovery (Phase 5): thin** — only category + keyword + sort; no price/capacity/location/date/event-type filters.
- A prioritised 7-item roadmap (impact ÷ risk) is included.

### 2. Implementation — Service requirements, capacity & logistics (roadmap item #1)
Chosen because it is **additive, backwards-compatible, and unblocks the most supplier types** (food trucks, mobile bars, fairground rides, inflatables, marquees, AV/production, security, workshops).

- **`database_service_requirements.sql`** — idempotent, self-contained migration adding `min/max_capacity`, `setup_minutes`, `breakdown_minutes`, `min_notice_days`, `space_required`, `indoor_outdoor` (enum), and `power/water/vehicle_access/equipment` flags to `services`. All nullable/defaulted → existing rows unaffected. Added to the README import order.
- **`ServiceModel`** — new columns in `allowedFields`.
- **`Service_Controller::update()`** — captures + validates the new fields (`is_natural` / `in_list` / length rules + a max≥min capacity check).
- **`service_edit.php`** — new "Logistics, Capacity & Requirements" section.
- **`service_view.php`** — customer-facing "Good to know" panel that shows only the fields a vendor filled in.

## Testing
- `php -l` clean on all modified PHP.
- Migration applies cleanly and is **idempotent** on re-run.
- **Browser-verified end-to-end:** vendor edits a service, sets capacity/logistics/requirements → "Service updated successfully" → values persist in the DB → customer detail page renders the "Good to know" block (capacity 30–250, outdoor-only, space, 14-day notice, setup/breakdown, mains power/water/vehicle access).

## Scope note
This PR delivers the audit + the first (lowest-risk) implementation increment. The remaining roadmap items — **custom-quote pricing**, **discovery filters**, **specific event-type taxonomy**, **availability management UI**, and **seasonal/venue/multi-day pricing** — each touch core flows or involve product decisions and are best done as their own focused PRs. The new fields are currently captured on the **edit** form; wiring them into the multi-step **create** flow is the natural immediate follow-up.

author: densanon-devs
body:
## Summary

11 probes mapping the 4 failure modes from **arXiv 2605.27461** (Pi0.5 deployment at Siemens packaging, May 2026) onto narrative-state edge cases. Designed as PROBES — passing means the FactLedger handles the case; failing means a real gap is exposed and pinned as a RED tripwire.

## Mapping

| VLA failure | Narrative analog probed |
|---|---|
| 1. Bag contents remain (65%) — small accessories hidden under manual | Buried sub-detail retrievability |
| 2. Multiple bags grasped (23%) — indistinct borders | NPC attribution preserved across near-identical facts |
| 3. Bag not fully inserted (15%) — occluded view | Ambiguous-location facts; NLI specificity-mismatch handling |
| 4. Poor grasps (15%) — no recovery | Malformed input (empty / non-str / oversized) handled gracefully |
| 5. (Meta) — no recovery in paper | NLI retry path actually engages on real contradiction, not on near-paraphrase |

## Results: 9/11 pass, 2 expose real gaps

**PASS — FactLedger already handles (9 tests):**
- VLA-1 main: compound fact sub-detail retrievable when sub-detail is equal-weight with primary
- VLA-2 ×2: NPC attribution preserved + restrict_to_npc isolation
- VLA-3 base: ambiguous-location text stored verbatim
- VLA-4 ×3: empty/non-string/oversized input handled gracefully
- VLA-5 ×2: NLI retry path fires on real contradiction; doesn't fire on near-paraphrase

**FAIL — RED tripwires pinning known gaps (2 tests):**
1. \`test_vla1_compound_fact_distractor_does_not_dominate\` — loud-primary-clause facts crowd out buried aside details in similarity retrieval. *VLA equivalent: small accessory buried under manual.*
2. \`test_vla3_partial_information_does_not_inflate_match\` — NLI labels specificity-mismatch as contradiction at 0.998 confidence. *VLA equivalent: occluded view → confidently wrong placement.*

Both failures are intentional tripwires — they pin known behavior so future changes to embedder / NLI / retrieval are caught. Not blockers; not fixed in this PR.

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

Implements the forgot-password REQUEST flow (slice 1 of 2) for issue #102. Slice 2 (the `/reset-password` confirm page + token consumption) will be stacked on this branch.

### What ships

- **`POST /api/auth/forgot-password`** — email input → mint token → send email. Always returns `{ ok: true }` (200) regardless of email existence.
- **`lib/password-reset.ts`** — `generatePasswordResetToken()` (UUID + 24h expiry) + `sendPasswordResetEmail()` (delegates to `sendEmail` with the `"password-reset"` template).
- **`lib/server/send-email.ts`** — additive: `"password-reset"` added to `EmailTemplate` union + `passwordResetRenderer` registered in `RENDERERS`. No existing renderers touched.
- **`lib/meta-db.ts`** — additive: `setPasswordResetToken(userId, token, expiresAt)` writing to the new dedicated `password_reset_token` / `password_reset_expires` columns.
- **`app/(auth)/forgot-password/page.tsx`** + **`layout.tsx`** — email form → generic "check your inbox" confirmation (no existence signal to the user).
- **`scripts/migrate-meta-password-reset-cols.ts`** — idempotent `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN` script. **Built, NOT run against any live DB.**

### SECURITY DECISION: separate reset-token columns

`password_reset_token` and `password_reset_expires` are **new, dedicated columns** — NOT a reuse of `verification_token` / `verification_expires`. Sharing one token column across email-verify and password-reset is a cross-purpose token-confusion risk: a verify token could be replayed at the reset endpoint (and vice versa) if they share storage. Separate columns enforce the boundary at the DB level.

### Security properties

| Property | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Anti-enumeration | Always returns `{ ok: true }` / 200 — no signal on email existence |
| Timing defence | On not-found: runs dummy `bcrypt.hash('...', 12)` so latency matches the happy path |
| Separate token columns | `password_reset_token` / `_expires` — never touches `verification_token` / `_expires` |
| Rate limits | Per-IP: 5/hr → hard 429; Per-email: 3/hr → silent 200 (anti-enum preserved) |
| Token entropy | `randomUUID()` = 128-bit CSPRNG — same source as email-verification |
| Token expiry | 24 hours — ISO string stored alongside token, checked at consume time (slice 2) |
| Email link safety | Link targets `/reset-password?token=<uuid>` — no PII in URL beyond the token |

### Migration

```sql
-- scripts/migrate-meta-password-reset-cols.ts runs:
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN password_reset_token TEXT;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN password_reset_expires TEXT;
-- Idempotent: exits cleanly if columns already exist.
```

Migration is **built and held**. Run only after explicit operator sign-off.

### Tests: 18 new tests across 2 files

**`__tests__/auth/password-reset-token.test.ts`** (7 tests)
- `generatePasswordResetToken`: UUID format, 24h expiry window, uniqueness per call
- `sendPasswordResetEmail`: delegates to `sendEmail` with correct template + data, resolves on success, silent-skip on no-api-key, throws on Resend API failure

**`__tests__/api/auth/forgot-password.test.ts`** (11 tests)
- Happy path: token stored + email sent
- **Anti-enumeration**: non-existent email returns `{ ok: true }`, no token stored, no email sent; responses for existing vs non-existent are byte-identical
- **Timing defence**: dummy bcrypt-12 hash is called on not-found path (asserted directly)
- Email normalisation (trim + lowercase)
- Input validation: 400 on missing email, invalid format, malformed JSON
- **Per-IP rate limit**: 429 hard block, no user lookup; key/params asserted
- **Per-email rate limit**: silent 200 (anti-enum preserved); no lookup/store/send
- DB error → 500

**Arch test** (`__tests__/auth/admin-write-routes-check-role.test.ts`): `auth/forgot-password/route.ts::POST` added to `NON_ADMIN_WRITE` — same classification as `auth/register`, `auth/resend-verification` (all use `publicHandler`, all are pre-session public endpoints). This file is not on the explicit allow-list; the arch test is a mechanical scanner that auto-discovers any new `app/api/**/route.ts` and fails if it is not classified. The addition is a pure one-line classification entry with no logic change.

### Allow-list pressure

One out-of-list file was touched: `__tests__/auth/admin-write-routes-check-role.test.ts`. The arch test is a filesystem scanner — any new `app/api/**/route.ts` triggers it. The change is a one-line classification entry (no logic), identical in kind to the existing `auth/resend-verification/route.ts::POST` entry. Flagged transparently.

### Slice 2 (reset-confirm)

Will be stacked on this branch: `POST /api/auth/reset-password { token, newPassword }` — token lookup against `password_reset_token` + expiry check, bcrypt hash of new password, `UPDATE users SET password_hash = ?, password_reset_token = NULL, password_reset_expires = NULL`.

### Verification status

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`: 42 errors (unchanged baseline — 0 new errors from this PR)
- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 4316 passed / 0 failed / 19 skipped
- `pnpm exec eslint [new files]`: 0 errors, 1 warning (`_args` unused — identical pre-existing pattern in `resend-verification.test.ts`)
- `pnpm build`: compiled successfully, `/forgot-password` appears as static route

**HITL (AUTH + meta-DB migration): built and HELD for sign-off; migration NOT run; do NOT promote.**

Closes part of #102. Also related: #117.

body:
## Problem

The build fails with `failed to compute cache key: "/requirements.txt": not found` because the Dockerfile uses `COPY requirements.txt .` expecting the build context to be the backend/ directory, but the build context is the repo root. The dockerfilePath was set to `/backend/Dockerfile`, which combined with a rootDirectory of `backend` would resolve to `backend/backend/Dockerfile` — a path that doesn't exist.

## Solution

Changed `dockerfilePath` in railway.json from `/backend/Dockerfile` to `Dockerfile`. With rootDirectory set to `backend`, the Dockerfile is correctly resolved at `backend/Dockerfile` relative to the repo root, and the build context becomes the `backend/` directory so `COPY requirements.txt .` finds `backend/requirements.txt` as expected.

### Changes
- **Modified** `railway.json`

body:
## Summary

Completes the last two acceptance bullets of the API gatekeeper sub-PRD
(`docs/prds/api-gatekeeper.md` §1/§4/§6/§7) for `ApiGatekeeper.execute`:

- **Retry with backoff on transient failures** per config (`max_retries`,
  `retry_after_seconds`).
- **`concurrent_max` enforced** per service.

## What changed

- **`gatekeeper/_retry.py`** (new) — retry policy.
  - *Transient vs permanent:* `TRANSIENT_ERRORS = (TimeoutError, ConnectionError)`
    are retried; everything else (e.g. `ValueError`) propagates immediately.
  - *Backoff:* **exponential**, `retry_after_seconds * 2.0 ** retry_index` — the
    base is a single named strategy constant; magnitude derives entirely from
    config's `retry_after_seconds` (no hard-coded delays).
  - `run_with_retry[T]` retries up to `max_retries`, calling `on_retry` + an
    injected `sleep_fn` between attempts.
- **`gatekeeper/_limiter.py`** — concurrency seam on the existing `_inflight`
  counter: `at_concurrency_cap` / `acquire` / `release` (release guarded against
  going negative).
- **`gatekeeper/_gatekeeper.py`** — `execute()` enqueues into the **same FIFO
  queue** when the rate window is exhausted **OR** the service is at
  `concurrent_max` (an over-cap call is queued, never exceeds the cap); `_run()`
  holds one in-flight slot across the whole retry sequence and releases it in a
  `finally` (even on error). New injectable `sleep_fn` (default `time.sleep`) so
  tests capture backoff delays with no real waiting. Each scheduled retry logs a
  `retry` event via the LOG package.
- **`gatekeeper/_events.py`** (new) — extracted the three log emitters
  (`_GatekeeperLog`) to keep `_gatekeeper.py` under the 150-line cap
  (155 → 70 code lines).

## Tests (TDD, red-first)

- `packages/core/tests/test_gatekeeper_retry.py` — retry-then-succeed, exhaust +
  re-raise, non-transient not retried, `max_retries=0`. Backoff delays asserted
  via an injected `sleep_fn` (no real sleeps); `retry` events read from JSONL.
- `packages/core/tests/test_gatekeeper_concurrency.py` — deterministic
  single-thread re-entry proves the in-flight counter is at the cap when the
  nested call is enqueued; slot released after success and after a raise.
- `test_gatekeeper_limiter.py` — added 2 tests for the new concurrency seam.

No existing tests changed (behaviour is additive).

## Gates (local)

- `uv sync` clean · `ruff check .` = All checks passed · `ruff format --check .`
  clean · `mypy` = no issues (62 files) · `pytest --cov` = **230 passed, 100%
  coverage** (>=85 required) · `check_line_limit.py` rc=0 · `secret_scan.py` rc=0.

Closes #93
